Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: A vulnerability in the handling of certain Ethernet frames in Cisco IOS XE Software for Catalyst 9000 Series Switches could allow an unauthenticated, adjacent attacker to cause an egress port to become blocked and drop all outbound traffic. This vulnerability is due to improper handling of crafted Ethernet frames. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending crafted Ethernet frames through an affected switch. Cisco has released software updates that address this vulnerability. There are no workarounds that address this vulnerability. Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: MKA session is seen as up but unable to pass traffic across the link, for example ping/lldp/CDP/lacp Conditions: Seen on a Catalyst 9500 connected to another non-Catalyst peer using the gcm-aes-xpn-256 cipher. May affect other Catalyst 9000 platforms as well. Workaround: Check for both peer's SCI values and make sure to configure lower key-server-priority for the higher SCI peer. Example -1 : SCI-1(CAT9K) : 5c5a.c74e.c5df.003d, SCI-2(NCS5500) : 0032.17bc.542c.0001 in this case , CAT9K SCI value is higher than NCS5500 So, ensure that the Catalyst 9500 is the key-server for the link by having a lower priority than its peer. The key-server priority can be configured manually or left at the default which is 0. Example: CAT9K : key-server-priority: 0 NCS5500 : key-server-priority: 16 Example -2 : SCI-1(NCS5500) : 5c5a.c74e.c5df.003d, SCI-2(CAT9K) : 0032.17bc.542c.0001 in this case , NCS5500 SCI value is higher than CAT9K So, ensure that NCS5500 is the key-server for the link by having a lower priority than its peer. The key-server priority must can be configured manually for XR systems (because the default is 16) Example: NCS5500 : key-server-priority: 0 CAT9K : key-server-priority: 16 Further Problem Description:

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: A vulnerability in the Common Open Policy Service (COPS) of Cisco IOS XE Software for Cisco cBR-8 Converged Broadband Routers could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause resource exhaustion, resulting in a denial of service (DoS) condition. This vulnerability is due to a deadlock condition in the code when processing COPS packets under certain conditions. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending COPS packets with high burst rates to an affected device. A successful exploit could allow a low-privileged attacker to cause the affected system to reload, resulting in a DoS condition, or allow a high-privileged attacker to execute arbitrary code as the root user and obtain full control of the affected system. BUG headline: SDA:SMR broken on External/Anywhere S1 Borders when default route not present.
Product - Series: Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9400 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9600 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9200 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9500 Series Switches
Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: SMR broken on External/Anywhere S1 Borders when default route not present. 1.As PETR, External/Anywhere imports 0/0 prefix to LISP DB. 2.Because there is no default route learned on the PETR, LISP DB for 0/0 is moved to the LISP away table. 3.The away table translates the 0/0 prefix to enforce SMR flag in CEF 4.Every single prefix not imported into LISP database from BGP on this border in a VRF will have SMR flag enabled due to the 0/0 away entry. Even if the destination prefix has a more specific route, the away 0/0 enforced SMR flag to it, which results in traffic loss as S1 does not support SMR for prefixes covered in away table. SMR is broken in the sense that non-LISP related traffic will be impacted by SMR operation; normal LISP related traffic (Border to Edge, Edge to Border) will work fine; but on the scenario of using S1 Borders as a Transit (ex: Interconnecting DCs using a LISP-enabled VRF), non-LISP traffic will be unable to be forwarded when SMR is covering such prefixes. In other words, when a prefix is part of the LISP remoteEID (mapcache) is covered by SMR, the platform treat it as glean (SMR can trigger LISP mobility), but when non-LISP prefixes are also covered by SMR, the platform treat is as special adjacency, which cannot be forwarded. Conditions: This issue was observed on 9500-X(S1) borders running IOS-XE 17.12.2 and 17.12.4. Workaround: To workaround this issue advertise the default route from the fusion router to the External/Anywhere border. Further Problem Description: NA

It manifests after a route flap event, such as an upstream BGP neighbor temporarily ceasing and then re-advertising the default route. BCPC9600X#show platform software fed active ip route vrf VRF_NAME 0.0.0.0/0 detail IPV4ROUTE_ID:id:0xxxxxxxxx nobj:(IPNEXTHOP_ID,0x5cd) 0.0.0.0/0 tblid:2 DA:0 State:(0) success NPD: device:0 lspa_rec:0 api_type:route(3) State:(0) success SDK: is_host:0 l3_dest:0xXXXXXXXXXXXX l3_dest:la_next_hop_base(oid=535) vrf(gid/oid):2/0x267 SDK Object Details: NPD: SDK oid 0x217, devid:0, asic:0 Next Hop Object: sdk nexthop oid:0x217,dev:0, gid:0x1 macaddr:0000.0000.0000, nh_type:other(5) ------------*** Next Hop Type: Other sdk outgoing port none Workaround: To resolve this, the faulty route can be re-programmed by introducing a more preferred route to override the existing one (e.g., a BGP route), and then removing it. This can be achieved by adding and immediately removing a null0 route within the affected VRF: ip route vrf VRF_NAME 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 null0 no ip route vrf VRF_NAME 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 null0 This action forces the system to re-evaluate and correctly program the next-hop type for the impacted route. BUG headline: Catalyst 9000 Series: IPv6 Traffic May Drop With FMFP Error Messages After Interface State Change
Product - Series: Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9400 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9600 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 3850 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9200 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9500 Series Switches
Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: A customer may observe IPv6 packet loss or traffic drops. Coinciding with the traffic loss, the device console or system logs will display error messages indicating that an object download to the Data Path (DP) has failed. The following sanitized syslog message illustrates the error observed when this issue occurs: %FMFP-3-OBJ_DWNLD_TO_DP_FAILED: Switch x F0/0: fman_fp_image: PREFIX xxxx:xxxx:xxxx:xxxx::x/128 (Table id xxxxxxxx) download to DP failed Conditions: This issue is observed in Software Defined Access (SDA) environments configured with IPv6 (dual-stack). The problem is triggered when an IPv6 host prefix transitions from being directly attached (resolved via an SVI) to pointing to a NULL0 interface. Common triggers for this state transition include: - Flapping (shut/no shut) a Border node interface connected to an external router or Fusion device. - Executing the 'clear device-tracking database' command while traffic is running. Workaround: There are no operational workarounds to prevent this issue once the specific state transition occurs. Reloading the device may be required to recover the forwarding state. Further Problem Description: This defect involves a failure in the Forwarding Manager (FMAN) to correctly update the Data Path (DP) when an IPv6 prefix adjacency changes state. This results in the prefix update failure logged in the symptoms.

BUG headline: IKEv2: ECMP is not working on IPsec tunnel on Catalyst 9300X
Product - Series: Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9400 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9600 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9200 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9500 Series Switches
Release Note Enclosure: Load sharing across multiple IPsec tunnels is critical for optimized traffic distribution in networks. The inability to achieve ECMP over IPsec tunnels limits network performance and does not align with expected behavior. Symptom: The problem is with flow-based load-balancing when ECMP is used. Packets are always forwarded out via first interface seen in cef output. sh ip cef vrf TEST 192.0.2.0 detail 192.0.2.0/24 , epoch 1, flags [rib only nolabel, rib defined all labels, default route], per-destination sharing recursive via 198.51.100.178 recursive via 198.51.100.176/30 attached to Tunnel1 recursive via 198.51.100.182 recursive via 198.51.100.180/30 attached to Tunnel2 Conditions: - Catalyst 9300X device. - IPsec tunnels configured with ECMP for load-balancing - Route from second tunnel with same cost installed later due to any reason, CEF updates this as second path which does not get reflected in switch datapath Workaround: "Clear ip route" when both tunnels are up will make it work since CEF will install both routes together which will be updated correctly in datapath too. Further Problem Description: The problem is only when IPSEC tunnels are used, for regular GREs load-balancing works as expected.

BUG headline: Cisco IOS XE Software for Catalyst Switches MPLS Denial of Service Vulnerability
Product - Series: Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9400 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9600 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9200 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9500 Series Switches
Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: A vulnerability in the egress MPLS packet processing function of Cisco IOS XE Software for Cisco Catalyst 3650, Catalyst 3850, and Catalyst 9000 Family Switches could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause an affected device to reload unexpectedly, resulting in a denial of service (DoS) condition. This vulnerability is due to insufficient input validation of IPv4 traffic. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a malformed packet out of an affected MPLS-enabled interface. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to cause the device to reload, resulting in a DoS condition. Cisco has released software updates that address this vulnerability. There are no workarounds that address this vulnerability. This advisory is available at the following link: https://tools.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-iosxe-mpls-dos-Ab4OUL3 The Cisco Product Security Incident Response Team (PSIRT) validates only the affected and fixed release information that is documented in this advisory. Further Problem Description: Please refer to the Security Advisory. *PSIRT Evaluation:* The Cisco PSIRT has assigned this bug the following CVSS version 3 score. The Base CVSS score as of the time of evaluation is 8.6: https://tools.cisco.com/security/center/cvssCalculator.x?version=3.0&vector=CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:N/I:N/A:H CVE ID CVE-2022-20870 has been assigned to document this issue. BUG headline: C9400 Loses Line Card Configuration after Upgrade
Product - Series: Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9400 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9600 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9200 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9500 Series Switches
Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: Cat9400 switch might experience physical interface configuration loss after an IOS-XE upgrade from the SmartLicensing-enabled release [17.03.01 and earlier] to SmartLicensing using Policy-enabled release [17.03.02 and later] if the configuration is not saved manually. All other configuration [global configuration, as well as logical interface configuration [Portchannel interfaces/Vlan SVI interfaces/Loopback interfaces/...], is retained. This problem is seen only when the switch was registered to CSSM/OnPrem Satellite prior to the upgrade, and the communication was successful. This issue can be identified by comparing the show running-config output where the physical interface configuration will be present to the show startup-config output where the physical interface configuration will be missing after the IOS-XE upgrade. If the switch ends up in this state, there is no immediate impact as the needed configuration is present in the running-config however should the switch reload due to a power outage or any other cause, the startup-config, which at this point is missing the physical interface configuration will be read and applied upon subsequent boot which will result in all the physical interfaces losing their original configuration. Conditions: Cat9400 switch IOS-XE upgrade from the SmartLicensing-enabled release [17.03.01 and earlier] to SmartLicensing using Policy-enabled release [17.03.02 and later] PKI certificates are regenerated upon the initial boot configuration is saved [due to PKI certificates being regenerated] before linecards come online and become operational Workaround: after the IOS-XE upgrade, compare the content of the show running-config output and the show startup-config output if the physical interface configuration is still present in the running-config but is already missing in the startup-config, then simply save the configuration by issuing the copy running-config startup-config command [in other words, this is the state just after the upgrade and before the subsequent reload] this action can also be automated via the following EEM script event manager applet STARTUP_CONFIG_FIXER authorization bypass event syslog pattern "Running configuration saved to NVRAM" maxrun 300 action 1 cli command "enable" action 2 wait 180 action 3 cli command "write memory" action 4 syslog msg "startup-config has been saved to prevent interface configuration loss" if the physical interface configuration is missing in both the running-config and the startup-config, then restore the configuration from backup [in other words, this is the state after the upgrade and after the subsequent reload] Further Problem Description: This is a timing issue where SmartLicensing Agent will regenerate PKI certificates upon the initial boot, and as part of this operation, will also initiate saving the running-config into startup-config. If this action is started after the linecards have booted up and initialized, no issue will be seen. If this action is started before the linecards have booted up and initialized, the running-config at that time will not contain the physical interface configuration [which will only appear once the linecards come online] and this "partial" running-config will be written into the startup-config stored in the NVRAM. This problem will be exposed the next time the switch boots up and this startup-config is read and applied. This being a timing issue, it does not affect all IOS-XE upgrade cycles and if the SmartLicensing Agent/PKI-initiated config saved is delayed by any event upon the initial boot, this problem will not occur.

BUG headline: ENH: Cat9k Switching -  Allow LACP Standalone / Independent on Layer 3 Etherchannel
Product - Series: Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9400 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9600 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9200 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9500 Series Switches
Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: Unable to configure Standalone / Independent mode for LACP with Layer 3 etherchannel / port-channel on Catalyst 9000 Series Switches Conditions: Configure a port channel Configure "no switchport" Attempt to configure "no port-channel standalone-disable" System returns: Switch(config-if)#no port-channel standalone-disable This feature is only supported on L2 port-channels <<<< Workaround: Use layer 2 port channel if standalone is a requirement Further Problem Description: The feature is desirable when there is a need to keep line protocol up when one side of the links being bundled is not configured - LACP will identify that there is no neighbor, and by default, suspend the ports (thus bringing line protocol down) The configuration "no port-channel standalone-disable" under the port-channel interface in the command line will override the default behavior and allow the ports to go into independent (otherwise known as standalone) mode. Then no further stack issues are seen. Another side affect to this is seen if the new switch has a different license than the stack license. Conditions: - RELAY-REPLY message ingresses the device through an MPLS enabled interface and "no ipv6 dhcp-relay trust-all" is configured, only specific interfaces are marked as relay trusted. - Device must be running 16.12.4 or 17.3.1 Workaround: - Configure "ipv6 dhcp-relay trust-all" (this is a default configuration) - Disable MPLS on the ingressing interface for RELAY-REPLY messages Further Problem Description: DHCPv6 RELAY-REPLY messages are dropped when punted if ingressing the device through an MPLS enabled interface, and "no ipv6 dhcp-relay trust-all" is configured, due to the fact that when the messages are punted, as they arrive from an MPLS enabled interface, internally the arriving interface is changed to Null0, since this interface is not marked as a relay trust interface the messages are dropped from the dhcp-relay trust check due to arriving on an untrusted interface.

BUG headline: Issue Detected as Resolved - Certificate with Common Name: "ISRG Root X1" will expire soon
Product - Series: Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9400 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9600 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9200 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9500 Series Switches
Release Note Enclosure: The digital certificate that is used by Cisco Catalyst 9200 and 9300 Switches to register with Cisco Umbrella DNS expired on September 30, 2024. Cisco Catalyst 9200 and 9300 Switches with the expired certificate will fail to register with the Cisco Umbrella DNS service. Symptom: Affected Cisco Catalyst 9200 and 9300 Switches with expired Cisco Umbrella root certificate authority (CA) certificates cannot establish secure connections with Cisco Umbrella DNS for device registration. Because affected devices are not registered with the Cisco Umbrella DNS service, user DNS requests are not redirected to the Cisco Umbrella domain server by the affected switches for DNS security policy enforcement. DNS requests from the users of affected switches will not be dropped and will be serviced by the DNS domain server that is configured on the devices. Conditions: Umbrella Registration may not go through if disconnected and reconnection is attempted.The Certificate ISRG is expiring and customer need to upgrade to newer version of said certificate to make umbrella work seamlessly. Workaround: Affected devices must have the affected certificate replaced with a new Cisco Umbrella root certificate that is valid until the year 2035. Customers who do not currently use Cisco Umbrella DNS but who expect to deploy it in the future can replace the affected certificate by upgrading Cisco Catalyst 9200 and 9300 Switches to a Cisco IOS XE Software release that contains the new certificate. The new certificate is installed automatically during the upgrade. Further Problem Description:

BUG headline: Global vrf default route entry & VRF specific default route entry should not have the same priority
Product - Series: Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9400 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9600 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9200 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9500 Series Switches
Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: A cat9500H or Cat9600 switch may see unexpected packet loss for traffic using a combination of a specific route on a specific port (or range of ports) on the switch. The loss may be total, with traffic being forwarded out the wrong interface, or could be partial loss as a result of CPU forwarding. Hosts located on a different source interface/module (which is mapped to a different internal forwarding engine) using the same VRF and route are unlikely to see the issue and may be unaffected. Instead the loss will appear as if its specific to one port, or a group of ports. Adding a new route for the traffic in question to take will correct the issue, but loss will return if this route is removed. Conditions: This is an extremely rare corner-case scenario that requires multiple different conditions to all be present in order to be hit: - Only Cat9500H and Cat9600 switches are vulnerable to this. - Switches must be running 17.1.1 or later. 16.x.x trains are not impacted. - Switch must have at least 12 VRFs to have a small chance of seeing this (the more VRFs defined, the higher the chances of this issue, but even with high scale the chances are still very low overall) - Switch must have large number of routes across all VRFs (estimated 50,000 or more - Higher numbers of routes are more likely to see this, but even with higher numbers this is still very rare) Workaround: Adding a more specific route to the destination has a high chance of correcting the behavior, but the behavior will return if this route is removed. Reloading the switch may also correct the behavior, however there is a unique sequence of events that must take place when programming the hardware which could cause the issue to reappear. Further Problem Description: PSIRT Evaluation: The Cisco PSIRT has evaluated this issue and determined it does not meet the criteria for PSIRT ownership or involvement. This issue will be addressed via normal resolution channels. If you believe that there is new information that would cause a change in the severity of this issue, please contact psirt@cisco.com for another evaluation. Additional information on Cisco's security vulnerability policy can be found at the following URL: http://www.cisco.com/en/US/products/products_security_vulnerability_policy.html

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: SIP Notify packet fragmented from a phone comes into the C9300. With a class-map to remark incoming traffic that is using port 5060 to CS3. The packet is being marked EF instead. The first class-map within the policy is to mark EF, the 2nd class-map is to mark it CS3. Nothing in the class-map for the EF marking should match the packet. BUG headline: C9600 - C9600-LC-48TX IPG CLI Knob Implementation
Product - Series: Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9400 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9600 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9200 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9500 Series Switches
Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: CSCvz67689 resolves the issues that may be encountered as part of CSCvw18201, where silent loss may be encountered when devices connect to the C9600-LC-48TX. Devices (issue has been encountered with other Cisco switches such as the Catalyst 2960S or 9200L switch as well as third-party equipment, such as DD630 server, Palo Alto Firewall, HP DL380 Gen 10 server) there may be other devices that have not been listed earlier, may encounter silent loss when connected to the C9600-LC-48TX linecard. This linecard is a 48 port multigigabit (mGIG/mgig) ethernet copper linecard which will allow 10GE, 5GE, 2.5GE, 1GE, 100Mbps, 10Mbps. The loss will not come in the form of an output drop, but may result in input errors (FCS Frames, Symbol Errors, CRCs) on both sides of the link (remote and local C9600) may have a chance of seeing input errors. Conditions: The issue has only been observed on the ports of the C9600-LC-48TX, when the speed/bandwidth of the link is either hardcoded or negotiated to 1000 Mb/s. The issue is not seen at lower or higher speeds/bandwidth than 1000 Mb/s. Workaround: If the remote-end supports a higher or lower speed/bandwidth than 1000 Mb/s, utilize a higher or lower speed link (10 Gb/s or 100 Mb/s) as the issue is not seen when using any other speed/bandwidth than 1000 Mb/s. If the remote device is unable to negotiate or support a different speed, move the affected link/device to a different linecard if possible. Further Problem Description: Below configurations to SGMII (1G) mode between Host and PHY conf t int te1/0/1 speed 1000 high-ipg OR speed 100 high-ipg OR speed 10 high-ipg OR speed auto 1000 high-ipg OR speed auto 100 high-ipg OR speed auto 10 high-ipg

BUG headline: SVL Link Instability May Result in IOMD Exhaustion
Product - Series: Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9400 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9600 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9200 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9500 Series Switches
Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: Catalyst 9000-series Stackwise Virtual capable platforms (C9400, C9500, C9500H, C9600) may encounter scenarios were there is an Input Output Module Daemon (IOMD) exhaustion. This daemon is responsible for anything interface related, such as reflecting whether or not an interface is up or not. For example, the active switch will report the interface on the standby switch as down, when in reality the interface on the standby switch is up, but they are unable to synchronize and agree on the interface state. You can validate which is true by checking interface LEDs or interface status on the remote device connecting to the Stackwise Virtual setup. This issue can result from Stackwise Virtual Link (SVL) instability in the form of numerous link flaps on the SVL. These link flaps themselves may be the result of L1 issues, such as input errors, CRCs, etc. If you believe you have encountered this defect please engage Cisco TAC for further troubleshooting assistance. Conditions: Catalyst 9000-series Stackwise Virtual capable platforms (C9400, C9500, C9500H, C9600) with numerous link flaps on the critical SVL link(s). Example output demonstrates the SVL link flapping: %NIF_MGR-6-PORT_CONN_DISCONNECTED: Chassis 1 R0/0: nif_mgr: TwentyFiveGigabitEthernet Port 2 on front side stack link 0 connection has DISCONNECTED: CONN_ERR_PORT_LINK_DOWN_EVENT %NIF_MGR-6-PORT_LINK_UP: Chassis 1 R0/0: nif_mgr: TwentyFiveGigabitEthernet Port 2 on front side stack link 0 is UP. %NIF_MGR-6-PORT_CONN_PENDING: Chassis 1 R0/0: nif_mgr: TwentyFiveGigabitEthernet Port 2 on front side stack link 0 connection is PENDING. %NIF_MGR-6-PORT_LINK_DOWN: Chassis 2 R0/0: nif_mgr: TwentyFiveGigabitEthernet Port 2 on front side stack link 0 is DOWN. %NIF_MGR-6-PORT_CONN_DISCONNECTED: Chassis 2 R0/0: nif_mgr: TwentyFiveGigabitEthernet Port 2 on front side stack link 0 connection has DISCONNECTED: CONN_ERR_PORT_LINK_DOWN_EVENT %NIF_MGR-6-PORT_LINK_UP: Chassis 2 R0/0: nif_mgr: TwentyFiveGigabitEthernet Port 2 on front side stack link 0 is UP. %NIF_MGR-6-PORT_CONN_PENDING: Chassis 2 R0/0: nif_mgr: TwentyFiveGigabitEthernet Port 2 on front side stack link 0 connection is PENDING. %NIF_MGR-6-PORT_LINK_DOWN: Chassis 2 R0/0: nif_mgr: TwentyFiveGigabitEthernet Port 2 on front side stack link 0 is DOWN. %NIF_MGR-6-PORT_CONN_DISCONNECTED: Chassis 2 R0/0: nif_mgr: TwentyFiveGigabitEthernet Port 2 on front side stack link 0 connection has DISCONNECTED: CONN_ERR_PORT_LINK_DOWN_EVENT Workaround: Reload or failover the SVL setup. BUG headline: 9500X/9600X - MAC addresses do not age out on portchannel
Product - Series: Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9400 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9600 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9200 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9500 Series Switches
Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: /// Most complete signature of THIS bug: in "show platform software fed (switch) active matm macTable vlan [vlan #]", MAC address "e_time" value, exceeds the "a_time" value on a portchannel interface. This bug does not apply to other kinds of interfaces. A_time is the aging timer. E_time is elapsed time. If E is greater than A, that means the switch failed to age out the MAC. /// Other surrounding symptoms + Unexpectedly high values of MACs learned in "show mac address-table count summary" + high / increasing counts of "L2 matm add error" in command "show platform software fed (switch) active learning stats" + Unexpected unknown unicast flooding of traffic due to MAC table being full, thus inability to learn new MACs (which WILL lead to flooding of traffic to MACs that could not be learned + Significantly less ARP adjacent hosts than MACs learned. While this could be natural, this broadly suggests that MACs are being kept while ARP is aging out (and hosts no longer respond). With default timers (4hr ARP, 300s MAC) - this should be inverse (ARPs retained while MACs are gone). + After clear mac address-table dynamic command, MAC table scale stabilizes far below previously count Conditions: MUST be 9500X-28C8D, 9500X-60L4D, or 9600X-SUP-2 MUST be MAC learning on a port channel interface Workaround: *clear mac address-table dynamic* will clear out stale MACs so that the system can learn new ones, until the aging failures cause the table to become full again. Further Problem Description: PSIRT Evaluation: The Cisco PSIRT has evaluated this issue and determined it does not meet the criteria for PSIRT ownership or involvement. This issue will be addressed via normal resolution channels. If you believe that there is new information that would cause a change in the severity of this issue, please contact psirt@cisco.com for another evaluation. Additional information on Cisco's security vulnerability policy can be found at the following URL: http://www.cisco.com/en/US/products/products_security_vulnerability_policy.html

BUG headline: Cat9000 - DHCP OFFER is incorrectly modified by Snooping Proxy-Bridge feature
Product - Series: Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9400 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9600 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9200 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9500 Series Switches
Release Note Enclosure: Proxy-bridge Snooping feature is triggering when Option 82 with remote-id hostname is used. Symptom: Endpoints unable to get IP address when using Option 82 with remote-id hostname configured on the layer 2 Cat9k switch. The DHCP Offer packet is processed by the switch with incorrect MAC address in the destination portion of the ethernet header. Conditions: DHCP transaction has Unicast bootp flag. Option 82 used with remote-id hostname configuration First encountered in 17.9.5. Workaround: 1. Remove the remote-id hostname option from configuration. "no ip dhcp snooping information option format remote-id hostname" >> This will change the sub-option 2 - Remote Agent ID on the Option 82 info. >> Switch will still send the sub-option 1 - Agent Circuit ID unchanged. 2. Change the bootp flag of endpoints to Broadcast flag 3. Downgrade to 17.9.4 version where issue is not present. Further Problem Description: Proxy-bridge Snooping was first introduced in 17.6.x On 17.9.5, the Proxy bridge is changing/rewriting the destination MAC of the OFFER packet upon injection to the data plane. This issue causes the endpoints to not obtain IP address given that the OFFER packet is sent with incorrect destination MAC. The Cat9k is taking the Option 82 Sub-option 2 Remote Agent ID HEX values (the hostname of switch in HEX) and taking a portion of the stream to add it as a destination MAC to the packet which is incorrect. Sub-option 1 - Agent Circuit ID is not affected and unchanged.

BUG headline: C9500X/C9600X: SVL - Packets Larger Than 9194 Bytes Dropped in SVL When System MTU is Set to 9216
Product - Series: Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9400 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9600 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9200 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9500 Series Switches
Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: - Any packet that passes through the SVL that is larger than 9194 B is dropped as an oversize frame. - Input Giant counter increases in "show interface" for the respective SVL. Conditions: - C9500X and C9600X with System MTU of 9216 Bytes. - Issue is seen only on SVL interfaces. Workaround: No workaround. Further Problem Description: - When system MTU is 9216, the MTU in the physical interfaces for the SVLs is set to a higher number because SVLs append a header. The actual value being used for this is 9284 Bytes. - However, if a packet needs to pass through the SVL we have: IP packet total length (9216 B) + Ethernet header (14 B) + VLAN header (4 B) + SVL VLAN header (4 B) + SVL header (64 B) + FCS (4 B) = 9306 B - Thus, the maximum possible frame size of 9306 bytes exceeds the actual SVL MTU of 9284 bytes by 22 bytes. This results in a condition where only packets of up to 9194 bytes (9216 - 22 = 9194) will not be dropped as Giants in the SVL. - In fixed releases, MTU is set to 9306 B. This can be validated using CLI "sh platform software fed switch acive/standby ifm if-id | i MTU".

BUG headline: Accounting Stop message is not sent for one of the access sessions after Reload.
Product - Series: Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9400 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9600 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9200 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9500 Series Switches
Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: Accounting Stop message is not sent for one of the access sessions after Reload. Conditions: SANET tries to initiate Accounting STOP message for a particular client when it receives the AAA Available event is received although the STOP message was already sent. Workaround: None Further Problem Description: In the setup where this issue occurred, when AAA server is not reachable clients are assigned to an SGT and authorized. SANET determines that the AAA server is reachable again when an attempt to reach the server is successful and in this case initiates an Accounting STOP record for the older session authorized by the SGT for one of the clients. As part of this the acct_stat_start_pending timer is started to wait for all the data to be sent as part of the STOP record. After sometime AAA notifies SANET that the AAA server is reachable via the AAA Available event. When this event is received, SANET once again tries to reauthenticate all client sessions. As a result Accounting STOP is triggered again for the client session where this timer is already running. This is treated as an error scenario and the client session will be terminated resulting in Accounting STOP not being sent.

BUG headline: 9200L Stack Running IOS-XE 17.14 with Large # of SANET-Enabled Ports May Crash During Config Changes
Product - Series: Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9400 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9600 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9200 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9500 Series Switches
Release Note Enclosure:
Symptom: A 9200L switch stack running IOS-XE 17.14 or later with a large number of members may see a crash in the Sessmgrd process when adding/removing SANET configurations (eg: dot1x) at the interface level if there are already a large number of ports using SANET. One way to determine a stack at risk is if the combined SANET configuration is sufficient to cause this database to be greater than 30MB: 
SWITCH#show platform software mount switch active R0 dir /tmp/rp/tdldb/0 | inc File\ Size|SM_CONFIG_DB_
File Name                File Size(Bytes)
SM_CONFIG_DB             33554432
Conditions:
  • 9200L in a large-scale setup (eg: 8 switches).
  • Nearly every single port has heavy SANET config (eg: 8 switch x 48 ports = ~400 ports).
  • 17.14.x or newer is used. This has been confirmed to *not* impact earlier versions due to the fact that SM_CONFIG_DB used to have a larger memory ceiling in those versions.
Workaround: Avoid using heavy per-interface SANET configurations (ie: IBNS 1.0 syntax). Consider migrating to IBNS 2.0 wherein SANET config is defined in a class-map / service-policy, which the interface configurations then reference. This is more efficient in terms of numbers of lines of unique configuration and more memory efficient for SM_CONFIG_DB -- and so, it will avoid the issue. https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/td/docs/switches/lan/catalyst9200/software/release/17-14/configuration_guide/sec/b_1714_sec_9200_cg/configuring_identity_control_policies.html Please read the document carefully before performing a migration via: 
SWITCH# authentication convert-to new-style

BUG headline: [NEAT] CISP installs a static MAC address entry pointing to a wrong interface
Product - Series: Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9400 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9600 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9200 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9500 Series Switches
Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: In a star topology there is the distribution switch [Authenticator] and multiple access switches [Supplicants] with no redundant connections // physical loop. It is possible to end up in a situation where the distribution switch [Authenticator] ends up installing a static MAC address entry pointing to a wrong interface. To illustrate this, let's imagine we have Client A behind Access switch A and Client B behind Access switch B. The distribution switch ends up installing a static MAC address entry of Client A pointing to the interface where Access switch B resides. Since addresses behind access switches are signaled via CISP, these are installed as static entries that do not age out. As a result, connectivity to Client A is disrupted since the distribution switch forwards traffic destined to Client A's MAC address to Access switch B, which has no path to Client A. Conditions: This NEAT setup has been working fine for years when only C3560 compact switches were installed. The problem surfaced once C9k compact switches was introduced into the network. Workaround: - shut/no shut the trunk link between the Authenticator and the affected Supplicant switch - clear mac address address table for the affected interface on the Authenticator switch - shut/no shut the interface towards the affected endpoint on the Supplicant switch Further Problem Description: This problem is seen upon introduction of C9k compact switches to the network. Each compact switch [access switch // Supplicant] only owns 10 endpoints or less.

BUG headline: Non-Zero Header Padding in SYN/ACK packet sent from Switch to Telnet/SSH session
Product - Series: Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst IE9300 Rugged Series,Cisco Catalyst 9400 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 8000V Edge Software,Cisco Catalyst 9600 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9200 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9500H Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9500 Series Switches
Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: Non-Zero Header Padding in SYN/ACK packet sent from Switch to Telnet/SSH session. If a Firewall is located in between the Client of the SSH session and the Switch, then the TCP/SYN sent by the Switch is dropped on the firewall with reasons such as "invalid TCP options". Conditions: This defect is observed in software version 17.9.5, when the command "ip ssh bulk-mode" is configured. In version 17.12.3, the behavior is seen regardless if the command "ip ssh bulk-mode" is enabled or disabled. Workaround: #1) On version 17.10.1 and above, configure the TCP Window Size on the Switch to a value lower than 64KB (thus avoiding the usage of the window scale TCP option). For example, set the TCP Window Size back to the default value of "ip tcp window-size 4128". Additionally, configure 'no ip ssh bulk-mode'. #2) Revert to IOS-XE version 17.9.5. Further Problem Description: Issue is seen with Telnet/SSH but not with HTTP/HTTPS WEB GUI connections. Telnet and SSH TCP/SYN packets include the End of Option List (EOL) and then it includes the Non-Zero Header Padding. The HTTP/ HTTPS WEB GUI TCP/SYN packets do not include an End of Option List (EOL). On versions 17.10.1 and later, the command "ip ssh bulk-mode" is configured by default.

BUG headline: C9300X use SFP-10G-T-X Copper transceiver has random packet loss with 1G speed after OIR
Product - Series: Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9400 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9600 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9200 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9500H Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9500 Series Switches
Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: It is observed in the field that C9300X having SFP-10G-T-X Copper transceiver with Serial Number MTC24xxxx or MTC25xxxx or MTC26xxxx connection to a peer end device (like a windows PC) exhibits random packet loss. As of now, no special error counters are found. Conditions: C9300X with SFP-10G-T-X (having Serial Numbers MTC24xxxx or MTC25xxxx or MTC26xxxx), C9300X running 17.6.x and 17.7.x. The problem occurs after going through an OIR event (starting at system boot). This issue is not applicable for SFP-10G-T-X operating in 10G speed Workaround: 1/ Pick an unused port (that has not been used since last bootup of switch) for insertion of SFP-10G-T-X intended to operate in 1G speed. 2/ After removal of SFP-10G-T-X operating in 1G speed, insert any other 10G transceiver/PID (Eg: SFP-10G-SR). After detection of the transceiver is successful remove it (no need to establish the link UP with a peer). Finally, insert the SFP-10G-T-X. 3/ Reload the switch to clear the issue. Further Problem Description: SFP-10G-T-X can operate at different speeds (1G or 10G) depending upon interface speed configuration or auto-negotiation with the peer. Once SFP-10G-T-X is removed from the port, switch software does clean-up activity to reset the port to default setting. When SFP-10G-T-X is operating in 1G speed, certain internal settings (speed/mode) are not getting cleaned-up during the transceiver removal and these settings remain as a stale data. Now if SFP-10G-T-X transceiver is re-inserted on the same port, due to the existing stale data, the initialization of the transceiver is not successful and leads to random packet drops.

BUG headline: Switchport Security Command triggering Bulk Sync Failure
Product - Series: Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9400 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9600 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9200 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9500H Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9500 Series Switches
Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: While configuring switchport security , if you configure -switchport port-security maximum 2- (in this specific case, we tested it with this line): Example: interface GigabitEthernet1/0/40 description not used switchport access vlan 999 switchport mode access switchport port-security maximum 2 <<<<<<<<<<<<< switchport port-security maximum 1 vlan access switchport port-security violation shutdown vlan switchport port-security mac-address sticky switchport port-security Once you save the configuration on the stack( normal write, or copy run start) , if you erase the command "switchport port-security maximum 2", and save again(we need to double save the config at this point), and reload the switch, the switch will boot up back, but will never finish the HA sync in progress state, because of this, the switch will not sync and trigger a reload on the standby switch, seeing the next message: Message from sysmgr: Reason Code:[4] Reset Reason:Reset/Reload requested by [stack-manager]. [Bulk Sync Failure]. To recover the STACK, you need to re-configure the "switchport port-security maximum 2", and the stack will boot correctly as we will be able to re-sync Conditions: Switchport security configured on the ports switchport mode access switchport port-security maximum 2 switchport port-security maximum 1 vlan access switchport port-security violation shutdown vlan switchport port-security mac-address sticky switchport port-security If you erase a switchport line, in this case, "switchport port-security maximum 2", and reload the standby, this will not complete the booting again because will not sync again. Workaround: Configure the "no policy config-sync bulk prc reload ". Switch(config)#redundancy Switch(config-red)#no policy config-sync bulk prc reload ++ Once the switches are up ( active and standby) we can re-configure the "switchport port-security maximum 2", line to recover the stack and avoid again the Bulk Sync Failure, otherwise will enter on a boot loop and the standby switch will reach the ROMMON (Switch:) state and we will need to manually boot it. we do not need to break the stack to recover the switch, we need to recover the stack from the active switch. Further Problem Description: !N/A!

BUG headline: SDA : 9500x / 9600x - ISIS Packets not bridged between switches

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: ISIS nodes connected between a 9600X-SUP-2 or 9500X using it as L2 transport will not form an adjacency; ISIS hellos are dropped by the switch. This prevents Lan Automation (DNA Center) to onboard multiple switches at the same time using a C9600X as seed device. ISIS adjacencies between agent and seed will work, while agent-to-agent adjacency in VLAN 1 will not. In case an agent becomes the ISIS DIS, SPF calculation in ISIS can lead to not installing routes on the RIB for the affected devices in VLAN1. Conditions: ISIS hellos between devices are forced to pass across the 9500x / 9600x as an L2 transport and then dropped, causing agent-to-agent adjacencies to fail. Release Note Enclosure: Memory leak observed due to buffers not getting freed by the Spanning Tree process on affected software versions. The issue leads to continuous memory consumption growth under the Spanning Tree and eventually results in low memory conditions, allocation failures and crash Symptom: Gradual increase in memory usage by the "Spanning Tree" process. Observed outputs: show processes memory sorted Processor Pool Total: 1363180300 Used: 1226956864 Free: 136223436 reserve P Pool Total: 102404 Used: 88 Free: 102316 lsmpi_io Pool Total: 6295128 Used: 6294296 Free: 832 PID TTY Allocated Freed Holding Getbufs Retbufs Process 241 0 679224688 448 678851240 141382596 0 Spanning Tree. << max usage show buffers usage Statistics for the Middle pool Caller pc : :xxx count: 242362 << max caller PC Resource User: Spanning T count: 242362 Error logs: %SYS-2-MALLOCFAIL: Memory allocation of 804 bytes failed from xxx , alignment 8 Pool: Processor Free: 146620 Cause: Memory fragmentation Alternate Pool: None Free: 0 Cause: No Alternate pool -Process= "Spanning Tree", ipl= 0, pid= 241 %SYS-4-FREEMEMLOW: Top Allocator Name: *Packet Header*, PC: Workaround: Reload the device to temporarily recover leaked memory. BUG headline: Catalyst 9300 - FED/MATM State Desynchronization and MAC Learning Lockout after clear mac address-table dynamic
Product - Series: Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9400 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9600 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 3850 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9200 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9500 Series Switches
Release Note Enclosure: A critical race condition between the control plane (IOSd) and the UADP ASIC driver (FED) during a bulk clear operation causes a deep software state desynchronization, permanently locking hardware counters and halting all new MAC learning until a reload is performed. Symptom: The control plane reports an empty or low dynamic MAC count (show mac address-table count), while the hardware driver remains permanently stuck at the maximum platform limit (Total non-cpu mac entries: 32768). The switch completely stops learning new MAC addresses after a dynamic table clear operation. Conditions: Catalyst 9300 Series Switches running Cisco IOS-XE. Triggered by executing the clear mac address-table dynamic command during periods of high dynamic MAC learning, traffic processing, or active scale events. Workaround: Perform a physical reload (reload) of the switch to reset the FED driver state and clear the stuck hardware counters. Further Problem Description: Under heavy dynamic MAC learning or high traffic concurrency, issuing a bulk clear mac address-table dynamic command can trigger a race condition between the IOSd control plane and the FED ASIC driver. This desynchronizes the internal states: although the software layer clears its active tables (showing 0 or minimal entries), the FED driver's resource allocation counter gets pinned at the maximum hardware limit (32768). The switch erroneously treats the memory as fully exhausted, creating a permanent MAC learning lockout that cannot be cleared via software commands and necessitates a full device reboot.

BUG headline: C9600X-SUP-2/C9500X Fails to Delete ECMP Next-Hop Object
Product - Series: Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 3650 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9400 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9600 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 3850 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9200 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9500H Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9500 Series Switches
Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: C9600X-SUP-2 in SD-Access operating as a collocated (control-plane + border on one box) border running IOS-XE 17.10.1 may encounter connectivity issues which potentially boil back towards pending objects in the Asynchronous Object Manager (AOM), which is in charge of helping programming various features into hardware. In this specific scenario, troubleshooting identified an IP packet (ICMP Reply) coming back from a device outside the SD fabric, egressing the Fusion Router, ingressing the Border, packet does not leave the Border. The issue is that in an SDA environment, prefixes can point to an ECMP of LISP paths. If one of the paths is deleted, prior to deletion of the ECMP object, all other prefixes should be programmed to point to another ECMP object, or an adjacency if single path present. This is done so that there is no traffic loss during the transition. If this is not done, internal programming will fail to delete the object, which results in the issue. Conditions: Issue was originally seen on a C9600X-SUP-2 in SD-Access operating as a collocated (control-plane + border on one box) border running IOS-XE 17.10.1. Issue may also occur on a C9500X that is leveraged in SDA, not specific to the C9600X Workaround: Reload the switch. As this problem happens with ECMP paths in LISP; identify the redundant LISP RLOCs, create a null0 /32 route to the RLOC and then remove it, this can re-program the impacted ECMP object. Further Problem Description:

BUG headline: C9500X / C9600X Routing Traffic to Incorrect Next-Hop MAC Address
Product - Series: Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 3650 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9400 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9600 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 3850 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9200 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9500H Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9500 Series Switches
Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: - Certain traffic flows are getting routed to the wrong next-hop MAC address. This will translate into problems like, end users not able to ping certain IPs or specific webpages are timing-out/not opening. - There's evidence of having download failures in the switch logs, i.e.: %FMFP-3-OBJ_DWNLD_TO_DP_FAILED: F0/0: fman_fp_image: adj 0x50, Flags Incomplete download to DP failed Conditions: - This issue has been seen in the field and recreated by TAC on C9600X-SUP-2 running IOS-XE release 17.10.1. Note: This issue is not specific to 17.10.1. If the trigger conditions are matched, it'll hit 17.7.1, 17.8.1, 17.9.(1/2/3), and 17.11.1. - This issue is the consequence of a hardware misprograming, where instead of using MAC_ADDRESS A as the correct next-hop, an incorrect MAC_ADDRESS, MAC_ADDRESS B is used to route certain traffic flows. Traffic is getting forwarded out of the C9600 switch, but dropped at the next-hop as it is reaching the incorrect routing neighbor. If you suspect that you are running into this defect, engage Cisco TAC to help validate the issue. Workaround: Shut/no shut the L3 interface where the switch has the legit/valid neighbor/next-hop for the affected traffic flows may resolve the connectivity issue temporarily. BUG headline: Catalyst 9000 Switch loses VLAN database content
Product - Series: Cisco Catalyst IE3300 Rugged Series,Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst IE9300 Rugged Series,Cisco Catalyst 9400 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst IE3200 Rugged Series,Cisco Catalyst IE3400 Rugged Series,Cisco Catalyst 9600 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 8300 Series Edge Platforms,Cisco Catalyst 9200 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9500 Series Switches
Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: If all the specific conditions from section below are met then the Catalyst 9000 Switch loses the content of the vlan.dat file, resulting in a loss of connectivity as the Vlans are gone. This issue affects all variants of Catalyst 9000 Switches (C9200 / C9300 / C9400 / C9500 and C9600). The issue is seen on standalone, Switch Stack and Stackwise Virtual deployments. Conditions: The issue will be seen after doing a manual reload once an IOS upgrade/downgrade was performed on the switch. Will be seen in the versions where "vtp version" is nvgened, which was done to add yang support for this cli, This fix is present from releases 17.12.1, 17.6.6, 17.9.4. Where downgrading/upgrading from these releases to other releases is causing this. This is due to the "vtp version" being nvgened, that is present in "show running", which is a design change done to enable yang for this CLI. Workaround: For releases, which does not have this infra, we dont have a way to fix this issue. Please apply following work-arounds to resolve this issue. a. configure vtp version to 1,(please make sure no vtp version cli is present in show running), will not nvgen and no parsing of the config will be done, no issue will be seen- Applicable from 17.13 b. as vtp domain config loss is happening after downgrade/upgrade, before reloading create a new vlan which will populate the vlan.dat file after downgrade/upgrade and issue will resolved. Further Problem Description: If the code update is performed via ISSU (for Stackwise Virtual setups) then issue is seen after the second reloads. Meaning, the first reload is the one done via ISSU triggers the issue where the domain loss will happen(vlan.dat file shows 564 Bytes), then a second reload the issue hit and vlans will lost. Besides Catalyst 9000 Switches, other IOS-XE based Switching platforms such as the IE9300 and the IE3x00 Rugged Series Switches are also affected by this issue. Catalyst 8300 Routers using SM-Based Switching Modules are also affected by this issue. Verify the vlan.dat file size (RT# dir | inc vlan.dat), as it is seen on all Catalyst Switches) then we know the issue will happen on the next reload. This issue triggered while implementing the fix of CSCwe51080 which was later backed out on CSCwn20712. The changes in CSCwi46941 address the issues in both CSCwe51080 and CSCwi46941. PSIRT Evaluation: The Cisco PSIRT has evaluated this issue and determined that it does not have a security impact that requires PSIRT ownership or involvement. This issue will be addressed via normal resolution channels. There is no PSIRT restriction that prohibits making this bug visible. If you believe that there is new information that would cause a change in the severity of this issue, please contact psirt@cisco.com for another evaluation. Additional information on Cisco's security vulnerability policy can be found at the following URL: https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/resources/security_vulnerability_policy.html

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: 9800 rejects clients with wrong PMKID with reason "CO_CLIENT_DELETE_REASON_DOT11_INVALID_PMKID" Conditions: In eWLC, When client moves from FT-AKM to dot1x-AKM, controller ignores the PMKID and initiates a 802.1x-EAP (PMK cache is not deleted). In AireOs, When client moves from FT-AKM to dot1x-AKM, controller ignores the PMKID and initiates a 802.1x-EAP (PMK cache is not deleted). While 802.1x-EAP transaction happens, Client initate a over-the-air Fast transition. controller allows this transition to happen and matches the PMKR1Name and continues to do Fast roam. The above flow helps the customer to keep the Audit session ID Workaround: None Further Problem Description: Although this bug CSCwa67566 shows as fixed in 17.9.1, after an FT (11r) to dot1x (11i) roam, the client may be stuck in RUN state, but unable to pass traffic. Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: Clients fails to do 802.1x authentication. Controller does not send EAP_ID_REQ and could see following error messages: [sanet-shim-translate] [20227]: (ERR): MAC@ :Failed to get sanet extn params.SSID length is 0 [client-auth] [20227]: (ERR): MAC: MAC@ L2 Authentication Start failed. method DOT1X, Policy VLAN 0,AAA override = 1 , NAC = 0 SSID length is 0 log is sometimes seen in events where client is able to do 802.1x authentication Conditions: First observed in 17.12.5 with 802.1x 11r and the "wireless client vlan-persistent" feature enabled globally on the WLC. Workaround: Downgrade code versions or disable "wireless client vlan-persistent". Disabling the VLAN persistent feature is global and does not cause a service interruption. Rebooting the AP may temporarily resolve the problem but it will return within hours or days. Further Problem Description: On a Catalyst 9800 controller running version 17.12.4 or .5 with the global "wireless client vlan-persistent" feature enabled will see clients on a 802.1x SSID with 11r, may see clients fail to authenticate. Within a radioactive trace, the following logs are seen: [sanet-shim-translate] [20227]: (ERR): MAC@ :Failed to get sanet extn params.SSID length is 0 [client-auth] [20227]: (ERR): MAC: MAC@ L2 Authentication Start failed. method DOT1X, Policy VLAN 0,AAA override = 1 , NAC = 0 An over-the-air capture or AP debug will show the client repeatedly sending an EAP response after the EAP start but it will never progress beyond the initial EAP start. Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: An IOS-XE device may experience an unexpected reboot, generating system-report, core, and crash files. This occurs during the Certificate Revocation List (CRL) fetch process, often indicated by: Jul 26 05:42:48.824: %PKI-6-TRUSTPOINT_DELETE: Trustpoint: DNAC-CA deleted succesfully Jul 26 05:42:49.089: %PARSER-5-HIDDEN: Warning!!! ' crypto key zeroize rsa DNAC-CA' is a hidden command. Use of this command is not recommended/supported and will be removed in future. CMD: 'crypto pki trustpoint DNAC-CA' 05:42:50 UTC Sat Jul 26 2025 Jul 26 05:42:50.382: %PKI-6-TRUSTPOINT_CREATE: Trustpoint: DNAC-CA created succesfully Jul 26 05:42:50.628: %PKI-3-CRL_FETCH_FAIL: CRL fetch for trustpoint DNAC-CA failed Reason : Failed to select socket. Timeout : 5 (Connection timed out) Conditions: This issue occurs when attempting to import a Certificate Authority (CA) chain with revocation checking set to 'crl' or 'crl none'. More specifically, the reboot happens if the CRL is being inserted after its associated trustpoint was deleted.This is Platform independent issue, can impact any box having this config. The sequence of events leading to the crash involves: 1) A trustpoint, through which a CRL was downloaded, is deleted. 2) The CRL fetch operation is performed. 3) When the system attempts to install the fetched CRL, it looks for the now-deleted trustpoint, leading to an access of freed memory and a device crash. This can be triggered manually or automatically via a controller such as CATC/DNAC. Workaround: To prevent this issue, ensure that the trustpoint associated with a CRL is removed after removing the CRL and downloading the CRL. One more option is to set revocation check to 'none' Further Problem Description: The root cause is an improper validity check of the trustpoint during the CRL download process. The system attempts to access a memory location (the trustpoint's label) that has already been freed because the trustpoint was deleted. The code fix addresses this by implementing a proper validity check for the trustpoint within the CRL processing flow.

BUG headline: Memory Leak in NBAR-SDAVC-Scheduler Leading to System Crash
Product - Series: Cisco 9800 Series Wireless Controllers,Cisco 8000 Series Routers,Cisco Catalyst 8200 Series Edge uCPE,Cisco Integrated Services Virtual Router,Cisco Catalyst 8000V Edge Software,Cisco Catalyst 8300 Series Edge Platforms,Cisco Catalyst 9200 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9500 Series Switches,Cisco SD-WAN,Cisco ASR 1000 Series Aggregation Services Routers,Cisco Catalyst 8500L Series Edge Platforms,Cisco Catalyst 9800 Series Wireless Controllers,Cisco Catalyst 9400 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 8200 Series Edge Platforms,Cisco Catalyst 3650 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9500H Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst Cellular Gateways,Cisco Catalyst 8500 Series Edge Platforms,Cisco 4000 Series Integrated Services Routers,Cisco Catalyst 8300 Series Edge Universal CPE,Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9600 Series Switches,Cisco 1000 Series Integrated Services Routers,Cisco Catalyst 3850 Series Switches,Cisco Cloud Services Router 1000V Series
Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: A memory leak occurs in the nbar-sdavc-scheduler process, leading to high memory usage and eventual system crashes. The system logs will show %SYS-2-MALLOCFAIL messages indicating memory allocation failures. Conditions: This issue is observed under the following conditions: - NBAR (Network-Based Application Recognition) is configured and in use. - The NBAR state becomes stuck in a 'PENDING' state for an extended period. This can happen, for example, after a system crash and subsequent switchover where ACKs are not received from all active clients. Switch#show ip nbar control-plane | i NBAR config state NBAR config state is PENDING Workaround: Reload the affected device and ensure that the NBAR state becomes 'ACTIVE'. Further Problem Description: The memory leak occurs when the NBAR-SDAVC-Scheduler process, responsible for managing NBAR configurations, enters a 'PENDING' state. In this state, the process accumulates configuration messages in an internal cache. An issue with this caching mechanism prevents these messages from being properly cleared, leading to a gradual but continuous increase in memory consumption. This uncontrolled memory growth eventually exhausts available system resources, causing the device to crash. The implemented solution introduces an enhanced monitoring and cleanup process. This process actively tracks the status of configuration message delivery. If a response is not received within a set timeframe, it identifies the communication issue, marks the configuration state as an error, and proactively clears the accumulated cache. This prevents further memory accumulation, thereby ensuring system stability and reliable NBAR operation.

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: DNS cache entries in NBAR are being populated even without a valid dns response. Conditions: SDWAN cedge running 17.3.2 Workaround: At this time there is no workaround. Please open a TAC case for further assistance. Further Problem Description: This issue is caused by clients sending multiple DNS requests in the same source/dest port. This is an uncommon behavior. Because NBAR is flow based. When the first request is sent, we will classify that flow based on the URL in the request. If another request is sent on that same source/dest port, we will classify the response IP as the application of the URL in the first request as the flow had already been classified based on the first packet. A fix for this issue was included in version 17.8.1 and up. It was also fixed as part of PP#60 that can be loaded on top of any 17.3.x and 17.6.x release. Also - it was fixed in 17.6.5 version specifically, to be used by customers which cant use PP update mechanism.

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: Data traffic destined to myapps.microsoft.com and enterpriseregistration.windows.net can cause conflicting entries in the NBAR dns learning cache. This can cause either flow to break depending on which happened first. Scenario is user A visits myapps.microsoft.com and it is classified as ms-services, cached in DNS cache, and egresses the router via CoR SaaS. Now user B visits enterpriseregistration.windows.net and the DNS cache is overwritten with windows-azure classification. Considering windows-azure is not in the CoR SaaS app-list, this is breaking the new flows for user A and since DNS entry is cached on the host, it is not overwriting the cache again. Check this via the commands below: show ip nbar classification dns learning cache 100000 show ip nbar classification socket-cache 100000 show sdwan app-fwd cflowd flows table To clear the DNS learning cache and check if that momentarily solves the issue: clear ip nbar classification dns learning cache Conditions: 1. CoR SaaS is used to send office365 traffic DIA. 2. windows-azure applications are used in the environment. Workaround: At this time there is no workaround, please open a TAC case. Release Note Enclosure: Switch experiences an unexpected reload Symptom: A Cat 9200 or 9200L switch may crash during virtual memory address translation. Most reloads will state a "Critical process fed fault on fp_0_0 (rc=139)", but some crashes will state "linux_iosd-image process on rp_0_0" or in rare cases a “Power Failure or Unknown” reload reason. Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: The IOS XE Smart Licensing daemon accumulated a binary/non-printable event log buffer of ~49 million characters without any size bound. When a user ran show license (or equivalent), SmartAgentDaemonShowEventLog_v2 → saShowEventLogInfo attempted to print this entire buffer via vsnprintf → IOS __doprnt. The __doprnt function iterated character by character, escaping each non-printable byte as \xXX (4 operations per byte). After printing 49,115,187 characters, the SIGVTALRM CPU hog watchdog fired. During stack unwinding, aarch64_fallback_frame_state encountered a corrupted return address (0x434) causing a secondary SIGSEGV that terminated the process. Impact Complete IOS XE process crash (linux_iosd-image killed) → RP reload Trigger Running any show command that invokes Smart Licensing event log display when the buffer is large Platform ASR1100 (AArch64, IOS XE 17.15.04c) — any platform using Smart Licensing is potentially affected Frequency risk Event log grows over time; devices running longer without license renewals are more likely to accumulate large logs Workaround Periodically clear Smart Licensing event log (license smart clear eventlog) to prevent buffer from growing unboundedly Conditions: The IOS XE Smart Licensing daemon accumulated a binary/non-printable event log buffer of ~49 million characters without any size bound. BOOTUP Logs: =========== sai_stage1: %OMPD-5-STATE_UP: R0/0: ompd: Operational state changed to UP sai_stage1: %VDAEMON-5-CONTROL_CONN_STATE_CHANGE: ... vManage 1.1.1.5 ... is UP sai_stage1: %DMI-5-AUTH_PASSED: User 'vmanage-admin' authenticated from 1.1.1.5 for netconf This is an **SD-WAN (Viptela) managed device**. vManage (1.1.1.5) was regularly connecting via NETCONF throughout the 5-day uptime — dozens of sessions. **vManage periodic NETCONF polling likely triggered the show license CLI** that invoked SmartAgentDaemonShowEventLog_v2. # How the crash was triggered: =========================== vManage NETCONF session → show license tech-support (or similar which we can confirm from customer to see what sort of outputs they collect related to the → SmartAgentDaemonShowEventLog_v2 → eventLogBuffer accumulated over 5 days = 49M chars → __doprnt CPU hog → SIGVTALRM → SIGSEGV → crash Workaround: The device will keep crashing until the eventLogBuffer is cleared. Options: Option 1 — Clear via CLI before vManage reconnects:license smart clear eventlog Run this immediately after boot before vManage NETCONF sessions start. Release Note Enclosure: Major releases and their minor releases starting at 17.7.x up to and including 17.13.x are impacted. Symptom: Ev type static route is installed in the global VRF for local-learned MAC/IPs that are single-homed or dual-homed single-active. These routes are visible with "show ip route" and "show ip static route", "show ipv6 route" and "show ipv6 static" respectively. The Ev type static routes are non-redistributable and do not have any effect outside of the device they are installed on. However, there is a possibility of the routes not being cleaned up which can leave a local adjacency which should not be present (seen when removing and re-adding VRF configuration, static routes can end up remaining in the global VRF table). Also - the routes are not needed for single-homed and dual-homed single-active MAC/IPs and may take up hardware resources unnecessarily. Conditions: BGP EVPN fabric with IRB. Workaround: No workaround. Further Problem Description: The Ev type static route was introduced in 17.7.1 for multi-homing all-active redundancy feature in EVPN Over MPLS with Integrated Routing and Bridging (https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/td/docs/routers/ios/config/17-x/mpls/b-mpls/m-evpn-over-mpls.html under Host MAC-IP Synchronization). As of 17.7.1 single-homed and dual-homed single-active MAC/IPs inherited this behavior. The inheriting of this behavior by single-homed and dual-homed single-active MAC/IPs is reverted with this defect while the behavior remains in place for multi-homed all-active MAC/IPs.

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: After deleting a Virtual Routing and Forwarding (VRF) instance (or removing its Route Distinguisher (RD) or VRF address-family), the device may take longer than expected to fully remove associated Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) routes and state. As a result, attempting to re-create a VRF with the same name shortly afterward may fail or require waiting, because the prior VRF’s BGP cleanup is still in progress. You can observe the condition by checking BGP VRF/AF state. The following sanitized output illustrates the behavior: Example: * Immediately after VRF deletion: Device# show bgp vpnv4 unicast all state BGP topology state: global::VPNv4 Unicast, state: normal VRF_NAME::VPNv4 Unicast, state: reset or delete in progress Flags: 0xXXXXXXXX scanner imported path deletion in progress * After cleanup completes: Device# show bgp vpnv4 unicast all state BGP topology state: global::VPNv4 Unicast, state: normal (Entry for VRF_NAME no longer present) Conditions: This issue can occur when any of the following configuration actions are performed on the device: 1. VRF deletion 2. VRF RD removal 3. VRF address-family removal This behavior is especially noticeable in environments where automated configuration workflows (for example, programmatic configuration replacement/transactions) delete and re-create VRFs quickly, because the BGP cleanup window can block immediate reuse of the VRF name. Workaround: Wait for the BGP cleanup to complete before re-creating the VRF with the same name. Practical options include: * Add a delay between the delete and re-create operations in automation workflows. * Increase the application/workflow timeout for VRF re-provisioning steps. Limitation: This workaround may not be acceptable for workflows that require fast, transactional VRF replacement because it introduces operational delay. Further Problem Description: In affected software, BGP cleanup after VRF deletion may take multiple scan cycles (the BGP general scan typically runs every 60 seconds), which can lead to delays on the order of minutes before a VRF name can be safely re-used.

Note: This workaround is only applicable if your wireless authentication does not require MPPE encryption keys. Further Problem Description: The IOS-XE RADIUS client fails to properly decode the MS-MPPE-Send-Key attribute (Microsoft Point-to-Point Encryption Send Key) when sent by the RADIUS server. Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: A standby member in a Catalyst 9200L stack may reload unexpectedly with a Critical software exception after issuing switch provision , causing stack member removal, SSO switchover, and service impact. Conditions: Occurs on Catalyst 9200/9200L stacks during stack scaling or configuration synchronization events that trigger DBAL GET‑N / GET‑N‑RECURSIVE queries (for example "switch provision ", SVI scaling, or NETCONF/DMI sync), particularly in environments with a large number of interfaces, SVIs or static routes. Workaround: There is no complete workaround that prevents the issue in IOS‑XE 17.15.x once the triggering conditions are met. However, the following mitigations can be done to prevent this event: Avoid stack scaling during production or perform the stack expasion after upgrading to a fixed version (17.15.5 or later). Further Problem Description: When a Catalyst 9200/9200L switch stack running IOS‑XE 17.15.x performs stack scaling or configuration synchronization operations, the system initiates a DMI/NETCONF database synchronization and rebuilds the operational state of interfaces and SVIs. In environments with a large number of interfaces, VLANs, SVIs, or scaling static routes from dashboard, this process can trigger DBAL database queries. Due to a software defect, the DBAL EVENTS handling may encounter a fatal condition, causing the linux_iosd process to crash on the standby stack member. As a result, the affected standby switch is removed from the stack and reloads unexpectedly, which may lead to an SSO switchover and temporary traffic disruption. The behavior is not expected and is not related to hardware failure. This issue is resolved in later IOS‑XE releases where the DBAL query handling logic has been corrected.

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: A Cisco IOS-XE device may experience a crash due to a spinlock condition happening in LFTS (Linux Forwarding Transport Service). The symptoms of this crash may show the following: 1) IOS crashes with the PuntInject Keepalive process. In this case, the IOSd crash is a victim of the underlying spinlock. UNIX-EXT-SIGNAL: Aborted(6), Process = PuntInject Keepalive Process 2) A kernel core file + kernel.rp.txt file is written. In this case, the kernel.rp.txt file will show the linux dmesg buffer which shows the CPU stall followed by a locked up thread with the lsmpi-rx process: [74755.149954] rcu: INFO: rcu_sched self-detected stall on CPU [74755.149986] CPU: 1 PID: 5132 Comm: lsmpi-rx Kdump: loaded Tainted: G S W O 5.15.167 #1 .. [74755.150089] RIP: 0010:queued_spin_lock_slowpath+0x43/0x1a0 .. [74755.150121] tcp_v4_err+0xe1/0x4e0 [74755.150129] icmp_unreach+0x87/0x190 [74755.150135] icmp_rcv+0x195/0x440 [74755.150141] ip_protocol_deliver_rcu+0x1ff/0x210 [74755.150145] ip_local_deliver_finish+0x44/0x60 [74755.150150] lfts_xmit+0x355/0x4f0 [lfts] 3) In some instances reported, after the device has experienced the condition a hang maybe observed while in the crashing state. A hard power-cycle is needed to recover from the situation. In this scenario, the device may have written traces to the flash under a pd_info directory which may contain a dmesg_output* file. The resulting dmesg_output file would show the same call trace dumped for the queued_spin_lock_slowpath. Conditions: This is a platform independent problem and has been observed on both Catalyst 9000 series switches (in both SDA/non-SDA environments) and 9800 WLCs. This has been with a modified 'ip mtu' configuration under an interface used for access the device (typically the loopback0 or a wireless management interface / SVI) Workaround: There are no known workarounds. Bringing the MTU on the accessible interface (loopback0, WMI, etc.) back to the default 1500 bytes can avoid the spinlock crash. This does NOT apply to a management port such as GigabitEthernet0/0. Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: - Issue is caused due to IOS TFTP detects as mandatory the BLKSIZE if there's any other optional header, however, based on the RFC, BLKSIZE shouldn't be mandatory if there's any other options header. - This happens from 17.12.X onwards. - TFTP request (RQQ) containing optional headers (ex: timeout, tsize, etc) without including blksize: [packet capture information] Trivial File Transfer Protocol Opcode: Read Request (1) Source File: ATA3001AFB249E8.cnf.xml Type: octet Option: timeout = 5 Option: tsize = 0 - The following error is displayed on debugs: TFTP: Looking for ATA3001AFB249E8.cnf.xml TFTP: Invalid option Handling blksize_option failure TFTP: Setting server block size to 512 Conditions: - Platform: C8200-1N-4T - Software: c8000be-universalk9.17.15.03a.SPA.bin - When the TFTP client (ATA) makes the request (RQQ) to the TFTP server (CME) it'll fail if it doesn't contains the BLKSIZE optional header. - Router is used as CME; issue has been observed only on ATA191 registration. Symptom: An IOS-XE device (router, switch, etc.) may experience a crash in IOS after running the show logging last ... command. show version may reflect a last reload reason of "Critical software exception", and the event should generate a system-report and/or crashinfo file. Conditions: A device running an affected version of code. The device crashes immediately after running the show logging last ... command. This issue results from a Segmentation Fault in the Exec (console), Virtual Exec (telnet), or SSH processes, depending on how the user was accessing the device when the "show logging last ..." command was run. Executing ‘show install rollback id <>? again should show SMU as type instead of ??? and we would not hit the error again. After successful installation of new SMU for new version we are no longer dependent on these SMUs. Option 2: ( Needs fix) and invocation from DNAC before SMU workflow Install remove file was supposed to help clearing such SMU entries if requested. But as you confirmed that CLI is not working effectively then we need to fix it. I believe it is broken 17.9 onwards. So unlike option 1 which restores the file, this option would be used to remove tracking of the file. So, that Improper state error is not hit.

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: If the subject-alt-name attribute is added to a certificate trustpoint, SCEP requests for that trustpoint are rejected by Windows NDES/CA due to invalid data. Error: WIN32: 13 ERROR_INVALID_DATA - Error Parsing Request Conditions: When the "ip domain name xxxx" setting is configured, the Zero Touch Deployment (ZTD) script automatically appends the configured domain name to the CN in the subject-name attribute of the certificate trustpoint. This triggers IOS-XE to add the subject-alt-name attribute to the same trustpoint. When that happens, the automatically generated subject-alt-name may cause the SCEP enrolment to Windows NDES/CA to fail because the SCEP request contains invalid data. Workaround: Do not configure the "ip domain name xxxx" setting. Further Problem Description: The automatic configuration of subject-alt-name was added in IOS-XE 17.7. The problem is caused by incorrect SAN encoding. Encoding was fixed with this bug fix.

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: Weak cryptographic algorithms should not be used for PKI as they are insecure and do not provide adequate protection from modern threats. These algorithms should be replaced with stronger algorithms. The following algorithms will be rejected when configured: -pki trustpoint - hash md5 - pki server - hash md5 - crypto pki certificate self-signed hash md5 Conditions: Device configured with weak cryptographic algorithms (hash md5) used in an PKI configuration. Workaround: Update the configuration to use strong cryptographic algorithms used for PKI. If that's not possible, then the following configuration command is required for PKI to continue to function with the weak algorithms upon an upgrade to IOS XE version 17.11.1: Device(config)#crypto engine compliance shield disable Note the above command will only take effect after a reboot. Hence this command should be enabled on the older image and already rebooted before upgrading to 17.11 or higher Cisco does NOT recommend this option as these weak cryptographic algorithms are insecure and do not provide adequate protection from modern threats and should only be used as a last resort.
