Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: The Catalyst 9k switch may experience a REPM process crash due to memory remap failure. In the output of "show platform software process database install-manager switch active R0 summary REPM_DB" the "Records" counter for "repm_tables_tbl" is increasing. This happens every time "show install summary" command is run. Eventually the switch runs out of memory allocated to its database and reloads. Conditions: The problem was found on an Active switch in stacked environment that went through a software upgrade to IOSXE version 17.8.x or newer. The problem was observed in a particular scenario where the switch is managed by DNA Center running version 2.3.5.3. In this setup a synchronization with the device is performed every 10 minutes. For each synchronization the controller is executing "show install summary" command and this causes additional tables getting created in REPM database. Workaround: Reloading the Active switch in the stack releases the memory After downgrading to 17.6.5 the issue was not observed anymore. Further Problem Description: Depending on how frequently the "show install summary" command is executed it might take between 4 to 8 weeks to deplete the available memory and observe the crash. Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: When an NHRP reply message is received, it corresponding request is not found in the re-transmit timer list and the reply is dropped and not processed, this would result in either a delay in bringing up an NHRP session (registration) or result in a flap of an NHRP shortcut tunnel (resolution). Conditions: There is no specific condition, it all depends on the sequence of replies that are received that exposes the logical error in code where an unrelated request is dequeued which again results in when the original reply is received the request is not found (as it was removed earlier case) and response is dropped before processing it. Workaround: There is no workaround available, however, this condition should not be very severe as the messages would be sent out after a certain NHRP control timer/data event. Ex: If a resolution request's reply was dropped, then the nhrp cache entry would time out and the tunnel would be torn down, then the shortcut tunnel would be recreated on the next data packet to the peer spoke. Further Problem Description: When an unrelated request is dequeued, the original request for which the reply was received still remains in the re-transmit queue, this will cause it to be sent again on the next retry interval and upon receiving the reply this request will be eventually deleted from the re-transmit queue. This will be extra control req/reply pair of messages that will be exchanged between the peers, as the request is eventually removed, hence no case of memory build up.

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: An IOS-XE device running software version 17.12.x or higher can experience a failure when renewing/installing certificates using SCEP with the default trustpoint hash algorithm set to SHA256. The failure occurs because the IOS-XE SCEP client is unable to properly parse the PKCS7 response signed with "sha256 With RSA Encryption." Although SHA256 is used for encryption, the SCEP client cannot decrypt the certificate signed with SHA256. As a result, the certificate renewal process fails. Conditions: - An IOS-XE device running software version 17.12.x or higher - Trustpoint is configured with the default hash algorithm set to SHA256. - SCEP server returns a certificate response signed with sha256 With RSA Encryption. - Certificate renewal/installation attempts fail when using the default SHA256 trustpoint hash. Workaround: Identify devices where trustpoint sdn-network-infra-iwan renewal has past expiration date. If past current date, requires: • force telemetry push • Manually update crypto pki trustpoint sdn-network-infra-iwan from "hash sha256" to "hash sha512". If "not past current date", update "crypto pki trustpoint sdn-network-infra-iwan" from "hash sha256" to "hash sha512" If customer upgrades to fixed version, the trustpoint will retain the same hash value. • Perform a force push to delete and create the new trustpoint. All new trustpoints will get created with "hash sha512" crypto pki trustpoint xyz enrollment url http://:80 subject-name cn=xyz.com subject-alt-name xyz.com.com revocation-check crl rsakeypair key 2048 no hash sha256 <<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<< hash sha512 <<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<< Further Problem Description:

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: When this issue occurs, a route-map pushed to a cEdge device via a CLI add-on template in Cisco SD-WAN Manager (vManage) is applied incompletely. Specifically, the description and match ip address statements within the route-map are missing on the device, even though vManage reports no errors and the configuration appears correct locally on the controller. You can verify this by running the following command on the affected edge device and observing that the expected statements are absent: Router# show sdwan running-config | section route-map route-map EDGE permit 110 set community 200:3051 route-map EDGE deny 990 The expected output should include additional statements, such as: Router# show sdwan running-config | section route-map route-map EDGE permit 110 description SET COMMUNITY FOR EDGE ROUTES set community 200:3051 match ip address prefix-list SITE-ROUTES route-map EDGE deny 990 description EXPLICIT DENY Conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met: - A route-map is deployed to a cEdge device using a CLI add-on template in Cisco SD-WAN Manager (vManage). - The vManage controller is running version 20.13.x or 20.14.x. - The target cEdge device is running an IOS XE software release that is earlier than the release series corresponding to the vManage version (for example, IOS XE 17.9.x when managed by vManage 20.13.x or 20.14.x). Note: The issue does not occur when the cEdge device is running the same release series as the vManage controller (for example, IOS XE 17.13.x or later when managed by vManage 20.13.x). Workaround: Option 1: Upgrade the cEdge device (Recommended) Upgrade the affected cEdge device to a software release within the same release series as the vManage controller. For example, if vManage is running 20.15.x, upgrade the cEdge to IOS XE 17.15.x. Option 2: Apply missing configuration manually If an immediate upgrade is not possible, manually apply the missing route-map statements directly on the affected device via CLI: Router# configure terminal Router(config)# route-map EDGE permit 110 Router(config-route-map)# description SET COMMUNITY FOR EDGE ROUTES Router(config-route-map)# match ip address prefix-list SITE-ROUTES Router(config-route-map)# end Note: Manually applied configurations may be overwritten the next time a CLI add-on template is pushed from vManage. Verify that subsequent template deployments do not revert these changes. Option 3: Use deprecated command syntax in the CLI template (vManage 20.15 and later) If you are running vManage version 20.15 or later and pushing to a cEdge device running an IOS XE release earlier than 17.15, include both the current and deprecated command forms in the CLI add-on template to ensure compatibility: route-map EDGE permit 110 description SET COMMUNITY FOR EDGE ROUTES description-deprecated SET COMMUNITY FOR EDGE ROUTES match ip address prefix-list SITE-ROUTES match ip address prefix-list-deprecated SITE-ROUTES Note: The deprecated command forms are silently disregarded by devices that support the current syntax, so including both forms does not cause errors on newer devices. Further Problem Description: PSIRT Evaluation: The Cisco PSIRT has evaluated this issue and determined it does not meet the criteria for PSIRT ownership or involvement. This issue will be addressed via normal resolution channels. If you believe that there is new information that would cause a change in the severity of this issue, please contact psirt@cisco.com for another evaluation. Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: This issues can be seen in deployments where we have FIAB (fabric in a box) and external border. On the FIAB, we have connected subnet in which clients are sitting. This subnet is advertised to border node, so border node will create entry for subnet in map cache. When Border will receive traffic for this subnet, based on this entry, it will send traffic to FIAB. When traffic will come to FIAB, it will check if client is connected / registered in fabric. Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: In Cisco SDA Fabric, Edge/Border fail to forward traffic to the desired ETR/RLOC. This causes end-to-end reachability, where traffic appears dropped by the Fabric. More specifically the CEF Signal Suppression is enabled, preventing the device from performing the LISP Map-Request to build the Map Cache/ and CEF table. The device incorrectly routing the traffic should show the following: - the LISP Control Plane has the Endpoint ID registered: ``` Border#show lisp instance-id 4097 ipv4 server 172.16.0.2 LISP Site Registration Information Locator Local State Pri/Wgt Scope 192.168.0.10 yes up 10/10 IPv4 none ``` - the LISP map-cache redirects to the Proxy ETR: ``` Border#show lisp instance-id 4097 ipv4 map-cache 172.16.0.2 LISP IPv4 Mapping Cache for EID-table default (IID 4097), 5 entries 172.16.0.2/32, uptime: 00:02:56, expires: never, via site-registration, send-map-request Sources: site-registration State: send-map-request, last modified: 00:02:56, map-source: local Exempt, Packets out: 12(6912 bytes), counters are not accurate (~ 00:00:25 ago) Configured as EID address space Encapsulating to proxy ETR ``` - the CEF signal suppression is enabled: ``` Border#show cef table internal Subblocks: Signal OCEs using this table for signal suppression state: 28 Suppress signal: enabled. ``` Conditions: This is seen in Fabric devices running 17.6.4 and earlier. Workaround: One granular workaround is to manually trigger the Map Request using the LIG tool or Ping command. Another more global is to clear the local LISP map-cache using "clear lisp instance-id * ipv4 map-cache". Further Problem Description: Fabric devices are not resolving remote destination due to signal suppression being enabled. This occurs in the situation that the number of entries should be well within range Signal suppression can occur when the number of entries exceeds the limit of the platform. When the number of entries reaches below a threshold signal suppression would again be disabled. In case of this issue signal suppression is not disabled when the amount of entries is below the limit and no clear indication exists that the maximum amount has been ever reached.

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: BFD session will remain in down state and not come up between a Nexus 9000 and Catalyst 9000 if we are using authentication with a key chain/string that is 16 characters or longer. Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: Route reflector chooses EVPN Ethernet Auto-discovery Route learned from route reflector peer as bestpath instead of the path learned directly the route reflector client. Conditions: Client is peering with multiple route reflectors, with route reflectors peering with each other and each having different cluster-id. Workaround: Configure the route reflectors with the same cluster-id. Further Problem Description: This behavior can result in high CPU. A particular route reflector will likely learn a route from the client first and and advertise it out before receiving a copy from its peering route reflectors. Because the route-reflector learned path is then chosen as best, a withdrawal will be sent to peering route-reflectors as non-client learned paths are not to be advertised to non-clients. All the peering route reflectors will thus be left with only the client-learned path and start advertising again. This creates the potential for a cycle of updates and withdrawals, causing high CPU. This can eventually converge if the timing of the updates and withdrawals settles on a state where one route reflector in the cluster only has the client-learned path with no other updates pending. A consequence of this is that a cluster may have only one device that forwards the path into the network and thus loses the redundancy of having redundant route reflectors. The bestpath decision causing this behavior occurs prior to the traditional bestpath tie-breaking algorithm, so there is no policy that can bypass it. The problem can be avoided by configuring the same cluster-id within the cluster peering with the same client, as then the route reflectors will not advertise the route to each other and trigger the bestpath behavior.

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: -BGP Sessions in active and Standby not in sync -Packet loss during SSO -BGP session flap on standby due to malformed updates Conditions: -Affects dual-RP platforms -SSO configured globally -Additional-paths send/receive configured on a neighbor or on an address-family Workaround: Remove SSO globally and additional-paths configuration from the address-family: router bgp no bgp ha-mode sso address-family no bgp additional-paths [send|receive] Then, for each affected neighbor, enable and disable additional-paths individually. This will clear the neighbor from the bad state router bgp address-family neighbor additional-paths send receive no neighbor additional-paths send receive At this point, the device is no longer in problem state. You may configure EITHER ha-mode sso OR additional-paths [send|receive] on the neighbor, BUT NOT BOTH Further Problem Description: The problem is only present in dual-RP devices. If possible, AVOID configuring sso at the global and neighbor level simultaneously (i.e. 'bgp ha-mode sso' and also 'neighbor ha-mode sso' under router bgp), unless disabling sso on an individual neighbor ('neighbor ha-mode sso disable'). Similarly, AVOID configuring additional-paths [send|receive] at the address-family and neighbor level simultaneously (i.e. 'bgp additional-paths [send|receive]' and also 'bgp additional-paths [send|receive]' under address-family mode in router bgp), unless disabling additional-paths on an individual neighbor ('neighbor additional-paths disable')

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: Netconf is not allowing connections to the device to get information or edit configuration. Checking the yang management processes we see Confd status: Phase1 and several processes in Failed state. show platform software yang-management process state Confd Status: Phase1 Process Status State ------------------------------------------------------- nesd Not Running Failed syncfd Not Running Failed ncsshd Running Init dmiauthd Not Running Failed nginx Running Not Applicable ndbmand Running Active pubd Running Active gnmib Not Running Not Applicable Conditions: OSPF is configured with VRF routing on the device. Netconf will fail with an error when ip ospf and the VRF are configured on an interface. Here is an example of the error: *Mar 7 19:04:07.036: %DMI-3-SYNC_ERR: Switch 1 R0/0: dmiauthd: An attempt to synchronize the running configuration to the NETCONF running data store has failed: /ios:native/interface/TenGigabitEthernet{1/0/1}/ip/ios-ospf:router-ospf/ospf/process-id{10}/id (value "10"): Configure router ospf and/or interface vrf(if applicable) at first before enabling respective ip ospf process; To delete/replace VRF remove ip ospf first. To delete router ospf remove ip ospf first This issue will occur with any interface (loopback, vlan, portchannel, subinterface, etc.). Here is an example configuration that is affected: ip vrf any_vrf router ospf 10 vrf any_vrf interface loopback 0 ip vrf forwarding any_vrf ip ospf 10 area 1 netconf-yang Workaround: Instead of using "ip vrf" the following can be used to define the vrf: vrf definition any_vrf ! address-family ipv4 exit-address-family Then under the interface "vrf forwarding" would be configured instead of "ip vrf forwarding" interface loopback 0 vrf forwarding any_vrf ip ospf 10 area 1 Note: When a VRF is removed from the device other configurations dependent on it may be removed as well. This means any router OSPF commands, as well as interfaces in a VRF, will need to be reconfigured after removed and readding the VRF commands. Note that when an interface is removed from a VRF the IP address is removed as well. This process can be simplified by using the following command: vrf upgrade-cli multi-af-mode {common-policies | non-common-policies} Information on this command can be found under "Single-Protocol VRF to Multiprotocol VRF Migration" here: https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/td/docs/ios-xml/ios/mp_l3_vpns/configuration/xe-3s/mp-l3-vpns-xe-3s-book/mp-vpn-ipv4-ipv6.html Further Problem Description: The following versions are affected: 17.16.1 17.15.2 The following versions are NOT affected: 17.9.6a 17.12.4

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: Loss of internet connectivity across all virtual networks (both IPv4 and IPv6) when FIAB loses connection to the remote border. LISP map-cache missing PETR entry, preventing traffic from reaching the internet even after the remote border connection is restored. Persistent connectivity issues despite the underlying physical link being restored. Conditions: SDA Architecture: The network is utilizing SDA Transit with SDA Pub/Sub. Fabric in a Box (FIAB) Design: The FIAB relies on a remote border node to provide internet access. Software Versions: DNAC: 2.3.7 IOS-XE: 17.12.4 / 17.15.2 C9300 Connectivity Loss Scenario: The FIAB temporarily loses its connection to the remote border node responsible for internet access. This results in a partial network outage and loss of internet connectivity for all overlay networks. Both IPv4 and IPv6 traffic are affected across the fabric. LISP Behavior: In a working state, the LISP map-cache for the corresponding instance-ID contains the PETR entry (Remote Border RLOC). When the FIAB loses connection to the remote border node, the LISP map-cache entry is not refreshed. Even after the connection is restored, the missing map-cache entry prevents internet access for all virtual networks. Workaround: Manual workarounds: clear lisp instance-id ipv4 refresh-subscription clear ipv6 lisp instance-id refresh-subscription Alternatively we can use EEM script attached Further Problem Description:

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: ISIS WATCHDOG crash when processing default route. Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: A vulnerability in the Protocol Independent Multicast (PIM) feature of Cisco IOS XE Software could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause a denial of service (DoS) condition on an affected device. Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: IOSd crashed in ospf router process when a config (DEFAULT_CONFIG attached) from bootflash is applied to running config. Conditions: Two different sequence of ospf operations: one triggered area deletion, and another triggered area creation with same id, while the deletion of area was still not complete. Use of memory by the newly created area post completion of deleted area has lead to this crash. Two configurations in this defect that has triggered this specific conditions are: passive-interface loopback0 and ip ospf area configuration under loopback0 interface, and mpls traffic-eng area 0 configuration. Workaround: No workarounds exist. Further Problem Description: Two different sequence of ospf operation: Sequence-1: ospf router process has triggered deletion of empty ospf area. And while the ospf_delete_area was in-execution, this process got suspended before deletion of otl area for area-id 0. passive-interface loopback0 config could have made this ospf area empty and could have triggered the delete area. Other interfaces may have been scheduled to be added to the area, but they are not scheduled yet, and hence empty area is being deleted. Sequence-2: "mpls traffic-eng area 0" has started to create area 0 from the parser context. Create area is attempting to create area 0, and otl area look-up for area 0 has returned the otl area memory pointer, which is valid now, but when the create area is complete, and when process gets context switched, ospf router process that was suspended above in ospf delete area resumes and now continues to delete the otl area memory pointer of previous area 0. But, Since, the new area 0 is also sharing the otl area memory block, accessing it now leads to crash.

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: When there are parallel adjacencies and one of them goes down, ISIS does not advertise the other active neighbor. This leads to traffic drop. Issue is seen after partial lsp-generation is introduced in 17.9. Hence fix is applicable to 17.9 and newer releases. Conditions: When there are parallel p2p interfaces and when features such as link-attributes, Segment-routing are not configured, only one adjacency with best metric is advertised. Release Note Enclosure:
Symptom: Unexpected device reload when device-tracking feature (SISF) is enabled and left running for a long time. When the crash occurs the below messages are generated: Exception to IOS Thread: Frame pointer 0x4DDE51E0, PC = 0x69692C50 UNIX-EXT-SIGNAL: Segmentation fault(11), Process = SISF Main Thread The crash is caused by a memory leak with the below symptoms: 1. In the output of "show process memory platform sorted" the RSS counter for linux_iosd-imag process is continuously increasing.
Switch#show process memory platform sorted System memory: 7764904K total, 3943700K used, 3821204K free, Lowest: 3820208K Pid Text Data Stack Dynamic RSS Name ---------------------------------------------------------------------- 10260 227197 2000240 136 364 2000240 linux_iosd-imag
AND 2. In the output of "show process memory platform detailed name iosd smaps | begin IOS_PRIV_OPER_DB" the Size and Rss counters are rapidly increasing:
Switch#show proc mem plat detailed name iosd smaps | begin IOS_PRIV_OPER_DB 8c80000000-8ccf5a1000 rw-s 00000000 00:28 88415 /tmp/rp/tdldb/0/IOS_PRIV_OPER_DB Size: 1300100 kB Rss: 1295284 kB
Conditions: This problem may happen over time if device-tracking MAC entries are repetitively deleted and created. Workaround: A periodic reboot of the affected device will reset the memory usage. The "device-tracking tdl-disable" service-internal command may be used to disable the SISF Crimson DB entirely and avoid this issue; however, this means that no SISF data will be available via the Crimson DB to any consumer (e.g. DNAC). This command requires service-internal to remain enabled to persist through reloads. This workaround will prevent further memory leakage due to this issue, but will not recover any memory that has already been leaked; a reboot will do this. The CLI only disables Notifications to DNAC, the command still holds good for switches with no DNAC implementation (of discovered MAC and IP bindings) what so ever. With TDL disabled, there is no functional change on the switch itself. An SMU hot patch is available for download for C9300, C9400, C9500 and C9600 platforms. Further Problem Description: When a Crimson DB entry is created, some elements like calendar_time are automatically allocated by the TDL library. The SISF code was also allocating that element without checking whether it already existed, leading to a leak. Over the course of time, after millions of creation / deletion cycles of device-tracking MAC entries, the switch runs out of Crimson memory. This issue was introduced in a new feature in 17.2.1 and 16.12.3. It exists in all releases from there until the releases where it has been fixed; it is fixed in 16.12.5, 17.3.2 and 17.4.1 (note that it is not fixed in 17.2.x). It is in PI code and may therefore be observed on any platform that supports both Crimson and SISF.

Release Note Enclosure: ACR pushes with standard 2-block VTY payloads (0-4, 5-50) leave VTY 16-50 with incomplete management-plane configuration. Missing exec-timeout causes stale VTY sessions to never time out (resource consumption + security exposure). Missing privilege level results in incorrect exec authorization on VTY 16-50 sessions. transport defaulting to ssh-only silently blocks non-SSH management access (e.g., telnet where required) on VTY 16-50. Silent failure with no NETCONF error means config drift goes undetected without explicit post-push validation. Affects all ACR/NETCONF-managed C9800 deployments on 17.15.x using the standard 2-block VTY payload structure. Symptom: After NETCONF replace push with a VTY block spanning 5-50 on C9800-80-K9 running IOS-XE 17.15.03: Device splits VTY 5-50 into two ranges: 5-15 and 16-50 VTY 5-15: receives all 5 config elements (exec-timeout, logging, password, privilege, transport) ✅ VTY 16-50: receives only 1 of 5 elements (password only) ❌ exec-timeout: MISSING privilege level: MISSING logging synchronous: MISSING transport input: defaults to ssh instead of all No error in NETCONF response ( returned) NETCONF get-config confirms partial config on VTY 16-50 Conditions: Platform: C9800-80-K9 Wireless LAN Controller IOS-XE: 17.15.03 (SMU-PATCHED) NETCONF: Port 830, candidate-datastore enabled Operation: edit-config with nc:operation="replace" on Payload defines a single VTY block 550 (or any block crossing line 16) with full config (timeout, logging, password, privilege, transport) 100% reproducible on first push Triggers on both 2-block (0-4, 5-50) and single-block (5-50) payloads Workaround: Use a 3-block VTY structure in ACR payloads, aligned to the platform boundary at line 16: Copy Code Block 1: 04 (full config) Block 2: 515 (full config) Block 3: 1650 (full config) The device applies full config to all VTY ranges and auto-merges 5-15 + 16-50 → 5-50 in show run if configs are identical. Workaround is effective and deployable in ACR templates. Further Problem Description: The platform has an internal VTY boundary at line 16. When a single NETCONF replace block spans this boundary, only the element propagates to the 16-50 range; all other elements (exec-timeout, privilege, logging, transport) are silently dropped or defaulted. Splitting the payload into 3 explicit blocks aligned to the boundary (0-4, 5-15, 16-50) avoids the issue. Not reproducible on IOS-XE 17.18.03 on the same platform — the 2-block payload (0-4, 5-50) applies full config across all VTY lines with no boundary split. Related to companion Bug A (VTY 0-4 privilege level 15 drop) which also affects NETCONF VTY handling on 17.15.03.

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: In a scenario where the Rendezvous Point (RP) is external to an SD-Access fabric, users may encounter a noticeable delay ranging from 30 to 60 seconds during the initial multicast traffic stream from a source, despite receivers already being part of the PIM shared tree within the fabric. This delay typically occurs when a Border node has pre-existing *,G state with the RLOCs of both the First Hop Router FHR and Last Hop Router LHR listed in the OIL for that group. Upon receipt of a PIM Join message from the External RP—a process that acts akin to a turnaround router or proxy join timer—the Border forms an S,G state. However, it cannot immediately import the OIL from the *,G state. This leads to a recalculation period where the OIL must be computed once more to facilitate the transition to the Source Tree, resulting in the observed startup delay for multicast traffic. Conditions: Native Multicast in use, not Headend Replication. External RP to the SD-Access fabric. Initial delay for new multicast group traffic, no prior S,G states. Workaround: Configure the Borders as RPs rather than using External RP (can be used in combination with MSDP) Further Problem Description:

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: A device may experience an unexpected reload. This occurs when multiple IP Service Level Agreement (IP SLA) configurations are sent to the device simultaneously, or when IP SLA operations are deleted and recreated rapidly (for example, during a configuration replacement operation). When this issue occurs, the system generates a crash file indicating a segmentation fault in the IP SLA Dynamic Hostname Process. The following sanitized output illustrates the error message seen in the crash information: Exception to IOS Thread: Frame pointer 0xXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX, PC = 0xXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX UNIX-EXT-SIGNAL: Segmentation fault(11), Process = IP SLA DynHostName Process -Traceback= 1#XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX ... Conditions: This issue is observed under the following conditions: 1. The device is configured with IP SLA operations (specifically icmp-echo probes using hostnames). 2. The global command 'ip sla periodic hostname resolution' is enabled. 3. IP SLA configurations are being modified, deleted, or replaced (e.g., via configure replace) while the hostname resolution process is active. The following sanitized configuration commands demonstrate the feature enablement that triggers this susceptibility: ! Enabling periodic hostname resolution Device(config)# ip sla periodic hostname resolution ! Sample IP SLA configuration using hostnames Device(config)# ip sla 100 Device(config-ip-sla)# icmp-echo www.example.com source-ip 192.0.2.1 Device(config-ip-sla)# exit Device(config)# ip sla schedule 100 life forever start-time now Workaround: To prevent the unexpected reload, disable the periodic hostname resolution feature. This can be done by removing the command from the global configuration: Device(config)# no ip sla periodic hostname resolution Note: When this command is disabled, the hostname defined in the IP SLA probe will be resolved only once during the initial configuration. It will not be dynamically re-resolved every few minutes. This workaround is acceptable unless the target hostname's IP address changes frequently. Further Problem Description: The crash is caused by a race condition where IP SLA operations are deleted (freed from memory) while the background dynamic hostname resolution thread attempts to access them to update resolved IP addresses. Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: In the event of a Layer 2 loop occurring within a Software-Defined Access (SDA) Fabric Edge node, the Anycast Gateway IP address associated with a specific VLAN may be incorrectly learned through a physical access port. This mislearning can occur even if the physical port is in a non-connected or error-disabled state. Consequently, the Anycast Gateway (SVI) entry in the Switch Integrated Security Features (SISF) / Device-Tracking database may go into a DOWN state or point to the wrong interface. Since this entry is crucial for the proper functioning of DHCP, client devices within the fabric may fail to obtain an IP address or experience significant network disruption. The following sanitized syslog message may be observed, indicating the SVI IP address is being "stolen" by a physical port: %SISF-4-IP_THEFT: IP Theft IP=192.0.2.1 VLAN=100 MAC=xxxx.xxxx.xxxx New(Spoof) MAC=yyyy.yyyy.yyyy IF=Vl100 New IF=GigabitEthernet1/0/1 Additionally, the device-tracking database may show the SVI entry in a DOWN state or associated with a physical interface instead of the VLAN interface: Device# show device-tracking database Network Layer Address Link Layer Address Interface vlan prlvl age state 192.0.2.1 xxxx.xxxx.xxxx Vl100 100 0100 7mn DOWN Conditions: This issue is observed in Cisco SDA Fabric Edge environments under the following conditions: - A Layer 2 loop occurs on the network. - The affected access port is configured with dot1x or MAB authentication. - The Anycast Gateway IP/MAC is incorrectly learned via the looped physical port. Workaround: To recover the SVI state after the Layer 2 loop has been resolved, remove and re-configure the affected SVI. 1. Remove the affected VLAN interface: Device# configure terminal Device(config)# no interface Vlan 2. Re-create the interface and re-apply the original configuration: Device(config)# interface Vlan Device(config-if)# ip address Device(config-if)# ip helper-address ! Re-apply other necessary configurations Further Problem Description: This defect addresses the hardening of the SVI SISF protection mechanism to prevent the Anycast Gateway from being overwritten during loop events. It does not prevent the Layer 2 loop itself.

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: In ISIS multi-topology not every change of "isis ipv6 metric " results in SPF calculation in MT-2. Result is that IPv6 RIB is not immediately recalculated. Both, primary and backup paths do not reflect latest metric setting. Note, problem is not seen for every metric change, only some changes are not detected. For example it's known that metric change between 1030 and 1240 is not detected. Detection of metric change is done by comparison of memory where is located old and new neighbor advertisement (TLV 222), Due bug it is not compared full size of metric field, hence some changes are detectable and some not. Conditions: ISIS multi-topology. Changes in interface command "isis ipv6 metric " Workaround: Next SPF fixes the problem. ISIS runs periodic SPFs every 15mins, so longest time to fix issue is 15mins, However it's possible new SPF is triggered sooner. SPF can be triggered manually by command test isis spf. Further Problem Description: Issue is PI, all platforms are affected. it's day-1 issue, rekeases without fix are affected.

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: NETCONF edit-config RPCs may time out. Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: Affected Cisco SD-WAN edge routers intermittently delay SNMPv3 Engine Discovery responses by approximately 15 seconds, even though the discovery requests are received immediately and forwarded to the SNMP application. During the delay, the collector retransmits requests every second. The router subsequently sends multiple usmStatsUnknownEngineIDs.0 Report PDUs together in a burst, often after the collector has already timed out or closed the associated UDP sockets. This results in inconsistent SNMPv3 discovery and authentication failures, devices being reported as unreachable, and missing or delayed monitoring data across the SD-WAN deployment. FIA traces show that the inbound packets are successfully punted to the control plane, with no forwarding-plane packet drops, confirming that the delay occurs after delivery to the SNMP application Conditions: Platform: C8200,IR8340 Software: IOS XE SD-WAN 17.15.4. SNMP version: SNMPv3. SNMP traffic is received through the SD-WAN tunnel and addressed to the management Loopback0 interface. The issue occurs while the router is under normal production SNMP polling load. Multiple NMS systems may be polling the router concurrently. A GetBulk operation is repeatedly executed against: 1.3.6.1.4.1.9.9.1002.1.1.5 ciscoMgmt.1002.1.1.5 CISCO-SDWAN-BFD-MIB::bfdSummary show snmp monitor response records these GetBulk operations taking approximately 14.6?16.8 seconds, closely matching the Engine Discovery response delay. The router may have packets queued in the SNMP process input queue while the slow request is being processed. The issue does not reproduce in an isolated lab test without the production polling condition; the same Engine Discovery transaction completes in less than 1 millisecond. No interface flap, QFP drop, tunnel failure, or ICMP error precedes the original delay. The router configuration may already exclude the affected BFD subtrees from the SNMP view, but slow processing is still observed for the same OID. Workaround: No confirmed router-side workaround is currently available. The recommended operational workaround is to remove the following OID from the NMS polling profile: 1.3.6.1.4.1.9.9.1002.1.1.5 1.3.6.1.4.1.9.9.1002.1.1.6 Further Problem Description:

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: This issue has been observed in deployments with multiple BGP peers in the IDLE or ACTIVE state that are continuously attempting to establish BGP peering. Starting with version 17.15.2, each time an IDLE BGP peer fails to establish a connection, it triggers the BGP scanner process. If multiple BGP peers remain in the IDLE state, the scanner process may run almost continuously, resulting in high CPU utilization. Normally, the BGP scanner process should run periodically (by default, every 60 seconds), and IDLE peers should not trigger it. This behavior has been observed starting with version 17.15.2. Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: A TCP-based application may be unable to write data on the wire. Conditions: This issue can occur under very rare timing conditions when a non-blocking TCP application is flow-controlled after a burst of outbound data, and the peer’s receive window changes while the local TCP send queue is recovering. Workaround: If application-level keepalives are used, they may also fail to be sent, causing the session to flap after the hold-down timer expires. Restarting the affected TCP session restores communication. Further Problem Description: In this condition, TCP may fail to notify the application that the connection is writable again after the send queue and peer window recover. The fix ensures that blocked writers are notified when the TCP connection can accept data again. Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: On Cisco IOS XE 17.15.x and later, LISP control-plane packets sent toward LISP components are sourced from an RLOC IP address that does NOT correspond to the actual outbound interface determined by the IPv4 routing table. The xTR consistently selects the numerically lowest IPv4 RLOC address configured under LISP as the IPv4 source address, regardless of which interface is used to forward the packet. On 17.12.x the behavior was different: the source IP matched the outbound interface address, so the source IP and the egress interface were always consistent. Because of this mismatch, if the upstream ISP or firewall enforces source-address filtering or strict-mode uRPF, the LISP control-plane packets are dropped. Conditions: - Cisco IOS XE Release 17.15.x or later. - The device is configured as a LISP xTR with two or more IPv4 RLOCs, and the RLOCs reside on different interfaces. - The default route (or the route used to reach LISP components) egresses an interface whose IP address is NOT the numerically lowest RLOC IP. Workaround: As a potential workaround, you can apply the following configuration: router lisp ipv4 source-locator Please note, however, that while this configuration works fine as long as the preferred source-locator interface is Up, if that interface goes down, the router will continue to use the down interface's IP address as the source IP when sending traffic out of a different interface. Because of this, you must use IP SLA/Tracking to monitor the status and reachability of each interface, and use EEM to dynamically control the configuration changes as needed whenever an interface state change occurs. Further Problem Description: This issue has been observed on the following versions: - 17.15.3a - 17.15.5 - 17.18.2 This issue has NOT been observed on the following versions: - 17.12.4 - 17.12.7b

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: - Running with 17.x release, no synchronization between the running and the candidate when we are changing the hostname after checking with the netconf. Conditions: - Issue only reported only in releases 17.x train. - Issue is not seen on 16.x train we tried the following: config t no Netconf-yang feature candidate-datastore netconf-yang feature candidate-datatstore end then run the script again. Essentially, the script 1. log in via IOS VTY with a long username, configure a hostname by CLI 2. validate that the current hostname is changed by CLI 3. validate that the current hostname is changed by Netconf get-config RPC 4. change the hostname by Netconf edit-config RPC 5. validate that the current hostname is correct by CLI ==> it failed at step 3 Workaround: Change the VTY username to a shorter name until a proper fix is in place. Further Problem Description: The issue occurs when we log in the VTY console with a long username and makes a configuration change. There is an internal bug that expects the username within a certain length. When the length is exceeded, a failure occurs that results in the config syncing failure. Though it was seen when "netconf-yang feature candidate-datatstore" was configured, it is not specific to candidate-datatstore. It could occur when "netconf-yang" is configured, regardless of if candidate-datatstore is configured or not.

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: Catalyst 9300L switch crash due to SISF there were "ip dhcp snooping" on vlan but no policy configured on trunk port. More than 4000 entries, 10-20 are normal. Others are from link local FE80 on trunk port. Crash happened when deleting one of FE80 entry (INCOMPLETE) > do invalid of related event ctx > event ctx in hash table already corrupted Conditions: This issue would occur when there is a large number of entries in the device-tracking database, mostly for IPv6 Link-Local addresses found on a port connected to another switch, typically configured as a trunk port. however, for this issue, there was no policy configured on the truck port, which cause SISF learn/delete of link locak entries in a loop. Generate lots of events. Workaround: configure the device-tracking policy on trunk port. See the Configuration Guide https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/td/docs/switches/lan/catalyst3850/software/release/16-6/configuration_guide/sec/b_166_sec_3850_cg/configuring_sisf_based_device_tracking.html#task_pzl_vxj_bfb, which could be useful for the customer to consult with. Further Problem Description: the fix has been committed to 17.3.6

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: In certain load scenarios, IOS can allocate a lot of transient memory to communicate information to other processes in the system. This will lead to memory pressure and all the things that you would expect under memory pressure is observed (CPUHOGS, memory warnings, etc) Once the memory is cleaned up, it is added to the IOS only pool and is not released back to the system for use by other processes. Conditions: This has only been seen in SDWAN applications, but in theory, it can occur in other features Workaround: There are no workarounds Further Problem Description: This issue is never the cause of a problem. The true underlying problem is whatever caused massive transient memory consumption. This issue only cleans up after such a thing has occurred. The code changes here allow the system to recover from a bad state. It doesn't cause the bad state in the first place, nor does it fix the bad state. Consider this a serviceability or reliability fix.

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: In Cisco IOS software that is using the Multiprotocol Label Switching (MPLS) Label Distribution Protocol (LDP), LDP may fail to withdraw some of the label bindings previously advertised to one or more peers. When this problem happens an error message similar to the following may be seen on the router that fails to withdraw the bindings: TIB-5-WDRAWTAG: 10.1.1.0/255.255.255.0, tag 44873; Withdrawn tag record has timed out Since this error message is throttled, a single error message is likely to be seen even if many label bindings are affected in a short period of time. Affected label bindings will continue to be stored in Label Information Bases (LIBs) of peers that do not receive the withdraw messages. Conditions: The problem is extremely unlikely to be encountered. It happens when LDP is unable to send the withdraw messages for one or more label bindings for more than 5 minutes after the associated local label bindings have been withdrawn. This has not been observed in normal situations. It has only been observed when stress testing the system with an unusually large number of IGP routes--50,000--and when all of these routes are simultaneously removed, creating a huge workload. Workaround: The problem can be corrected by restarting the LDP session, for example, via the clear mpls ldp neighbor EXEC command. Further Problem Description:

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: A vulnerability in the implementation of the Resource Public Key Infrastructure (RPKI) feature of Cisco IOS XE Software could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause the Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) process to crash, resulting in a denial of service (DoS) condition. This vulnerability is due to the incorrect handling of a specific RPKI to Router (RTR) Protocol packet header. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by compromising the RPKI validator server and sending a specifically crafted RTR packet to an affected device. Alternatively, the attacker could use man-in-the-middle techniques to impersonate the RPKI validator server and send a crafted RTR response packet over the established RTR TCP connection to the affected device. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to cause a DoS condition because the BGP process could constantly restart and BGP routing could become unstable. Cisco has released software updates that address this vulnerability. There are no workarounds that address this vulnerability. This advisory is available at the following link: https://tools.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-iosxe-rpki-dos-2EgCNeKE Conditions: Please refer to the Security Advisory. Release Note Enclosure:
Symptom: When a device [switch/router/...] is running IOS-XE release 17.04.01 or earlier and has aaa server group configuration block referencing VRF to provide connectivity to TACACS+ or RADIUS server outside of the global routing table, and this VRF is configured using the ip vrf syntax, such configuration will be rejected upon upgrade to 17.05.01 or later release. This will result in the loss of connectivity to the affected TACACS+ or RADIUS server unless it is also reachable within the global routing table. The following messages will be seen on the console upon bootup [depending on whether IPv4 or IPv6 connectivity towards TACACS+ or RADIUS server is used] IPv4 Table-id not existing for tacacs sg VRF, config may fail IPv6 table-id not existing for tacacs sg VRF, config may fail IPv4 Tableid not existing for radius sg VRF, config may fail IPv6 Tableid not existing for radius sg VRF config may fail Conditions: - device is running IOS-XE release 17.04.01 or earlier - aaa server group configured for RADIUS or TACACS+ servers is using VRF to provide connectivity to the server(s) - VRF is configured using the ip vrf syntax If these conditions are met, and the device is upgraded to 17.05.01 or later release, the VRF configuration under the aaa group server configuration block will be rejected. This will result in the loss of connectivity to the affected TACACS+ or RADIUS server unless it is also reachable within the global routing table. Workaround: Convert the VRF configuration from the ip vrf syntax to the vrf definition syntax 

vrf upgrade-cli multi-af-mode non-common-policies vrf
or 

vrf upgrade-cli multi-af-mode common-policies vrf
Further Problem Description: A sample of the problematic configuration could look like this: 

!
aaa new-model
aaa group server radius 
 server-private  key 
 ip vrf forwarding 
aaa group server tacacs+ 
 server-private  key 
 ip vrf forwarding 
!
ip vrf VRF_NAME
!
This configuration has been accepted and works fine in IOS-XE releases up to 17.04.01. Starting from the 17.05.01 release, additional validation of the supplied VRF is performed in AAA code, and if the VRF referenced within the aaa group server configuration block does not exist, the line is rejected. The reason for this rejection upon bootup is that VRF is configured using the ip vrf syntax is located below the aaa group server configuration block, and thus, at the time when AAA code is validating the supplied VRF, such VRF has not been created yet.

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: The system crashes. After the crash, multiple messages each 5 seconds appear in the Syslogs, as follows: %PKI-3-CRL_FETCH_FAIL: CRL fetch for trustpoint DNAC-CA failed Reason : Failed to select socket. Timeout : 5 (Connection timed out) The router is unable to fetch a CRL from the DNAC-CA trustpoint and faces a timeout of 5 seconds. or %PKI-3-CRL_FETCH_FAIL: CRL fetch for trustpoint DNAC-CA failed Reason : Enrollment URL not configured Conditions: This issue was found on an ISR 4K running 17.5.1a (others may apply). A DNAC-CA trustpoint was configured, containing a certificate that refers to a CRL Distribution Point (CDP), however the device was unable to download the CRL from the CDP, as indicated by the %PKI-3-CRL_FETCH_FAIL errors. Example of the affected configuration: crypto pki trustpoint DNAC-CA enrollment mode ra enrollment terminal usage ssl-client revocation-check crl none <<<<<<<<<<<<<< Workaround: There are multiple potential workarounds: Workaround1: Make sure the CDP is reachable from the device, so the CRL download does not fail. Workaround2: If using Cisco DNA Center 2.3.4.0 or later to manage the device, follow these steps to disable the CRL check: 1) In the Cisco DNA Center GUI navigate to Design > Network Settings > Security and Trust, and select "Revocation - Check: None" from the dropdown. 2) Navigate to Provision > Inventory, select the device, and select Actions > Telemetry > Update Telemety Settings ; make sure the "Force Configuration Push" checkbox is checked, click Next, optionally choose when to deploy the change, and click Apply. Workaround 3: If the device is managed by Cisco DNA Center 2.3.3.x or older, or is not managed by Cisco DNA Center, then manually disable the CRL check on the device: crypto pki trustpoint DNAC-CA revocation-check none PLEASE NOTE: disabling the CRL check may weaken security. If the Cisco DNA Center certificate gets revoked and is placed on the CRL, the device will not be aware of this and will still consider the certificate as valid. Check fixed releases - bug is resolved in 17.6.6 Further Problem Description:

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: On a C9600X or C9500X in stackwise-virtual, after a reload or power-cycle, ports could show as down or err-disabled. This behavior is specific to dual-rate optics such as SFP-10/25G-LR-S, on linecards or switches that have port-groups (this includes C9600-LC-48YL, and C9600-LC-40YL4CD, and C9500X-60L4D). Ports in a port-group will detect a config-mismatch between other port in the port-group, resulting in one or both interfaces in the port-group being down or errdisable. Logs that may be seen (if errdisable detect cause sfp-config-mismatch is not configured, will not see this error message): %PM-4-ERR_DISABLE: sfp-config-mismatch error detected on Fif1/1/0/41, putting Fif1/1/0/41 in err-disable state Conditions: C9600X or C9500X in stackwise-virtual running on software versions 17.10.1 and above. Hardware: • C9600-LC-48YL • C9600-LC-40YL4CD • C9500X-60L4D • Dual-rate optics such as SFP-10/25G-LR-S Upon reload or power-cycle, will see interfaces on the switch go down or errdisable due to sfp-config-mismatch If interface is down or errdisabled can check if there is mismatch in hardware speed: Switch#show platform hardware fed switch active npu slot 1 port 12 port-info ----------- Display L1 port debug info------------ |-------------------------------------------------| | SW port debug states | |-------------------------------------------------| | Slot/Port | 1/12 | Speed | speed_25Gbps <<<<<< Checking what this is set to. If interface is configured for 10G, but 25G is seen here; that is indicative of this defect. | Active | Yes | XCVR Presence | Present | Admin | Enabled | Disabled | Yes | Link State | Down | Init Done | Yes | XCVR Type | 750 | Breakout | Disabled | Delete Mask | 0 | LED State | Amber On | Breakout Progress | 0 | Breakout Mode | 7 | Maximum Subports | 0 | Port Group Cfg | 2 | Port Group mode | 0 | Flow Control Mode | TX/RX OFF |-------------------------------------------------| |-------------------------------------------------| | LED port debug states | |-------------------------------------------------| | Slot/Port | 1/12 | Suspended | Yes | Stp blocked | No | Txrx_error | No | Txrx_active | No |-------------------------------------------------| LC present 0 Outstanding ports to be deleted 48 Total failed deleted ports 0 Check what ports are in port-group: Switch#show hw-module switch 1 slot 1 port-group speed ------------------ show portmap switch 1 slot 1 speed ------------------ -------------------------------------------------- Port-groupPorts Speed -------------------------------------------------- 1 Fif1/0/1, Fif1/0/2 NONE 2 Fif1/0/3, Fif1/0/4 NONE 3 Fif1/0/5, Fif1/0/6 NONE 4 Fif1/0/7, Fif1/0/8 NONE 5 Fif1/0/9, Fif1/0/10 NONE 6 Fif1/0/11, Fif1/0/12 NONE Workaround: 1. Configure 'Errdisable detect cause sfp-config-mismatch' and 'Errdisable Recovery cause sfp-config-mismatch'. This allows the errdisable state to be detected and the switch will attempt to recover the interface after set amount of time. The default time for errdisable recovery is 5 minutes (300 seconds); this can be changed down to 30 seconds with command 'errdisable recovery interval 30'. Switch(config)#errdisable recovery interval 30 2. Shut / No shut the affected interfaces if they are errdisable and errdisable recovery is not configured. 3. Remove and re-insert the optics of the affected interfaces. 4. Use hard-coded optics instead of dual-rate. For example, SFP-10G-LR is a hard-coded optic, and SFP-10/25G-LR is a dual-rate optic. Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: A vulnerability in the TLS library of Cisco IOS XE Software could allow an unauthenticated, adjacent attacker to exhaust the available memory of an affected device. This vulnerability is due to improper management of memory resources during TLS connection setup. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by repeatedly triggering the conditions that cause the memory increase. This could be done in a variety of ways, such as by repeatedly attempting Extensible Authentication Protocol (EAP) authentication when local EAP is enabled on an affected device or by using a machine-in-the-middle attack and resetting TLS connections between the affected device and other devices. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to exhaust the available memory on an affected device, resulting in an unexpected reload and a denial of service (DoS) condition. This advisory is available at the following link: https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-iosxe-tls-dos-TVgLDEZL Conditions: Please refer to the Security Advisory. Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: Locally destined messages may be lost after shutting and then no-shutting a Dialer interface, or an associated interface with which it shares a configured IP. Conditions: This may happen for sessions created from interfaces (such as Dialer or Virtual-Template interfaces) that have a configured IP address. A configured address includes one that is configured directly on the interface (eg: ip address A.B.C.D 255.255.255.0) or shared through the "ip unnumbered" command (eg: ip unnumbered Loopback0). Workaround: Configure the Dialer or Virtual-Template interface so that its gets an IP address from a local pool. Alternatively, it can also be configured to receive an IP address delegated to it from its peer (eg: DHCP). This way, the address will only be owned by the Virtual-Access interface created for the resultant session, allowing for consistent behaviour for the session while it is up. Further Problem Description: The same issue also affects SCEP enrollment process due to mishandling of incoming packet for SCEP enrollment request resulting in resetting the connection. Conditions: Example of excessive rate of the following logs: 2024/01/31 07:03:37.788716629 {plogd_R0-0}{1}: [plogd] [27960]: UUID: 0, ra: 0, TID: 0 (debug): sending: facility 16. %IOSXE-6-PLATFORM: R0/0: cpp_cp: QFP:0.0 Thread:004 TS:00003516285262695048 %FW-6-SESS_AUDIT_TRAIL: (target:class)-(INSIDE-to-INSIDE:INSIDE-to-INSIDE):Stop tcp session: initiator (:) sent 0 bytes -- responder (:) sent 0 bytes, from 2024/02/21 07:31:09.465865578 {plogd_R0-0}{1}: [plogd] [8731]: UUID: 0, ra: 0, TID: 0 (debug): sending: facility 16. %IOSXE-6-PLATFORM: R0/0: cpp_cp: QFP:0.0 Thread:003 TS:00000001369394636708 %FW-6-SESS_AUDIT_TRAIL_START: (target:class)-(INSIDE-to-INSIDE:INSIDE-to-INSIDE):Start tcp session: initiator (:) -- responder (:) from Interface Workaround: If the ZBF logging is the culprit, use High-Speed Logging with Netflow: https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/td/docs/ios-xml/ios/sec_data_zbf/configuration/xe-16/sec-data-zbf-xe-16-book/sec-data-fw-hsl.html If Controller-mode Implicit ACL Logging is the culprit, disable implicit-acl-logging OR increase the log-frequency to reduce the chance of hitting this. Here are other options to solve this problem: + Under policy configuration, increase the log-frequency to 2048 or some higher number which needs to be base 2. This would reduce the likelihood of the issue but still might be seen under the right conditions. + Under policy configuration, remove "implicit-acl-logging". Further Problem Description: The Plogd process fails due to it is not capable of store a burst of logs being generated in a short of time, these logs can be generated by any feature, therefore it is expected to hit the crash even if ZBFW is not configured or if the command "implicit-acl-logging" is not applied. So far ZBF and ACL are the known features that can trigger this failure but it may happen due to another feature. The fix for this process is not a change on the feature generating the logs but an optimization on how the logs are being stored and handled by Plogd process.

Release Note Enclosure: The bug was found during customer use. Symptom: - When attempting to push a device template with a CLI add-on to an IOS-XE SD-WAN (cEdge) router in controller mode, an error message is encountered: CONFD_ERRCODE_INCONSISTENT_VALU(38). - The error specifically points to the description in a route-map, indicating a discrepancy between vManage's attempts to over-write the existing description which has been pushed via a previous CLI Add-On Template. - The inability to overwrite the route-map description results in a configuration push failure, impacting the customer’s ability to manage router configurations effectively. Conditions: - The issue is observed with SDWAN setups using IOS-XE SD-WAN (cEdge) routers and controller mode. - It only arises when trying to update or overwrite the route-map description using the CLI Add-On Template from vManage. - vManage software version in use: 20.13.1; cEdge version: 17.13.1a. - Existing configurations on the router include route-map descriptions which are not being overwritten by new template configurations. Workaround: - The only current workaround identified is to manually remove the CLI Add-On template entirely, push the configuration to the router, and then re-add a new CLI Add-On template. However, this approach may not be feasible for the customer’s operational environment. Further Problem Description: - The issue lies in the discrepancy between the IOSd and Confd configurations when using vManage to push template updates. After pushing the updated CLI Add-On Template: Router#sh run | sec route-map <<<<<<<< IOSd config route-map TO-SP1-EDGE deny 110 description BLOCK ENTERPRISE NETWORKS <<<<<<<< Old description is still present description *** BLOCK ENTERPRISE NETWORKS *** <<<<<<<< New description is also present match ip address prefix-list AEP-PUB-SIXTEEN DEFAULT-ONLY TEN-SLASH-EIGHT <<>> Router#sh sdwan run | sec route-map <<<<<<<< Confd config route-map TO-SP1-EDGE deny 110 description BLOCK ENTERPRISE NETWORKS <<<<<<<< Only old description is present match ip address prefix-list AEP-PUB-SIXTEEN DEFAULT-ONLY TEN-SLASH-EIGHT <<>>

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: A router or switch running IOS-XE may experience a signal 6 "abort" in the DBAL EVENTS process. This is triggered by a thread deadlock scenario causing the process to stop responding when walking data related to the "GREEN" assist facility. UNIX-EXT-SIGNAL: Aborted(6), Process = DBAL EVENTS Conditions: - So far seen in IOS-XE 17.9.x, 17.12.x. Other versions may be impacted. - Could be triggered be something that updates the Crimson DB, which the GREEN facility acts as a query and validation service for. This is very broad and could include something like a route or adjacency update. Exact triggers are unknown but very rare. Workaround: None. Unless it is clear what is triggering this, a code upgrade is required. Further Problem Description: The reason for the crash is due to GREEN-BE trying to set the DB thread affinity while IOS is also setting DB thread affinity through the DB lock manager. Only the DB lock manager should be doing this, but if both are trying to set affinity it ends up in a deadlock, resulting in a signal 6 "abort". Please open a TAC case if you suspect you're hitting this bug, as there are several crashes related to DBAL EVENTS that could appear similar at surface level.

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: A router running an IOS-XE may experience a crash when a user exits an SSH session after one or more users had very recently made TACACS configuration changes via SSH. Conditions: TACACS configuration changes were made via SSH seconds or minutes prior to a concurrent SSH session logging out. This bug is very rare to hit and requires very specific timing of events. Workaround: Avoid using SSH for TACACS configuration changes. Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: A switch can unexpectedly reload due to a critical software exception, cause by a memory allocation error. Exception to IOS Thread: Frame pointer 0xXXXXXXX, PC = 0xXXXXXXX UNIX-EXT-SIGNAL: Segmentation fault(11), Process = SISF Main Thread When this issue is encountered, a long-term increase in the size of the Crimson IOS Private Operational Database will be observed. In the output of "show process memory platform detailed name iosd smaps | begin IOS_PRIV_OPER_DB" the Size and Rss counters are rapidly increasing: Switch#show proc mem plat detailed name iosd smaps | begin IOS_PRIV_OPER_DB 8c80000000-8ccf5a1000 rw-s 00000000 00:28 88415 /tmp/rp/tdldb/0/IOS_PRIV_OPER_DB Size: 1300100 kB Rss: 1295284 kB Note that the immediate symptoms of this issue may vary depending on which feature is first unable to allocate new memory when it needs to, but the database size increase will always be present. Conditions: This problem may happen over time as device-tracking MAC entries with attached IPv6 addresses are created and removed from the SISF database. IPv4 addresses do not trigger this issue. Note that this is triggered by the presence of IPv6 addresses in the network; no specific IPv6 configuration on the affected device is required. Workaround: A periodic reboot of the affected device will reset the memory usage. The "device-tracking tdl-disable" service-internal command may be used to disable the SISF Crimson DB entirely and avoid this issue; however, this means that no SISF data will be available via the Crimson DB to any consumer (e.g. DNAC). This command requires service-internal to remain enabled to persist through reloads. Further Problem Description: When devices are detected in the network, SISF adds entries for the MAC and IP addresses to the Crimson DB, and creates a linkage between the two to indicate their association. On deletion, memory in the linkage between MAC and IPv6 entries is not entirely freed. Over time, as millions of such linkages are created and deleted in response to network events, the switch's Crimson memory is exhausted. This issue was introduced in a new feature in 17.2.1 and 16.12.3. It exists in all releases from there until the releases where it has been fixed; it is fixed in 17.3.6, 17.6.4 and 17.9.1. It is in PI code and may therefore be observed on any platform that supports both Crimson and SISF.

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: A vulnerability in the Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) subsystem of Cisco IOS XE Software could allow an authenticated, remote attacker to cause a denial of service (DoS) condition on an affected device. This vulnerability is due to improper error handling when parsing a specific SNMP request. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a specific SNMP request to an affected device. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to cause the device to reload unexpectedly, resulting in a DoS condition. This vulnerability affects SNMP versions 1, 2c, and 3. To exploit this vulnerability through SNMP v2c or earlier, the attacker must know a valid read-write or read-only SNMP community string for the affected system. To exploit this vulnerability through SNMP v3, the attacker must have valid SNMP user credentials for the affected system. Cisco has released software updates that address this vulnerability. There are no workarounds that address this vulnerability. However, there is a mitigation. This advisory is available at the following link: https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-snmpwred-x3MJyf5M The Cisco Product Security Incident Response Team (PSIRT) validates only the affected and fixed release information that is documented in this advisory. Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: Weak crypto algorithms including MD5, DES, and 3DES should not be used for SNMP v3 user configuration as these algorithms are insecure and do not provide adequate protection from modern threats. Instead, SHA, SHA-2, and AES should be used for authentication and privacy protocols respectively. Conditions: SNMP v3 user configured to use MD5 as the authentication protocol, or DES and 3DES as the privacy protocol. Workaround: Update the authentication protocol to SHA or SHA-2, and privacy protocol to AES respectively. If this is not possible, then the following configuration command is required for SNMP to continue to function with the weak algorithms upon an upgrade to IOS XE version 17.11.1: Device(config)#crypto engine compliance shield disable Note the above command will only take effect after a reboot. Cisco does NOT recommend this option as these weak cryptographic algorithms are insecure and do not provide adequate protection from modern threats and should only be used as a last resort. BUG headline: Paramiko SSH client, having password auth, fails to connect to IOS
Product - Series: Cisco 9800 Series Wireless Controllers,Cisco 8000 Series Routers,Cisco Embedded Services 3300 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 8200 Series Edge uCPE,Cisco Catalyst IE3400 Rugged Series,Cisco Integrated Services Virtual Router,Cisco Catalyst 8000V Edge Software,Cisco Catalyst 8300 Series Edge Platforms,Cisco Catalyst 9200 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9500 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst ESS9300 Embedded Series Switches,Cisco ASR 1000 Series Aggregation Services Routers,Cisco ASR 900 Series Aggregation Services Routers,Cisco Catalyst 8500L Series Edge Platforms,Cisco Catalyst 9800 Series Wireless Controllers,Cisco Catalyst IE9300 Rugged Series,Cisco cBR Series Converged Broadband Routers,Cisco Catalyst IE3400 Heavy Duty Series,Cisco Catalyst 9400 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst IE3200 Rugged Series,Cisco Catalyst 8200 Series Edge Platforms,Cisco Catalyst IE3300 Rugged Series,Cisco 4200 Series Integrated Services Routers,Cisco Catalyst 9500H Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst Cellular Gateways,Cisco Catalyst 8500 Series Edge Platforms,Cisco ESR6300 Embedded Series Routers,Cisco 4000 Series Integrated Services Routers,Cisco Catalyst 8300 Series Edge Universal CPE,Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series Switches,Cisco ASR 9000 Series Aggregation Services Routers,Cisco Catalyst 9600 Series Switches,Cisco 1000 Series Integrated Services Routers,Cisco Catalyst 3850 Series Switches,Cisco Cloud Services Router 1000V Series
Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: When connecting to an IOS device using the Paramiko SSH client, and the client is using the 'password' authentication method, the connection will fail due to no common supported authentication methods. The following error will be observed in syslogs on the IOS device: Jun 21 16:41:59.834 EDT: %SSH-3-SERVER_AUTH_METH_ERR: Server does not support/Configured with 'password' Authentication method Conditions: Paramiko SSH client is in use, and is configured for the "password" SSH authentication type. IOS device (SSH server) must be running a release that has the fix for CSCuz65461. Workaround: Use any other SSH client, such as OpenSSH. Further Problem Description: This issue is a side effect of the fix for CSCuz65461, exposed by the manner in which Paramiko negotiates its SSH sessions. A brief summary: - SSH client and server must agree upon a common authentication method. ("password", "publickey", etc) - Most SSH clients will open a connection by sending a request with an authentication method of "none". The server will ignore this and send back a list of the authentication methods it supports. - The client will then compare this against its supported methods, select one in common, and send a second request using that authentication method. - In contrast, the Paramiko SSH client sends its first request with the "password" authentication method. The IOS SSH server has not yet prepared its list of authentication methods, and so the request fails with a mismatch. The fix for this issue adjusts the IOS SSH server behavior to resolve this issue. The Paramiko SSH client is a Python SSH implementation which is often used in scripting and automation. A notable example of this is the Ansible automation engine, which uses Paramiko internally: accordingly, the Ansible engine may not be able to connect to a device running a release affected by this problem.

This vulnerability is due to insufficient input validation during processing of CIP packets. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a malformed CIP packet to an affected device. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to cause the affected device to unexpectedly reload, resulting in a DoS condition. Cisco has released software updates that address this vulnerability. There are no workarounds that address this vulnerability. This advisory is available at the following link: https://tools.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-iosxe-cip-dos-9rTbKLt9 The Cisco Product Security Incident Response Team (PSIRT) validates only the affected and fixed release information that is documented in this advisory. Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: A vulnerability in the diagnostic shell for Cisco IOS XE could allow an authenticated, local attacker to use certain diagnostic shell commands which can overwrite system files. These system files maybe be sensitive and should not be able to be overwritten by a user of the diagnostic shell. The vulnerability is due to lack of proper input validation for certain diagnostic shell commands. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by authenticating to the device, enter the diagnostic shell and provide crafted user intput to commands at the local diagnostic shell CLI. An exploit could allow the attacker to overwrite system files which should be restricted. This advisory is available at the following link: https://tools.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-20180207-ios Conditions: The diagnostic shell required valid credentials and is available via: * By default on the AUX port. * Using TELNET or SSH if the feature ''persistent telnet or ssh'' is enabled. * On the console if the break key is used. This gets the user to a diagnostic shell which offers a IOS like CLI called ''bshell''. Workaround: None. Further Problem Description: As of March 13th, 2017, all Cisco IOS XE software releases are affected by this vulnerability. For fix information, please review the "Known Fixed Releases". Open a support case with your support organization if you require additional assistance. PSIRT Evaluation: The Cisco PSIRT has assigned this bug the following CVSS version 3 score. Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: The Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) subsystem of Cisco IOS and IOS XE Software contains multiple vulnerabilities that could allow an authenticated, remote attacker to remotely execute code on an affected system or cause an affected system to reload. An attacker could exploit these vulnerabilities by sending a crafted SNMP packet to an affected system via IPv4 or IPv6. Only traffic directed to an affected system can be used to exploit these vulnerabilities. The vulnerabilities are due to a buffer overflow condition in the SNMP subsystem of the affected software. The vulnerabilities affect all versions of SNMP Versions 1, 2c, and 3. To exploit these vulnerabilities via SNMP Version 2c or earlier, the attacker must know the SNMP read-only community string for the affected system. To exploit these vulnerabilities via SNMP Version 3, the attacker must have user credentials for the affected system. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to execute arbitrary code and obtain full control of the affected system or cause the affected system to reload. Cisco will release software updates that address these vulnerabilities. There are workarounds that address these vulnerabilities. The advisory is available at the following link: https://tools.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-20170629-snmp Conditions: Devices running an affected version of Cisco IOS Software or Cisco IOS XE Software. Workaround: Administrators are advised to allow only trusted users to have SNMP access on an affected system. Administrators are also advised to monitor affected systems by using the show snmp host command in the CLI. In addition, administrators can mitigate these vulnerabilities by disabling the following MIBs on a device: ADSL-LINE-MIB ALPS-MIB CISCO-ADSL-DMT-LINE-MIB CISCO-BSTUN-MIB CISCO-MAC-AUTH-BYPASS-MIB CISCO-SLB-EXT-MIB CISCO-VOICE-DNIS-MIB CISCO-VOICE-NUMBER-EXPANSION-MIB TN3270E-RT-MIB To create or update a view entry and disable the affected MIBs, administrators can use the snmp-server view global configuration command, as shown in the following example: snmp-server view NO_BAD_SNMP iso included snmp-server view NO_BAD_SNMP internet included snmp-server view NO_BAD_SNMP snmpUsmMIB excluded snmp-server view NO_BAD_SNMP snmpVacmMIB excluded snmp-server view NO_BAD_SNMP snmpCommunityMIB excluded snmp-server view NO_BAD_SNMP ciscoMgmt.252 excluded snmp-server view NO_BAD_SNMP transmission.94 excluded snmp-server view NO_BAD_SNMP mib-2.34.9 excluded snmp-server view NO_BAD_SNMP ciscoMgmt.35 excluded snmp-server view NO_BAD_SNMP ciscoMgmt.95 excluded snmp-server view NO_BAD_SNMP ciscoMgmt.130 excluded snmp-server view NO_BAD_SNMP ciscoMgmt.219 excluded snmp-server view NO_BAD_SNMP ciscoMgmt.254 excluded snmp-server view NO_BAD_SNMP ciscoMabMIB excluded snmp-server view NO_BAD_SNMP ciscoExperiment.997 excluded To then apply this configuration to a community string, administrators can use the following command: snmp-server community mycomm view NO_BAD_SNMP RO For SNMP Version 3, administrators can use the following command: snmp-server group v3group auth read NO_BAD_SNMP write NO_BAD_SNMP Further Problem Description: Customer are advised to utilize the Cisco IOS Software Checker or Contact Cisco TAC to determine if fixed software has been released for an affected platform. Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: A vulnerability in the Secure Shell (SSH) server code of Cisco IOS Software and Cisco IOS XE Software could allow an authenticated, remote attacker to cause an affected device to reload. The vulnerability is due to an internal state not being represented correctly in the SSH state machine, which leads to an unexpected behavior. Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: BGP session will not come up with peer if an unrecognized or unsupported capability is received from the peer in the BGP OPEN. Message similar to the following might be observed: Aug 4 16:20:22.627: %BGP-3-NOTIFICATION: sent to neighbor 10.100.100.100 active 2/0 (open: unspecific subcode) 0 bytes Aug 4 16:20:22.627: %BGP-4-MSGDUMP: unsupported or mal-formatted message received from 10.100.100.100: Expected behavior is that the local device should ignore the unrecognized/unsupported capability and bring the session up with the known capabilities, but that does not occur. Conditions: Local device is an IOS or IOS-XE device running a release that has the changes introduced in CSCuz20869. Remote BGP peer sends a BGP OPEN which advertises a capability that is not recognized or not supported by the local device. Workaround: Identify the unsupported capability that is being advertised, and reconfigure the remote peer to suppress advertisement of this capability. The exact method to do so will vary based on the remote peer's platform, software version, etc; The unsupported capability can be identified by enabling "debug bgp ipv4 unicast in" on the local peer. For example the following debug messages tell us that the peer is sending as BGP capability 5 which is not supported by the local peer: *Sep 11 18:31:14.867: BGP: 10.128.129.134 active OPEN has CAPABILITY code: 5, length 6 *Sep 11 18:31:14.867: BGP: 10.128.129.134 active unrecognized capability code: 5 *Sep 11 18:31:14.867: BGP: 10.128.129.134 active malformed/un-supported OPEN capability *Sep 11 18:31:14.867: BGP: 10.128.129.134 active went from OpenSent to Closing *Sep 11 18:31:14.867: %BGP-3-NOTIFICATION: sent to neighbor 10.128.129.134 active 2/0 (open: unspecific subcode) 0 bytes Further Problem Description: This defect is unintended collateral caused by the fix of CSCuz20869. If a given release does not have the prior fix, then it is not impacted by this problem.

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: The Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) subsystem of Cisco IOS and IOS XE Software contains multiple vulnerabilities that could allow an authenticated, remote attacker to remotely execute code on an affected system or cause an affected system to reload. An attacker could exploit these vulnerabilities by sending a crafted SNMP packet to an affected system via IPv4 or IPv6. Only traffic directed to an affected system can be used to exploit these vulnerabilities. The vulnerabilities are due to a buffer overflow condition in the SNMP subsystem of the affected software. The vulnerabilities affect all versions of SNMP Versions 1, 2c, and 3. To exploit these vulnerabilities via SNMP Version 2c or earlier, the attacker must know the SNMP read-only community string for the affected system. To exploit these vulnerabilities via SNMP Version 3, the attacker must have user credentials for the affected system. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to execute arbitrary code and obtain full control of the affected system or cause the affected system to reload. Cisco will release software updates that address these vulnerabilities. There are workarounds that address these vulnerabilities. The advisory is available at the following link: https://tools.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-20170629-snmp Conditions: Devices running an affected version of Cisco IOS Software or Cisco IOS XE Software. Workaround: Administrators are advised to allow only trusted users to have SNMP access on an affected system.
