BUG headline: C9300 Rcv-Err counter keeps increasing on connected to other non-mgig devices
Product - Series: Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series Switches
Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: When a Catalyst 9300 multigigabit series switch (UN/UXW/etc) is connected to a 2960X via copper ethernet/RJ45, traffic is degraded and the frames received causes errors on the interface to increment. This can be seen via "show interface N controllers": Switch#:show interface Five1/0/48 controller FiveGigabitEthernet1/0/48 is up, line protocol is up MTU 1500 bytes, BW 1000000 Kbit/sec, DLY 10 usec, reliability 189/255, txload 1/255, rxload 1/255 Encapsulation ARPA, loopback not set Keepalive set (10 sec) Full-duplex, 1000Mb/s, media type is 100/1000/2.5G/5GBaseTX input flow-control is on, output flow-control is unsupported ARP type: ARPA, ARP Timeout 04:00:00 34107 input errors, 0 CRC, 0 frame, 0 overrun, 0 ignored 0 2048 to 4095 byte frames 0 2048 to 4095 byte frames 0 4096 to 8191 byte frames 0 4096 to 8191 byte frames 0 8192 to 16383 byte frames 0 8192 to 16383 byte frames 0 16384 to 32767 byte frame 0 16384 to 32767 byte frame 0 > 32768 byte frames 0 > 32768 byte frames 0 Late collision frames 34107 SymbolErr frames <<<<<<<<<<<<<<<< Conditions: The switch must be a Cisco Catalyst 9300 switch using multigigabit ports (front panel copper/RJ45 ports that are capable of negotiating at speeds greater than 1Gbps.) C9300-48UN, C9300-24UN, UXW. This issue can be seeing when connecting the mgig C9300 with other devices too (APs, Servers, firewalls, non-mgig equipment). This is not specific to C2960. HW Version 04/05 are impacted. This can be seen in "show inventory": Switch-9300#sh inv NAME: "c93xx Stack", DESCR: "c93xx Stack" PID: C9300-48UN , VID: V04 , SN: [omitted] Switch-9300#sh inv NAME: "c93xx Stack", DESCR: "c93xx Stack" PID: C9300-48UN , VID: V05 , SN: [omitted] Workaround: --Can hardcode the interfaces to 100/Full ("speed 100" and "duplex full"). --Use a different device on the other side. --Use fiber Further Problem Description: This is caused by an error in the way the switch interprets and processes the preamble of the frame when it is received. It has been found that the fix for this defect may not address all cases of failure. Please open a TAC SR for assistance in getting this fixed through a workaround as an EEM script.

BUG headline: Cat9300 - SNMP monitoring of Cisco TrustSec SXP connection
Product - Series: Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9400 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9600 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9200 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9500 Series Switches
Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: After upgrading to Cisco IOS XE versions 17.12.5 and 17.15.3, customers are experiencing an issue with SNMP monitoring of Cisco TrustSec SXP connections. Specifically: • The SNMP walk through the ciscoTrustSecSxpMIB (OID: 1.3.6.1.4.1.9.9.720) behaves as if it has only one table, preventing retrieval of specific SXP connection details. • Previously working versions (e.g., 17.12.4 and 17.15.2) allowed customers to retrieve the connection status of specific SXP peers via SNMP. Expected Behavior: In versions 17.12.4 and 17.15.2, customers could retrieve specific SXP connection details using an SNMP GET or SNMP Walk command. BUG headline: C9500X/9600X - Creating SVI breaks flooding of some multicast local network addresses (224.0.0.0/24)
Product - Series: Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9400 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9600 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9200 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9500 Series Switches
Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: A Catalyst 9500X or 9600X-SUP-2 does not flood local network control multicast packets in the address range of 224.0.0.0 - 224.0.0.255 to a local VLAN. These packets are not normally routed. But they should be flooded into the same broadcast domain / VLAN on which they are recieved. Conditions: An SVI must be configured for the affected VLAN to hit this issue. If there is no "interface VLAN", then, this issue will not be hit An IP address is not required - the issue will be hit regardless PIM configuration is not required - the issue will be hit regardless Workaround: Have no SVI Further Problem Description: These packets are sent to the system CPU. At present they are dropped after being sent to the CPU and processed for any features that might require a protocol in this address range. Other addresses in this range will simply be dropped. A fix for this defect will still require the CPU to generate a copy to be sent/injected into the broadcast domain to allow flooding of these packets. Packet loss will be observed if the amount of traffic entering the system for these types of packets is greater than 2000PPS over a longer average or greater than a 11000 PPS burst, due to the default system policer. Cisco is still investigating a further enhancment to allow this traffic to be flooded in hardware to mitigate problems the CPU policer may cause in network environments where traffic exceeds the CPU policer limitations.

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: ++ Stale FNF exports observed on collectors like stealth watch. ++ From the output of #show platform software fed switch active fnf flow-table asic <> st-index 0 num-flows <>, we can see ETA deleting the flow but AVC being unable to. From lab output : C9300STACK#$fnf flow-table asic 1 start-index 0 num-flows 1000 Flow Table for Asic 1 idx start 0 end 10: num_flows_per_asic 66048 ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Srch Copy Stop Delt Tcp Idx LUT Vld done Owner ToCpu Copy Reqed Flg AppId fields ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 34287 1 1 1 3 1 0 2 0 0 {229, 0x1} {230, 0x2} {221, 0x0} {22, 0x026} {325, 0x6A4F} {324, 0x050} {284, 0x6} {297, 0x1010102} {300, 0xDDD14} Conditions: ETA and AVC is configured Workaround: There is no known workaround at this time. Even after reload, the stale flows re-appear. Further Problem Description: As per baseline software, ETA claims flows for ETA and AVC. If for some reason, AVC is not aware of the flow, at the time of clearing the flows, ETA is able to clear it, but AVC is not. This can result in stale FNF exports to flow collectors like stealth watch, thereby over-utilising stealth watch resources. To avoid this, an enhancement is made to software to allow ETA claim the flow only for ETA. This defect is to track this enhancement. It still needs to be investigated as to why AVC remains unaware of such flows.

BUG headline: Interface Speed Mismatch occurs after ISSU/SSO, due to QSA link swap with 40G/100G link

As part of ISSU functionality, the existing standby device will reload into the new software version first. Once it is up again the active switch will reload into the new software. At this point the previous standby becomes active and this is where the the speed mismatch occurs. The standby -> active transition results in the new active retraining the media type of a previously inserted optic. The interface will be up and operating at the inserted optic rate but the media type will be that of the previous optic. Observed log: 000483: *Jul 12 21:21:19.401 CEST: %ETC-5-CANNOT_BUNDLE2: Hu1/0/17 is not compatible with Hu2/0/17 and will be suspended (speed of Hu1/0/17 is 40G, Hu2/0/17 is 10G) Example of affected interface: Device#sh int hu2/0/17 HundredGigE2/0/17 is up, line protocol is up (connected) Hardware is Hundred Gigabit Ethernet, address is 7872.5d1b.8131 (bia 7872.5d1b.8131) Description: Test MTU 1500 bytes, BW 40000000 Kbit/sec, DLY 10 usec, reliability 255/255, txload 1/255, rxload 1/255 Encapsulation ARPA, loopback not set Keepalive set (10 sec) Full-duplex, 40Gb/s, link type is force-up, media type is CVR QSFP SFP10G(SFP-10GBase-LR) <<<<<<<< showing as 10g Conditions: Optic speed change such as replacing a 10g optic with a 40g optic. This must occur prior to an ISSU and without a reload being performed between the optic change and the ISSU. The traps are generated under normal operating conditions as MAC addresses are learned (and aged out) on the port-channels. The frequency and number of traps varies depending on the number and frequency of MAC addresses learned and the aging time (default is 5 minutes). The traps are triggered as MACs age out on the port-channel member ports not receiving traffic from those hosts/MAC addresses.

Conditions: A Catalyst 9600 switch will generate no core file, no system report, and will not generate any logs indicating why it is going down. The only symptom seen is a reset reason of: CpuCatastrophicError within the 'show version' output. Workaround: None. Further Problem Description: Note - The vast majority of switches that experience this issue will see an unexpected reload only once, and are expected to remain stable after the event. The recommendation if seen is to continue to monitor the switch for stability as if it were a parity error. This defect provides a hardening mechanism designed to help prevent the unexpected reloads in the first place for this specific reset reason. If your switch creates a crash file, system-report or any other log file during an unexpected, it is not experiencing this issue and should be investigated separately. This fix provides additional hardening to what was done on CSCvy15243. Customers are encouraged to upgrade past both this fix and CSCvy15243. Additionally, this defect addresses the hardening fix specific for the 9600 platform. For 9300, 9500, and 9500H, these platform specific fixes have been addressed via CSCvr77861.

BUG headline: L3 ECMP load balancing not working as expected for fragmented packets
Product - Series: Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9400 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9600 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9200 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9500 Series Switches
Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: Fragments of the same packet might be hashed differently depending on the tuple. By default we use the following parameters for load-balancing: src ip, dest ip, source port, dest port and L4 protocol. When the packet is fragmented the 5-tuples are being used for the hash of the 1st fragment only, however, in rest of the fragment since the IP header remains same (next protocol: UDP) the payload is being treated/decoded as UDP header and so it uses garbage value as L4 ports in computing hash which is causing the hash calculation to give them a different path. This can happen with packets generated by the switch or with routed packets passing through the switch. Conditions: This was observed on a L3 ECMP dual ISP scenario. Specifically for fragmented EAP-TLS radius packets, ECMP hashes the fragments differently causing the fragments to reach the remote ISE server out of order and the authentication to timeout. Workaround: A static route with ip sla tracking can be used to force the affected traffic through one of the links OR Change the CEF load-balancing algorithm to "original". The original algorithm takes the src/dst ip and the IP protocol into the hash computation. ignoring the L4 headers giving the fragments of the same packets the same path Further Problem Description:

BUG headline: Unkown Unicast block bit set to 1 when switchport block unicast is not applied

Conditions: + Create a smart ports macro which includes the command "switchport block unicast" + Apply the macro manually to a port. + Confirm the command "show platform pm port-data hun x/y/z | inc Unknown Unicast Blocked" shows both bits set to 1 and 1 as expected. + Set the interface to default with "default interface hun x/y/z" + See the output shows the Unknown Unicast Blocked bit operational value still set to 1 when the administrative value is back to 0. SWITCH#$port-data Twe1/0/1 | inc Unknown Unicast Blocked Unknown Unicast Blocked 0 1 SWITCH# + Apply another config to the interface. + This new config no longer has the command "switchport block unicast" + The bit is still set to 1 even with the new config. SWITCH#$port-data Twe1/0/1 | inc Unknown Unicast Blocked Unknown Unicast Blocked 0 1 SWITCH# Workaround: + To avoid the issue: + Apply a "shutdown" and "no shutdown" to the interface once you do a "default interface Hun x/y/z" and then proceed to add the new configuration. + To fix the issue: + Apply "switchport block unicast" and "no switchport block unicast" to the affected port. It will not clear the bit set to 1 but will allow Unkown Unicast flooding to work on that port. + Or toggle the interface L2/L3 mode, with "no switchport" and "switchport" commands. + Or Apply a "shutdown" and "no shutdown" to the interface. Further Problem Description: + Unknown unicast flooding issue seen on 16.12.3 and 16.12.3a + 16.12.5a and 17.3.3 show the same behavior of the Unknown Unicast Blocked bit seen as 1 but the issue is not seen. + Recommendation is to bounce the interface (shut/no shut) when applying macros (even if the interface was set to default).

BUG headline: QPolicer credit calculation algorithm adjustment to be more lenient to short bursts/spikes

Release Note Enclosure:
Symptom: This issue is specific to Cat9500 High Performance and Cat9600 switches that are configured with egress QoS policy that has Priority Queue configured with policer and is operating in Shared mode. This issue is only seen if there is bursty traffic going out through such a priority queue and spikes in the traffic rate are above the configured rate-limiting value. The symptom of this issue is that the average interface rate is well below the configured rate-limiting value for the priority queue, but there are Total Output Drops incrementing continuously on such an interface. These drops are seen under the QpolicerDrop column in the output of the show platform hardware fed [switch] qos queue stats interface command. The application performance is suffering due to a portion of the traffic stream being dropped by the switch. Applications that implement proper packet pacing [and thus generate rather flat traffic profile as opposed to bursty traffic pattern] do not exhibit such a problem. This issue cannot be confirmed by looking at the CLI outputs alone. Detailed analysis of the problematic data steam is needed. SPAN capture of the incoming traffic [that is enqueued in either PQ1 or PQ2 in Shared mode on the egress interface where drops are seen] is needed. I/O graph needs to be reviewed at 100ms/10ms/1ms granularity to see if there are spikes/bursts in traffic above the configured rate-limiting value. BUG headline: Cat9500: CISCO-ENTITY-SENSOR-MIB is returning wrong threshold values for thermal sensors
Product - Series: Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9400 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9600 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9200 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9500 Series Switches
Release Note Enclosure:
Symptom: When polling CISCO-ENTITY-SENSOR-MIB on Catalyst 9500 switch, the returned values cause a logical error when using the reference algorithm expressed in pseudocode 

        ...
        if (entSensorStatus == ok) then
            if (evaluate(entSensorValue, entSensorThresholdRelation, 
                entSensorThresholdValue))
            then
                if (entSensorThresholdNotificationEnable == true))
                then
                    raise_alarm(sensor's entPhysicalIndex);
                endif
            endif
        endif
        ...
There are 4 Thresholds (entSensorThresholdValue) and their corresponding logical comparison operators (entSensorThresholdRelation) against which the actual value (entSensorValue) will be evaluated. 

CISCO-ENTITY-SENSOR-MIB::entSensorValue.1014 = INTEGER: 29

CISCO-ENTITY-SENSOR-MIB::entSensorThresholdRelation.1014.1 = INTEGER: greaterOrEqual(4)
CISCO-ENTITY-SENSOR-MIB::entSensorThresholdRelation.1014.2 = INTEGER: greaterOrEqual(4)
CISCO-ENTITY-SENSOR-MIB::entSensorThresholdRelation.1014.3 = INTEGER: lessOrEqual(2)
CISCO-ENTITY-SENSOR-MIB::entSensorThresholdRelation.1014.4 = INTEGER: lessOrEqual(2)

CISCO-ENTITY-SENSOR-MIB::entSensorThresholdValue.1014.1 = INTEGER: 125
CISCO-ENTITY-SENSOR-MIB::entSensorThresholdValue.1014.2 = INTEGER: 105
CISCO-ENTITY-SENSOR-MIB::entSensorThresholdValue.1014.3 = INTEGER: 105
CISCO-ENTITY-SENSOR-MIB::entSensorThresholdValue.1014.4 = INTEGER: -10
applying the logic from the 1st row of entSensorThresholdRelation we get 29 >= 125 ==> FALSE ==> no alarm triggered applying the logic from the 2nd row of entSensorThresholdRelation we get 29 >= 105 ==> FALSE ==> no alarm triggered applying the logic from the 3rd row of entSensorThresholdRelation we get 29 <= 105 ==> TRUE ===> alarm triggered even though the the device operates well within acceptable environmental conditions applying the logic from the 4th row of entSensorThresholdRelation we get 29 <= -10 ==> FALSE ==> no alarm triggered When the NMS system is poling this MIB and using the reference algorithm to evaluate the received values, it will generate alerts that are false positives Conditions: - Cat9500 switch - NMS station polling CISCO-ENTITY-SENSOR-MIB - NMS station using reference algorithm for evaluating returned value to trigger an alarm Workaround: none apart from not monitoring CISCO-ENTITY-SENSOR-MIB and using the reference evaluation algorithm Further Problem Description: These are false positives due to returned values causing incorrect evaluation of the values

BUG headline: Flexible Template MultiD: MPLS global routes not displayed in TCAM cli
Product - Series: Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9400 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9600 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9200 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9500 Series Switches
Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: A part ipv4 or ipv6 routes in scale scenarios(for scale higher that 32000) will not get installed in hardware Traffic for those prefixes will be dropped. Conditions: This issue is seen when mpls is enabled on the system along with high ipv4 or ipv6 route scale ( global). There are active mpls interfaces. mpls labels get allocated for all global ipv4 prefixes. Workaround: we can limit the label allocation of mpls for global prefixes using prefix lists and global label allocation filter mpls ldp label allocate global prefix-list mpls_list ip prefix-list mpls_list permit Further Problem Description: Every prefix learnt ( ipv4 ) in the global table gets a label allocated to it. Since mpls and ipv4/v6 use the same hash table 2 entries are consumed for every single prefix. This means we cannot scale L3 routes to the prescribed limit but only half of it.

BUG headline: C9200/C9200L (17.3/17.6) - Output queue overloaded due to incorrect QoS programming.

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: C9200/C9200L switchports may run out of queue buffers causing all outgoing packets on specific interfaces to be dropped. Conditions: Conditions to trigger this software defect: - Specific to C9200 and C9200L switches with hardware version "V02" and "V03" (CLI - "show switch" or "show module" provides this version details). - QoS policy configured on interfaces operating at 10 Mbps or 100 Mbps. - Running one of these IOS-XE software version of 17.3.1, 17.3.2, 17.3.3, 17.3.4, 17.4.1, 17.5.1, 17.6.1 (Please refer to the defect - CSCvz54607 if similar issue is encountered in IOS-XE versions ? 16.12.5, 16.12.5b, 16.12.6). - CLI output of "show platform hardware fed switch <> qos queue config interface <>", show "port weight" as "2560" and "port shaping_step" as "256". - CLI output of "show platform hardware fed switch <> qos queue stats interface <>", show incrementing Hardware Drop Counters in "Drop-THx" - The following log message may occur indicating this condition: %FED_QOS_ERRMSG-3-QUEUE_SCHEDULER_HW_ERROR: Switch 7 R0/0: fed: Failed to configure queue scheduler for GigabitEthernet7/0/6: code 1. This log message does not always appear when the issue is present. Workaround: Remove the QoS policy on interfaces operating at 10Mbps or 100Mbps and reload the system. The same can be used to recover from the issue. Further Problem Description: - Without the QoS policy configured on interfaces operating at 10Mbps or 100Mpbs, the issue will not be triggered. - Once the issue has triggered, following symptoms related to outgoing traffic on the port (but not limited to) may be experienced : - Connected end devices will not get IP address and will not be get a voice vlan. - ARP and ping from the switch to the connected end devices having static IP addresses would fail. - Upgrade to IOS-XE version 17.3.4b resolves this issue.

BUG headline: Cat9300: CISCO-ENTITY-SENSOR-MIB is returning wrong threshold values for thermal sensors
Product - Series: Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9400 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9600 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9200 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9500 Series Switches
Release Note Enclosure:
Symptom: When polling CISCO-ENTITY-SENSOR-MIB on Catalyst 9300 switch, the returned values cause a logical error when using the reference algorithm expressed in pseudocode 

        ...
        if (entSensorStatus == ok) then
            if (evaluate(entSensorValue, entSensorThresholdRelation, 
                entSensorThresholdValue))
            then
                if (entSensorThresholdNotificationEnable == true))
                then
                    raise_alarm(sensor's entPhysicalIndex);
                endif
            endif
        endif
        ...
There are 4 Thresholds (entSensorThresholdValue) and their corresponding logical comparison operators (entSensorThresholdRelation) against which the actual value (entSensorValue) will be evaluated. 

CISCO-ENTITY-SENSOR-MIB::entSensorValue.1011 = INTEGER: 27

CISCO-ENTITY-SENSOR-MIB::entSensorThresholdRelation.1011.1 = INTEGER: greaterOrEqual(4)
CISCO-ENTITY-SENSOR-MIB::entSensorThresholdRelation.1011.2 = INTEGER: greaterOrEqual(4)
CISCO-ENTITY-SENSOR-MIB::entSensorThresholdRelation.1011.3 = INTEGER: lessOrEqual(2)
CISCO-ENTITY-SENSOR-MIB::entSensorThresholdRelation.1011.4 = INTEGER: lessOrEqual(2)

CISCO-ENTITY-SENSOR-MIB::entSensorThresholdValue.1011.1 = INTEGER: 125
CISCO-ENTITY-SENSOR-MIB::entSensorThresholdValue.1011.2 = INTEGER: 105
CISCO-ENTITY-SENSOR-MIB::entSensorThresholdValue.1011.3 = INTEGER: 105
CISCO-ENTITY-SENSOR-MIB::entSensorThresholdValue.1011.4 = INTEGER: -5
applying the logic from the 1st row of entSensorThresholdRelation we get 27 >= 125 ==> FALSE ==> no alarm triggered applying the logic from the 2nd row of entSensorThresholdRelation we get 27 >= 105 ==> FALSE ==> no alarm triggered applying the logic from the 3rd row of entSensorThresholdRelation we get 27 <= 105 ==> TRUE ===> alarm triggered even though the the device operates well within acceptable environmental conditions applying the logic from the 4th row of entSensorThresholdRelation we get 27 <= -5 ===> FALSE ==> no alarm triggered When the NMS system is poling this MIB and using the reference algorithm to evaluate the received values, it will generate alerts that are false positives Conditions: - Cat9300 switch - NMS station polling CISCO-ENTITY-SENSOR-MIB - NMS station using reference algorithm for evaluating returned value to trigger an alarm Workaround: none apart from not monitoring CISCO-ENTITY-SENSOR-MIB and using the reference evaluation algorithm Further Problem Description: These are false positives due to returned values causing incorrect evaluation of the values

BUG headline: Multicast-boundary filter-autorp not blocking RP announce in outbound that is denied in applied ACL.
Product - Series: Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9400 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9600 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9200 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9500 Series Switches
Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: Based on analysis, following filter ?ip multicast boundary multicast_boundary filter-autorp? applied on the Mcast boundary interface is blocking all the RP advertisement for the groups which are not explicitly defined within the filter list only the Outbound direction and processing all the inbound RP announcements on the boundary interface originated from the outside scope. ++ As per the logic it should be filtering RP advertisement in both directions.Based on the below document, If we configure the filter-autorp keyword, the user-defined boundary also examines Auto-RP discovery & announcement messages and removes any Auto-RP group range announcements from the Auto-RP packets that are denied by the boundary ACL. An Auto-RP group range announcement is permitted and passed by the boundary only if all addresses in the Auto-RP group range are permitted by the boundary ACL. If any address is not permitted, the entire group range is filtered and removed from the Auto-RP message before the Auto-RP message is forwarded. That’s being said, filter-autorp should be inspecting the contents of the RP-announce message and will filter based on the access-list added to it. https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/td/docs/ios-xml/ios/ipmulti/command/imc-xe-3se-5700-cr-book/imc-xe-3se-3850-cr-book_chapter_01.html Conditions: This issue is seen when we use Multicast boundary statement with autpo-rp keyword. The filter applied is only blocking the RP announcement from originated from local scope towards the outside scope ie., Inside ( LAN) towards the WAN(Outside). But it is processing the announcement in the other way around ie., from Outside to inside. Workaround: Apply the multicast-boundary filter on the inbound at the remote neighbor side. Further Problem Description:

BUG headline: Romvar: Bootloop if SWITCH_DISABLE_PASSWORD_RECOVERY and SWITCH_IGNORE_STARTUP_CFG are both set to 1

Release Note Enclosure:
Symptom: Device enters a bootloop crash with the following log:
UNIX-EXT-SIGNAL: Segmentation fault(11), Process = Net Background
Conditions: ROMMON variables: SWITCH_DISABLE_PASSWORD_RECOVERY - This variable can be set to 1 in case an admin wants to prevent a password recovery procedure SWITCH_IGNORE_STARTUP_CFG - Set value to 1, in order to ignore the startup configuration When both of these variables are set to 1, the device gets stuck on a bootloop crash. switch: set SWITCH_DISABLE_PASSWORD_RECOVERY=1 SWITCH_IGNORE_STARTUP_CFG=1

BUG headline: Port-channel members in stackwise Cat9k may fail to forward traffic out one or more member links
Product - Series: Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9400 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9600 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9200 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9500 Series Switches
Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: A catalyst 9000 series switch may fail to forward traffic out one or more port-channel members which are distributed across more than one chassis configured in stackwise virtual. Conditions: First seen on Catalyst 9600s running 17.6.x - Other SVL capable platforms and images may also be impacted. This impacts switches with larger scale - such as switches with 20 or 30+ Multi-chassis etherchannels (MECs) which are allowing several dozen, or even hundreds of vlans each. This issue can be triggered by large amount of link flaps of the port-channel members at this scale or higher (either physically or through a channel-protocol failure) where the switch needs to perform a large number of programming updates for these members and vlans. Workaround: A failover or reload of the chassis in question will allow a clearing and proper re-programming of the port-channel member. Further Problem Description: This is a rare issue that is not expected to be seen in most deployments and is specific to devices where large amounts of instability or programming updates take place. There is not an exact scale or number of changes which can trigger this, and instead the larger and more frequent the changes, the greater the chance that something can be missed. It also will not be seen every time there is instability and may not impact the member which was impacted by instability.

BUG headline: Interfaces stop forwarding traffic and not releasing QoS buffers
Product - Series: Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9400 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9600 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9200 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9500 Series Switches
Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: After a period of normal operation, interfaces connecting specific end-points stop forwarding traffic. Interfaces are in up/up state, but neither of interface counters change their values (like RX/TX bytes, drops etc.), no MAC learning happen. When in a broken state interface does not enqueue traffic in the queues and previously consumed buffers from shared pool never released. This is seen in the output of the following command: show platform hardware fed switch active qos queue stats interface , where "Enqueue" and "Drop" columns have values that don't change over time. "Buffer" column has a non-zero value that is stuck and never returns to 0 regardless of the current traffic load or interface status. Connecting different end-points, defaulting configuration, bouncing (by issuing shut/no shut command sequence) of interfaces doesn't change condition. Conditions: Issue is seen on Cat 9k IOS-XE 17.6.4, 17.6.5 versions. Affected ports are negotiated at 100 Mb/s. Flow-control should be enabled. Workaround: Reload the whole switch Further Problem Description:

BUG headline: Consistency Checker(CCK) detected inconsistency for l2m_vlan, Stale VLANs in FED
Product - Series: Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9400 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9600 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9200 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9500 Series Switches
Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: Error Message Seen: %FED_CCK_ERRMSG-4-INCONSISTENCY_FOUND: Chassis 1 F0/0: fed: Consistency Checker(CCK) detected inconsistency for l2m_vlan. Check 'show consistency run-id 455 detail'. "run-id" will change with time and vary system to system. Detail output shows STALE VLANs in FED: Switch#:show consistency run-id 455 detail Object-Type:l2m_vlan Start-time:2022/05/20 18:00:05 Status:Completed State:Inconsistent Key/data Reason (Ipv4, vlan: 1280) Stale snoop:off stp_tcn:off flood:off pimsn:off evpn:off (Ipv4, vlan: 2048) Stale snoop:off stp_tcn:off flood:off pimsn:off evpn:off Conditions: Create an L2 VLAN Associate an interface / port with that VLAN Delete the VLAN Workaround: There is no known operational problem due to this bug, so a workaround is provided only to circumvent the log message. The error message is seen as the switch runs a software consistency checker periodically. To stop the error message, configure a logging discriminator, or reload the switch after a VLAN is removed. Further Problem Description: This issue is due to a Stale entry existing in the FED (forwarding engine driver) software layer of IOS-XE. Starting in IOS-XE 17.9, a consistency checker runs on a regular basis to validate programming of various features across the system. When it runs, any inconsistencies detected are logged to the system log buffer. The presence of an inconsistency does not mean there is a certain operational issue with the switch. Analysis is needed for new inconsistencies detected. For this specific inconsistency, no immediate action is necessary UNLESS you see a further inconsistency after adding back a previously removed VLAN, or, if other unexpected behavior exists that correlates with this error message.

These changes are committed into: - IOSXE 16.12.6 and newer - IOSXE 17.3.1 and newer (including newer 17.x releases).

BUG headline: Cat9k with no SDG configuration routing mDNS traffic
Product - Series: Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9400 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9600 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9200 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9500 Series Switches
Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: If a Wireshark capture (using SPAN or EPC) is taken: - The source MAC of the mDNS multicast packet is rewritten with the BIA MAC address of the Cat9k that is incorrectly routing the traffic. - mDNS packets showing the same IP Identifier and TTL is decrementing. One single burst of 1000 packets from a mDNS source of traffic using a TTL 230 is causing ~1.5-2Gb of traffic replication. This could cause output drops on the physical interfaces. Multicast counters on the interfaces will increase drastically as a result of the multicast routing loop (i.e. mDNS packet with TTL 230 - the packet will loop until TTL expires). Conditions: - Cat9k with no Service Discovery Gateway (SDG) configuration in place. - This issue has been reported in 16.12.x and 17.3.x IOS-XE trains. - mDNS traffic is coming with an APIPA source IP address (169.254.x.x) Workaround: - Blocking mDNS on the SVI resolves the issue: ip access-list extended BLOCK-MDNS deny udp any host 224.0.0.251 eq 5353 permit ip any any If mDNS is in use, configure SDG feature on the Cat9k. Further Problem Description: This problem was successfully reproduced with the following setup: (mDNS source) -- VLAN900 -- Twex/x/x -- C9600_A -- (etherchannel) -- C9600_B 9600s are HSRP peers and PIM neighbors. A single burst of 1000 packets from a mDNS source of traffic using a TTL 230 is causing ~1.5-2Gb of traffic on both directions on the etherchannel between the 9600 switches.

BUG headline: Cat9k: Egress ACL on NAT outside interface matches IP header prior NAT translation
Product - Series: Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9400 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9600 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9200 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9500 Series Switches
Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: This issue was observed in situation where Cat9k have configured egress ACL on NAT outside interface. When processing packet, egress ACL is evaluating IP header prior translation. Therefore, if this ACL have entries denying inside local addresses, traffic will be dropped. With the egress ACL on NAT outside interface, ACL should evaluate IP header post translation instead. Therefore, you have to make sure that ACL is not matching inside local addresses. Example configuration could be seen below. In this case, OUTSIDE_ACL is matching inside local subnet 192.168.1.0/24 and therefore, traffic from this subnet will be dropped when egressing via Twe1/0/1. ip access-list extended NAT permit ip 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.255 any ip nat inside source list NAT interface Twe1/0/1 overload ip access-list extended OUTSIDE_ACL deny ip 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.255 any permit ip any any interface Twe1/0/1 ip nat outside ip access-group OUTSIDE_ACL out This behavior will impact only traffic forwarded via hardware path. Since ALG traffic is processed via software path, it will not be affected. Conditions: - Cat9k platform - egress ACL on NAT outside interface matching inside local addresses Workaround: - remove ACL or make sure that its not matching inside local addresses Further Problem Description: None. PSIRT Evaluation: The Cisco PSIRT has evaluated this issue and determined that it does not have a security impact that requires PSIRT ownership or involvement. This issue will be addressed via normal resolution channels. There is no PSIRT restriction that prohibits making this bug visible. BUG headline: Cat9k: Multicast routing disabled globally after removal of multicast routing from VRF
Product - Series: Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9400 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9600 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9200 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9500 Series Switches
Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: This issue was observed in deployment where Cat9k is part of MPLS network running mVPN services and acting as RP. In case that multicast routing is disabled in VRF via command "no ip multicast-routing vrf /name/", this issue will cause that multicast routing is disabled globally on device instead of particular VRF only. As result, this will cause that device will no longer punt multicast packets to CPU to trigger multicast control plane which may lead to outage for multicast stream. During the time of the issue, device will report that 0 packets been received from affected S,G entry despite the fact that device is receiving traffic and PIM tunnel interface will be set with A flag. This can be observed because multicast control plane is expecting to receive multicast traffic natively over S,G. For this, device have to punt initial packet to CPU to inform multicast control plane about S,G traffic. Due to this issue, packet will not be punted to CPU and therefore, multicast control plane will stuck in this state. C9K#sh ip mfib 239.1.1.1 (192.168.1.10,239.1.1.1) Flags: HW SW Forwarding: 0/0/0/0, Other: 0/0/0 HW Forwarding: 0/0/0/0, Other: 0/0/0 Tunnel1 Flags: A TwentyFiveGigE1/0/3 Flags: NS TwentyFiveGigE1/0/2 Flags: F NS Pkts: 0/0/0 Rate: 0 pps Same symptom could be observed also in case that there is problem with S,G tree along the path so it may not be so obvious if device is affected by this problem. Also, after removal of multicast routing, issue may not surface immediately since traffic flowing via established S,G tree will not be affected. However, new multicast sources may experience outage. Please note that if you will deconfigure VRF with enabled multicast routing, command "no ip multicast-routing vrf /name/" will be removed implicitly leading to this issue. To recover from this problem, you can disable/enable multicast routing for existing VRF on device. Conditions: - Cat9k platform with 17.9 train - removal of multicast routing for VRF - removal of data/default mdt for VRF Workaround: - disable/enable multicast routing for existing VRF or in global Further Problem Description:

BUG headline: Cat9k: NAT traffic is processed by CPU after device reload

BUG headline: Backout CSCwe51080 NETCONF sync failing due to vlan-list name exceeding model length expectations
Product - Series: Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9400 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9600 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9200 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9500 Series Switches
Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: This defect (CSCwn20712) tracks the backing out of the commits for CSCwe51080, whose changes resulted in the issues documented in CSCwi46941. The changes in CSCwi46941 address the issues in both CSCwe51080 and CSCwi46941. Conditions: N/A Workaround: When a VLAN is configured with more than 32 characters, the dmiauthd process will crash due to a constraint present in the model if the VTP version is not populated during initial sync-up. To resolve this issue, the VTP version was NVGEN'ed, which will populate the VTP version, satisfying the constraint mentioned above. This change was implemented via CSCwe51080. However, NVGEN'ing the VTP version resulted in issues with corruption of the vlan.dat file, and in certain scenarios, this would result in a loss of all VLANs, which would impact traffic. Defect CSCwi46941 was raised to address the "lost VLAN database" issue, and the code was changed to move the NVGEN part of the VTP version to another location, which addresses both CSCwe51080 and CSCwi46941. The changes to the code base via CSCwi46941 cannot be back-ported to 17.9 or 17.12 as the infrastructure needed to fix CSCwe51080 is not present in those throttles. The changes originally made by CSCwe51080 were later backed out by this defect CSCwn20712. This defect is simply to document the versioning where CSCwe51080 was back out. Further Problem Description:

BUG headline: Temporary AP Disruption Due to DTLS Download Failure on Cisco eWLC
Product - Series: Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9400 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9600 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9200 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9500 Series Switches
Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: Access Points (APs) briefly go offline and are temporarily unable to pass traffic, leading to a service-impacting issue. This is indicated by the error message %FMFP-3-OBJ_DWNLD_TO_DP_FAILED appearing in the logs. The APs do not reboot, and service typically restores automatically without manual intervention. Conditions: - This issue affects the Embedded Wireless LAN Controller (eWLC) functionality on Cisco Catalyst 9000 Series Switches (including Catalyst 9200, 9300, 9400, 9500, and 9600 Series Switches). - The problem is often triggered by specific scenarios such as AP session renewal or rejoin events. Workaround: None, as the system automatically recovers from the temporary disruption. Further Problem Description: The core issue stems from a synchronization problem during DTLS session cleanup. When an AP rejoins or renews its session, the Wireless LAN Controller (WLC) first programs the switch with a new session while removing the old one. If the WLC then attempts to send a delete request for the old session (which the switch has already removed), the switch cannot find it, resulting in a "Could not find session" error. This triggers the %FMFP-3-OBJ_DWNLD_TO_DP_FAILED message. This error is often benign, as the new AP session is already established and functional, and the traffic disruption is temporary. The problem is difficult to reproduce locally, suggesting a race condition.

AND 9500H#show consistency-checker run-id (run-id) detail Process: IOSD Process: FMAN-RP Process: FMAN-FP (Active) Process: FED (Active) Object-Type:l3m_entry Start-time:2023/02/22 15:18:43 Status:Completed State:Inconsistent <<<<<<<<< Key/data Reason (table_id:0x0, (*,239.1.1.1)) Hw inconsistency <<<<<<<< Entry Flags: C Total entries: 3 Obj_id/IfName: 0xf80004e1/L2LISP0 Obj_flags: F <<<<< Obj_id/IfName: 0xf8000461/Port-channel2 Obj_flags: A Obj_id/IfName: 0xf80004d1/L2LISP0 Obj_flags: F <<<<< Hardware Inconsistencies: HW_CHECK_TYPE:**rep-ri info** ErrorType :inconsistent Val :asic:0, ri(refcnt):0x16802(2), port_id:88() <<<<<< - 2 counted Exp Val:asic:0, ri(refcnt):0x16802(1), port_id:88() <<<<<< - 1 expected Where there is an additional entry for rep-ri info than expected by consistency checker. Conditions: As of today, this is only observed in the field when the following LISP configuration is used. But other scenarios and technologies (multicast, possibly) could see the same result in certain configurations. Have the following: Broadcast-underlay configured with LISP instance-ids using same multicast group on two or more instance-ids instance-id 100 service ethernet eid-table vlan 10 broadcast-underlay 239.1.1.1 <<<< database-mapping mac locator-set LAB-KL exit-service-ethernet ! exit-instance-id ! instance-id 101 service ethernet eid-table vlan 11 broadcast-underlay 239.1.1.1 database-mapping mac locator-set LAB-KL exit-service-ethernet 9500H#show ip mroute (*, 239.1.1.1), 00:31:46/stopped, RP 192.168.1.1, flags: SJC Incoming interface: Port-channel2, RPF nbr 10.2.3.2 Outgoing interface list: L2LISP0.100, Forward/Sparse-Dense, 00:31:46/00:01:43, flags: L2LISP0.101, Forward/Sparse-Dense, 00:31:46/00:01:43, flags: Must be a UADP 3.0 based switch for this defect to apply Must have "Exp Val" for (refcnt) to be 1 Must have "Val" for (refcnt) to be 2 Workaround: Issue is not operationally impacting beyond the log message. This only affects models with the UADP 3.0 forwarding ASIC. If you see similar symptoms on another switch model, this defect will not address the issue. If you see the same error message have rep-ri info discrepancies that do not align exactly to these conditions, this defect may not apply The error message indicates the automatic consistency checker has detected a possible inconsistency between software programming layers, or software and hardware programming. In this case, the detection is incorrect and there is no issue beyond the checker itself not handling this scenario properly. If a consistency checker failure is seen for something outside the specific list of symptoms in this defect, another issue may be hit and other defects should be reviewed or a case opened with Cisco TAC.

BUG headline: Catalyst 9000: Interface Total Output Drops Counter May Show Very Large False Values
Product - Series: Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9400 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9600 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 3850 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9200 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9500 Series Switches
Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: On some switch interfaces, the Total Output Drops counter may suddenly show an extremely large value (around 18,446,7xx,xxx,xxx,xxxx), even though there is no actual packet loss or performance impact. These values may also appear in other transmit-related counters, such as ?Collisions,? and then later return to zero or a normal-looking number without any change in traffic or configuration. Monitoring tools that rely on interface counters may raise false alarms when this occurs. The following sanitized command output illustrates the symptom: Device# show interfaces GigabitEthernet1/0/24 GigabitEthernet1/0/24 is up, line protocol is up (connected) Hardware is Gigabit Ethernet, address is xxxx.xxxx.xxxx (bia xxxx.xxxx.xxxx) MTU 9216 bytes, BW 100000 Kbit/sec, DLY 100 usec, ... Input queue: 0/375/0/0 (size/max/drops/flushes); Total output drops: 18446744073709xxxxx <--- Unusually large value Queueing strategy: fifo Output queue: 0/40 (size/max) 5 minute input rate 0 bits/sec, 0 packets/sec 5 minute output rate 0 bits/sec, 0 packets/sec ... In some cases, you may see similarly large values in other transmit counters, for example: Device# show controller ethernet-controller GigabitEthernet1/0/24 ... Excess Defer frames 30112 ... Collision fragments 0 ... LAST UPDATE 1409 msecs AGO (Values and interface names above are examples.) Conditions: - The issue appears randomly on multiple interfaces. - It can occur after clearing interface counters or after normal statistics updates from the hardware. - There is no corresponding increase in actual packet drops, and data-plane traffic continues to flow normally. There is no specific user configuration (such as QoS policies) required to trigger the problem; it is related to how certain internal drop and statistics counters (for example, queue drop statistics and ?Excess Deferred Frames?) were combined and displayed in the CLI. Workaround: There is no configuration change required to restore traffic flow, because this is a cosmetic CLI display issue only; forwarding is not affected. To temporarily clear the false counter values and reduce false alerts from monitoring tools, you can: 1. Clear interface counters on the affected interfaces: Device# clear counters interface GigabitEthernet1/0/24 2. Allow time for the counters to update; in many cases, the unrealistic values clear on their own as new statistics are collected. Limitations and notes: - Clearing counters only resets the displayed statistics; it does not change any underlying behavior in the software. The large values may reappear later until the software fix is applied. - Because the issue is cosmetic, you do not need to take any action for traffic forwarding. You should, however, tune monitoring or alerting rules to avoid treating these extremely large values as true congestion or packet loss events. Further Problem Description: The issue is cosmetic and does not affect packet forwarding, performance, or reliability. This defect is caused by how the device aggregates and reports two types of transmit statistics in the CLI: - Actual queue drop counters (for example, packets dropped by Active Queue Management [AQM] or egress QoS queues). - Interface-level ?Excess Deferred Frames? counters maintained by the Network Interface (NIF). In affected releases, updates from the hardware statistics path could incorrectly interact with the logic that tracks ?Total output drops.? Under certain conditions—especially after counters are cleared or when values wrap internally—this could cause the displayed Total Output Drops (and sometimes related fields) to jump to a very large 64-bit value (around 18,446,7xx,xxx,xxx,xxxx), even though there are no real drops.

BUG headline: ECN bits being included as part of ECMP hash on IPv6 TCP flows
Product - Series: Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9400 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9600 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 3850 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9200 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9500 Series Switches
Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: Users experience unexpected termination of TCP connections, particularly when ECN is negotiated and the destination is anycast. TCP Reset (RST) packets are received from the server side after the initial connection handshake, indicating that the receiving endpoint does not recognize an established connection. Different packets belonging to the same TCP flow, such as the initial SYN packet and subsequent data packets, are observed to take different network paths. Conditions: The problem specifically manifests with TCP connections operating over IPv6. Explicit Congestion Notification must be enabled on both the client and server, and successfully negotiated during the TCP handshake. This means that data packets will carry ECN bits (e.g., ECT(1)) after negotiation, while the initial SYN packet does not. The target service or host must be deployed using anycast. In an anycast setup, multiple servers share the same IP address, and traffic is routed to the "nearest" or "best" available endpoint. When different packets of a single flow are hashed to different paths due to ECN bit changes, they can end up at different anycast endpoints, leading to connection failure. Workaround: - Do not use ECMP Further Problem Description:

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: A Catalyst 9500X may fail to transmit packets with larger MTU after MACSEC is enabled on a a nearby port. Prior to enabling MACSEC all ports are able to transmit at link MTU, however after MACSEC is enabled some port with jumbo MTU are unable to transmit at even half the size of interface MTU. Example: hu1/0/5 has MACSEC while hu1/0/6 and hu1/0/7 do not have MACSEC. All ports inherit the system MTU of 9216. After hu1/0/5 is configured with MACSEC, the other 2 ports fail to transmit packets and can only forward at a much smaller MTU. OSPF flaps may be observed due to retry limit exceeded if an update packet is larger than the MTU that the interface can forward after MACSEC was enabled on neighboring port. Conditions: 9500X configured with MACSEC and nearby port without MACSEC. Issue has been seen on 17.10 and 17.11 Workaround: Remove MACSEC. Product - Series: Cisco Catalyst 9400 Supervisor Engine-1XL,Cisco Catalyst 9400X Supervisor Engine-2XL,Cisco Catalyst 9400 Supervisor Engine-1XL-Y,Cisco Catalyst 9800X Series Wireless Controllers,Cisco 9800 Series Wireless Controllers,Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9800 Series Wireless Controllers,Cisco Catalyst 9400 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9400 Supervisor Engine-1,Cisco Catalyst 9500H Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9400X Supervisor Engine-2,Cisco Catalyst 9500 Series Switches
Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: Clients using media streaming or multicast traffic, may stop receiving multicast frames This happens after a controller high availability switchover, and after a Broadcast Key rotation (GTK) Traffic resumes only after the affected clients re-authenticate to the wireless network. Error messages similar to the following may appear in the logs: [client-keymgmt]: MAC: 4c49.6c50.2927 Keymgmt: Failed to start client key rotation. Link encryption is False Conditions: -HA Stateful Switchover (SSO) event occurs -Broadcast Key rotation timer is reached (1 h by default) -Clients are actively receiving media-stream or multicast traffic at the time of or after the SSO Workaround: Modify the broadcast key rotation timer to be higher, for example 24 hours: wireless security dot1x group-key interval 86400 Then disable and enable back all WLANs, to force new timer application Further Problem Description: The issue is caused by a failure in the Group Temporal Key (GTK) rotation process following an SSO event. The key rotation mechanism does not properly reinitialize after the switchover, resulting in the "Link encryption is False" error. Unicast traffic is not affected; only broadcast and multicast traffic streams are impacted.

BUG headline: 802.11r Re-auth failed due to Invalid PMKID after roaming failure

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: Client won´t connect with reason invalid PMKID when trying to fast roam If keys are not flushed , client will report trying to connect multiple times to the AP with same failure code , until static re-config / intervention. Conditions: 802.11r Frequent inter-wncd roaming 9800 wlc, 17.9.3 Workaround: Delete previous keys / force client to go with full assoc process Further Problem Description: Client initiated FT roam by sending FT Auth Req on a certain wncd instance, wncd x. Controller sends FT Auth Response as expected. It is expected client sends Re-assoc for a successful FT roam. In this case, client sends an Assoc Req to another wncd instance, wncd y. Now a full auth is performed and new PMK shall be derived. Subsequent, roams from client is seen with the updated PMK in FT Auth. However, when client roams back to wncd x, updated PMK is not available in local PMK cache. Henceforth, we trigger a sync update of local PMK cache from global PMK DB which was solved. Initial suspect was on PMK sync between local and global DBs. After comparison checks of PMK name computation and derived from client, upon 11r IE revalidation, PMKID from client was picking up an incremented sequence of bytes and henceforth, Invalid PMK failure was observed.

BUG headline: OCSP Revocation Check on Full Certificate Chain
Product - Series: Cisco 8000 Series Routers,Cisco Embedded Services 3300 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 8200 Series Edge uCPE,Cisco Catalyst IE3400 Rugged Series,Cisco Integrated Services Virtual Router,Cisco Catalyst 8000V Edge Software,Cisco Catalyst 8300 Series Edge Platforms,Cisco Catalyst 9500 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst IR8100 Heavy Duty Series Routers,Cisco ASR 1000 Series Aggregation Services Routers,Cisco Catalyst 8500L Series Edge Platforms,Cisco Catalyst 9800 Series Wireless Controllers,Cisco Catalyst IE9300 Rugged Series,Cisco Catalyst IE3400 Heavy Duty Series,Cisco Catalyst 9400 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst IE3200 Rugged Series,Cisco Catalyst IR1100 Rugged Series Routers,Cisco Catalyst 8200 Series Edge Platforms,Cisco Catalyst IR8300 Rugged Series Router,Cisco Catalyst IE3300 Rugged Series,Cisco Catalyst ESS9300 Embedded Series Switch,Cisco Catalyst 8500 Series Edge Platforms,Cisco ESR6300 Embedded Series Routers,Cisco 4000 Series Integrated Services Routers,Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series Switches,Cisco Catalyst 9600 Series Switches,Cisco 1000 Series Integrated Services Routers
Release Note Enclosure: Refer to RFC 5280 Symptom: Debug entries in message log contain the following: CRYPTO_PKI: (A33D5) Certificate not validated %PKI-3-CERTIFICATE_INVALID: Certificate chain validation has failed.:Certificate chain validation has failed. CRYPTO_PKI: (A33D5) Certificate validation failed Conditions: IPsec is configured between IOS-XE and a peer device. The peer device can be another IOS-XE device or a strongSwan host. To perform an OCSP Revocation Check on the full certificate chain, it's understood that a Multi-CA Capable OCSP Responder is required. An example of this for OpenSSL can be found at: https://lightshipsec.com/multi-ca-capable-ocsp-responder-in-openssl/. When this multi-CA capable OCSP Responder is used and IOS-XE is configured with a root and subordinate trustpoints along with the 'chain-validation continue' command, IOS-XE will only perform the OCSP revocation check on the Intermediate CA certificate. If the 'chain-validation continue' command is removed from the subordinate trustpoint, IOS-XE will only perform the OCSP revocation check on the peer certificate. It never performs a revocation check on the full chain. Workaround: Further Problem Description: Conversely, IOS-XE will perform an OCSP Revocation Check on the full certificate chain when TLS is used with the multi-CA capable OCSP Responder. For example, as a TLS client to a remote Syslog server. This suggests there is a bug that prevents an OCSP Revocation Check from being performed on the full certificate chain when IPsec is used.

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: A vulnerability in the DHCP snooping feature of Cisco IOS XE Software could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause an affected device to reload unexpectedly, resulting in a denial of service (DoS) condition. This vulnerability is due to a crafted IPv4 DHCP request packet being mishandled when endpoint analytics are enabled. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted DHCP request through an affected device. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to cause the device to reload, resulting in a DoS condition. Note: The attack vector is listed as network because a DHCP relay anywhere on the network could allow exploits from networks other than the adjacent one. Cisco has released software updates that address this vulnerability. There are no workarounds that address this vulnerability. This advisory is available at the following link: https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-dhcp-dos-T3CXPO9z The Cisco Product Security Incident Response Team (PSIRT) validates only the affected and fixed release information that is documented in this advisory. Further Problem Description: Please refer to the Security Advisory. PSIRT Evaluation: The Cisco PSIRT has assigned this bug the following CVSS version 3 score. The Base CVSS score as of the time of evaluation is 8.6: https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/cvssCalculator.x?version=3.0&vector=CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:N/I:N/A:H CVE ID CVE-2024-20259 has been assigned to document this issue. Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: BGP routing for a specific Virtual Routing and Forwarding (VRF) instance may stop functioning unexpectedly. This occurs because the BGP address-family configuration is removed from the device's active running configuration (IOS DB), even though it remains present in the SD-WAN configuration database (Config DB). The discrepancy can be verified by comparing the output of show sdwan running-config (where the configuration exists) and show running-config (where it is missing). Sanitized Example: 1) The configuration is present in the SD-WAN database: Device# show sdwan running-config vrf definition [VRF_ID] rd 65xxx:10 ... router bgp 65xxx ... ! address-family ipv4 unicast vrf [VRF_ID] bgp router-id x.x.x.x distance bgp 20 200 20 maximum-paths eibgp 2 propagate-aspath propagate-community redistribute omp translate-rib-metric route-map ompToBgp exit-address-family 2) The configuration is missing from the active IOS running configuration: Device# show running-config vrf definition [VRF_ID] rd 65xxx:10 router bgp 65xxx ... ! ! <--- Missing: address-family ipv4 unicast vrf [VRF_ID] Conditions: This issue is observed on Cisco SD-WAN Edge devices under the following conditions: - A BGP address-family is configured within a service VPN template. - The VRF Route Distinguisher (RD) is subsequently modified. This modification typically occurs via a CLI Add-On template in the management controller or through direct CLI modification on the device. Workaround: Prevention: To prevent this issue, ensure that both the custom Route Distinguisher (RD) and the BGP VRF address-family are configured and deployed simultaneously within the same configuration change. Avoid modifying the RD independently after the initial deployment. Recovery: If the issue has already occurred, perform the following steps to restore connectivity: 1) Remove the BGP configuration section from the affected service VPN template in the management controller. 2) Deploy this updated configuration to the device (this clears the stale state). 3) Re-add the BGP configuration section back to the service VPN template. 4) Deploy the configuration again. This will push the complete and correct BGP VRF address-family configuration to the device. Further Problem Description:

Release Note Enclosure: IOS XE 17.15.1a in C1111-4P crash when EEM applet with CLI pattern for config mode executes Symptom: On Cisco ISR C1111-4P running Cisco IOS XE 17.15.1a, configuring and triggering an Embedded Event Manager (EEM) applet with a CLI event pattern matching entry into configuration mode (for example, event cli pattern "^[Cc][Oo][Nn][Ff].*" enter or event cli pattern "conf t|config terminal" enter causes the device to crash/reload. The crash occurs immediately upon entering configuration mode (conf t) when the EEM applet is present and enabled. Conditions: Platform: Cisco ISR C1111-4P Software version: Cisco IOS XE 17.15.1a Feature in use: Embedded Event Manager (EEM) EEM applet configuration: event cli pattern "^[Cc][Oo][Nn][Ff].*" enter or event cli pattern ?conf t|config terminal? enter Trigger: Entering configuration mode (configure terminal) This behavior is not observed in the following versions tested: Cisco IOS XE 17.3.x Cisco IOS XE 17.9.x Cisco IOS XE 17.15.4c This indicates a regression specific to 17.15.1a. Workaround: Disable or remove the affected EEM applet to prevent the crash. or Upgrade the device to Cisco IOS XE 17.15.4c or later fixed release Further Problem Description: This issue appears to be a software regression in Cisco IOS XE 17.15.1a, where EEM applets triggered by CLI entry into configuration mode (conf t) result in a system crash. The same EEM logic works as expected on earlier releases (17.3.x, 17.9.x) and on later maintenance release 17.15.4c, strongly suggesting a defect introduced in 17.15.1a and fixed in a subsequent 17.15.x release. The issue impacts device stability and can cause repeated reloads if the EEM applet remains configured.

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: A static IP/MAC binding can be removed from SISF configuration if the same IP/MAC is discovered on a different fabric-edge in an SDA deployment. This discovery may be dynamic (e.g. the presence of a host at another switch) or due to the configuration of the same IP/MAC binding on a second device. Conditions: This issue may be observed when a static binding on one FE is discovered on a second FE. Workaround: If the issue is triggered by the same IP/MAC binding being configured on multiple devices, this is a network misconfiguration that should be fixed. If it is triggered by dynamic host discovery then mitigation would depend on isolating the host that is duplicating a static binding's IP and MAC elsewhere and addressing the root cause of that. Further Problem Description: This issue exists in platform-independent code and may be observed on any platform that supports SISF. It is a day-1 issue that is present in all releases up to those where it is fixed; it is fixed in 17.12.6 and 17.15.1.

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: An IOS-XE device may unexpectedly reload shortly after startup (typically within the first few minutes of booting). The device crashes due to a segmentation fault in an internal process. After the reload, the last reload reason will display "Critical software exception" and reference a generated system-report file containing diagnostic information. Conditions: - The problem manifests during the configuration application phase immediately following a device reboot. - While initially observed on specific hardware platforms, the issue can potentially affect any IOS-XE device in similar deployment scenarios. Workaround: There is no known workaround to prevent this issue at this time. If you experience unexpected reloads matching this description, please open a service request with Cisco Technical Assistance Center (TAC) and provide the following information: - The complete "show tech-support" output from the affected device - The system-report file referenced in the reload reason (typically found in bootflash) Note: Collecting this diagnostic information will help Cisco TAC confirm whether your device is affected by this specific defect and provide appropriate guidance. Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: When this issue occurs, deployment of a Next-Generation Firewall (NGFW) policy (for example, a policy group push from Cisco SD-WAN Manager) fails. The device rejects the configuration because the generated access control list (ACL) reference name is longer than the supported length for the command. Policy group deployment fails with this error message: [9-May-2025 14:24:53 UTC] Failed to deploy device with Policy Group - PolicyGroup, Error: bad value: "acl-ngfwPolicyName_492025102358461_4-seq-ngfwRuleSequenceName-acl_" has a bad length/size. This is more likely when the policy name begins with a number and an additional prefix is added during name generation. Workaround: Use shorter names so the generated ACL reference stays within the supported length. 1) Shorten the NGFW rule sequence name and/or policy name in Cisco SD-WAN Manager. 2) Re-deploy the policy after reducing name length. sudo sed -i '1i/var/log/dnf.log\' /etc/logrotate.d/dnf
sudo sed -i '1i/var/log/dnf.rpm.log\' /etc/logrotate.d/dnf

event manager applet GUESTSHELL_LOGROTATE_FIXUP event syslog pattern "Guestshell is up at" maxrun 30 action 1.0 cli command "enable" action 1.1 wait 10 action 2.0 cli command "guestshell" pattern "guestshell@guestshell" action 2.1 wait 5 action 3.0 cli command "sudo mkdir /root" pattern "guestshell@guestshell" action 4.0 cli command "sudo cp /etc/logrotate.conf /home/guestshell/logrotate.conf.backup" pattern "guestshell@guestshell" action 4.1 cli command "sudo sed -i 's/rotate log files weekly/rotate log files daily/g' /etc/logrotate.conf" pattern "guestshell@guestshell" action 4.2 cli command "sudo sed -i 's/weekly/daily/g' /etc/logrotate.conf" pattern "guestshell@guestshell" action 4.3 cli command "sudo sed -i 's/keep 4 weeks worth of backlogs/keep 7 days worth of backlogs/g' /etc/logrotate.conf" pattern "guestshell@guestshell" action 4.4 cli command "sudo sed -i 's/rotate 4/rotate 7/g' /etc/logrotate.conf" pattern "guestshell@guestshell" action 4.5 cli command "sudo sed -i 's/#compress/compress/g' /etc/logrotate.conf" pattern "guestshell@guestshell" action 5.0 cli command "sudo cp /etc/logrotate.d/dnf /home/guestshell/dnf.backup" pattern "guestshell@guestshell" action 5.1 cli command "sudo sed -i '1i/var/log/dnf.librepo.log\' /etc/logrotate.d/dnf" pattern "guestshell@guestshell" action 5.2 cli command "sudo sed -i '1i/var/log/dnf.log\' /etc/logrotate.d/dnf" pattern "guestshell@guestshell" action 5.3 cli command "sudo sed -i '1i/var/log/dnf.rpm.log\' /etc/logrotate.d/dnf" pattern "guestshell@guestshell" action 5.4 cli command "sudo sed -i '1i/var/log/hawkey.log\' /etc/logrotate.d/dnf" pattern "guestshell@guestshell" action 5.5 cli command "sudo sed -i 's/\/var\/log\/hawkey.log {/{/g' /etc/logrotate.d/dnf" pattern "guestshell@guestshell" action 6.0 cli command "exit" action 7.0 syslog priority debugging msg "GUESTSHELL LOGROTATE FIXUP COMPLETED" ! Further Problem Description: /var/volatile is a TMPFS type of filesystem 

[guestshell@guestshell ~]$ mount -v | grep volatile
none on /var/volatile type tmpfs (rw,relatime,seclabel,uid=100000,gid=100000)
[guestshell@guestshell ~]$
Guestshell has 256MB of memory allocated by default This whole TMPFS has to fit into the 256MB of memory allocated for Guestshell, and if too much data is written into TMPFS, then cgroups will kill the container since the allocated memory is exceeded.

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: In some cases the NHRP shortcut cannot be build between spoke sites. Hub sends Traffic Indication to wrong spoke using incorrect MPLS label. Also spoke sends the Resolution Request with incorrect MPLS label. Only NHRP is affected - at the same time the real traffic works fine - ping spoke-hub-spoke works. Conditions: FlexVPN or DMVPN with MPLS It can happen if there are at least two sites (spoke and spoke or hub and spoke) advertises overlapping subnets in the same VRF. Examples: Hub itself has 10.0.x.x/16 in the lan in vrf XX SpokeA has 10.1.y.y/14 in the lan in vrf XX or SpokeC has 10.0.x.x/16 in the lan in vrf XX SpokeA has 10.1.y.y/14 in the lan in vrf XX Workaround: The overlap between sites needs to be removed. Further Problem Description: SpokeB pings 10.1.y.y in vrf XX. It is not matching the 10.0.x.x/16 network the Hub has. The hub tries to send Traffic Indication for return traffic to SpokeA - it should forward the Resolution request to 10.1.y.y over Virtual-Access2 with label 16, according to routing. But a wrong MPLS label is applied and the packet is dropped. At the same time the SpokeB receives Traffic Indication and sends Resolution Request to 10.1.y.y, but NHRP also gets incorrect MPLS label, and traffic is sent using incorrect label. The Traffic Indication from the Hub is always affected. The Resolution Request from the spoke is affected if hub advertises individual overlapping subnets to spokes. If hub sends a summary route the spokes should send Resolution Request fine, and hub will forward it using data plane as any other packet. The problem cause is NHRP asking MPLS for label for longest match on subnet, disregarding mask. NHRP should ask for longest match using host address.

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: Problem: If SCEP URL is specified with FQDN then PKI client does not fall back to IPv4 address when connectivity to DNS resolved IPv6 address fails. The following error can be seen: % Error: failed to open file. % Error in receiving Certificate Authority certificate: status = FAIL, cert length = 0 Conditions: SCEP enrolment URL defined as FQDN. DNS server resolves the FQDN both to IPv4 (A record) and IPv6 (AAAA record). There is at least one interface on the router configured with an IPv6 address. It can be in different VRF than source interface configured under the crypto pki trustpoint. There is no IPv6 reachability from the PKI trustpoint interface to the resolved IPv6 address of the PKI SCEP server. Workaround: Use IP address instead of FQDN for the SCEP server. Make the DNS server stop replying the AAAA requests. Further Problem Description: When resolving DNS name of a server, ip http client asks DNS system for resolution of destination server name top IPv6 A address first, with AAAA record by default. If IPv6 resolution fails, then IPv4 (A) is tried. If there is AAAA answer then ip http client uses IPv6 to connect. Currently the PKI does not do graceful fallback to IPv4, nor there is an option to configure IPv4 as the preferred protocol. The fix is that PKI checks if the source interface has IPv6 enabled. If not, then PKI resolves A name directly.

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: Virtual Access (VA) interface does not inherit IPv4 or IPv6 address from Virtual Template (VT) unnumbered interface. The connectivity over the tunnel is broken. VA with derived "tunnel mode ipsec ipv4" has IPv4 overlay protocol disabled. VA with derived "tunnel mode ipsec ipv6" has IPv6 overlay protocol disabled. Informational level log is seen upon VA creation: Apr 9 07:42:03: %TUNSS-6-PROTECTION_IPV4_IPV6_ADDR_DISABLE: Disabling IPv4 protocol The 'debug tunnel protection' debug shows: Apr 9 07:42:03: IPSEC-IFC IPSEC/Vi2(203.0.113.2/198.51.100.2): tunnel_protection_socket_up Apr 9 07:42:03: IPSEC-IFC IPSEC/Vi2: Tunnel is IPSec IPv4 - ipv6-overlay Apr 9 07:42:03: IPSEC-IFC IPSEC/Vi2: Disabling IPv4 address <<<< Conditions: VT configured with: "tunnel mode ipsec ipv4 or "tunnel mode ipsec ipv6" The VT referred tunnel protection ipsec profile has "set mixed-mode" configured. Example: interface Virtual-Template1 type tunnel description VPN connection to spoke ip unnumbered Loopback0 ip mtu 1400 ip tcp adjust-mss 1360 tunnel mode ipsec ipv4 <--- tunnel protection ipsec profile Cisco-LAB end crypto ipsec profile Cisco-LAB set transform-set Cisco-LAB set pfs groupxyz set mixed-mode <--- set ikev2-profile Cisco-LAB Workaround: Disable ipsec profile "set mixed-mode" option when the Virtual Template (VT) does not use mixed-mode - it has: "tunnel mode ipsec ipv4" or "tunnel mode ipsec ipv6" Configure ipsec profile with "set mixed-mode" only when the VT is configured for mixed mode, e.g.: interface Virtual-Template1 type tunnel description VPN connection to spoke ip unnumbered Loopback0 ip mtu 1400 ip tcp adjust-mss 1360 tunnel mode ipsec ipv4 v6-overlay OR tunnel mode ipsec ipv6 v4-overlay tunnel protection ipsec profile Cisco-LAB end Further Problem Description: The correct operation logic is: 1. `tunnel mode ipsec ipv4` -> disable IPv6 if present in VT configuration 2. `tunnel mode ipsec ipv6` -> disable IPv4 if present in VT configuration 3. `tunnel mode ipsec ipv4 v6-overlay` -> disable IPv4 if present in VT configuration 4. `tunnel mode ipsec ipv6 v4-overlay` -> disable IPv6 if present in VT configuration Due to the bug the 3/4 logic was applied to scenarios 1/2 incorrectly, based just on "set mixed-mode".

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: The scenario is that a secondary node has registered to the primary (using hello message), however it has not sent an update message (which has the load details), in the detail CLI we assume load details are always present and hence the crash. The is a very rare case in which this would happen, only when the CLI is executed in the time window that the client connects to primary (for the 1st time) and then load information is yet to be sent (load interval is 6 sec by default). Conditions: IKEv2 IPv6 Cluster Load balance This feature is applicable only to C8500-12X Workaround: Use the CLI after load information is shared. Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: This issue was seen in network running MPLS TE services with usage of OSPF protocol. Due to this issue, it may happen that after quick deletion and configuration of new sub interface with same IP address, for example via some automation script, previously generated opaque LSAs are not flushed from database. Therefore, we can see in OSPF database that there is multiple opaque LSAs holding duplicate IP address / neighbor information. In this situation, even if reconfigured interface is subsequently deleted, these old opaque LSAs will this stay in database and they are in even refreshed every 30 minutes by OSPF process. This is may cause problems for the routers calculating path used by TE tunnels. To recover from this state, e.q. flush these invalid opaque LSAs from database, we need to clear OSPF process. Conditions: MPLS network running TE and OSPF Workaround: Enough time should be given for the LSA to be deleted from network before configuring the same IP address. Further Problem Description:

It can also impact traffic if a device immediately starts sending/receiving traffic over a VPN tunnel. Conditions: It can happen when all the tunnels are coming up simultaneously after: 1. Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: Have router A configured with strict SID for prefix P. Have router B redistributing prefix P including strict SID into another SR capable protocol. Routers A and B are not neighbours. Change value of strict SID on router A or remove strict SID from the configuration. Strict SID value is not updated in destination protocol on router B.
