Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: IKEv1 or IKEv2 tunnel using pre-shared key is not getting established. Debugs indicate problem with pre-shared key mismatch. IKEv2: Failed to authenticate SA errors are seen IKEv1: %CRYPTO-4-IKMP_BAD_MESSAGE: IKE message from x.x.x.x failed its sanity check or is malformed The problem with router behaviour is that when it cannot decrypt the pre-shared key it is sending the encrypted form of pre-shared key to the peer. This is not correct - the router should abort the negotiation. Conditions: "password encryption aes" is configured, encrypted pre-shared keys are present in the configuration, e.g.: crypto ikev2 keyring CRYPTO peer ANY address 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 pre-shared-key 6 FcdG`K_gaK\EAVAUDORGHNIfLEQAAB AND the actual password encryption key is missing on the router. Why could it be missing? Because configuration was copy-pasted from backup, or another device, with encrypted pre-shared-keys, but the "key config-key password-encrypt " with correct password was not configured. How to know if password encryption key is missing? Configure a dummy pre-shared key and check if it gets encrypted. If encryption key is missing the following error is seen: crypto ikev2 keyring CRYPTO peer test address 203.0.113.1 pre-shared-key test-password >>Cannot encrypt password. Please configure a configuration-key with 'key config-key'<< Workaround: How to get out of missing encryption key situation: 1. If the old "key config-key password-encrypt" key is stored in documentation and available - reapply it: conf t key config-key password-encrypt The VPN should start working. 2. If the "key config-key password-encrypt" key is not known, then set a new one, document it, and re-apply all the pre-shared keys in clear text form, so that they get encrypted with the new encryption key. Further Problem Description: The problem is caused by missing password encryption key - configured with "key config-key password-encrypt ". This bug fix doesn't address why the password encryptio key is missing. Note - this configuration part is used to encrypt pre-shared-keys in running-config and IS NOT displayed in the running-config. There is no way to retrieve it from the router. When password encryption is used the pre-shared-keys are stored in configuration in encrypted form - e.g.: before encryption: pre-shared-key Example-password after encryption: pre-shared-key 6 FcdG`K_gaK\EAVAUDORGHNIfLEQAAB When router needs to use the pre-shared-key to establish VPN it decrypts it with the password encryption key - configured with "key config-key password-encrypt ", stored in secure storage and not visible in the running config. If the encryption key is missing, for whatever reason, the router cannot decrypt the pre-shared-key. This bug fix is changing behaviour - when router is not able to decrypt pre-shared-key: - before the fix - it is sending the encrypted form as pre-shared key - e.g. FcdG`K_gaK\EAVAUDORGHNIfLEQAAB in the above example. - after the fix - the router is aborting negotiation and showing in ISAKMP/IKEv2 debugs that it cannot decrypt the pre-shared-key. The signs that the password was configured, but is lost are: Passwords are saved as type 6, e.g.: crypto ikev2 keyring CRYPTO peer ANY address 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 pre-shared-key 6 FcdG`K_gaK\EAVAUDORGHNIfLEQAAB <-- note 6! AND router gives warning when trying to configure a new password: "configure terminal crypto ikev2 keyring TEST peer test address 203.0.113.1 pre-shared-key test-password Cannot encrypt password. Please configure a configuration-key with 'key config-key'" The new password is saved in configuration without " 6 " - as clear text password. The fix: if the router is unable to decrypt password the clear debug message is produced: IKEv1: 000194: *Sep 5 10:26:07.995 GMT-SUM: ISAKMP: (0):found peer pre-shared key matching x.x.x.x 000195: *Sep 5 10:26:07.995 GMT-SUM: ISAKMP: Failed to decrypt key IKEv2: 001898: *Sep 5 10:43:14.332 GMT-SUM: IKEv2:(SESSION ID = 1,SA ID = 2):Generate my authentication data 001899: *Sep 5 10:43:14.332 GMT-SUM: IKEv2-ERROR:(SESSION ID = 1,SA ID = 2):: No pskey found 001900: *Sep 5 10:43:14.332 GMT-SUM: IKEv2:(SESSION ID = 1,SA ID = 2):Auth exchange failed More about the password encryption: http://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/docs/security-vpn/ipsec-negotiation-ike-protocols/46420-pre-sh-keys-ios-rtr-cfg.html WARNING - There could be a situation where the configuration was restored from a backup, and password encryption key was not set. Someone not knowing how password encryption works could assume the encrypted form of pre-shared key is the pre-shared key itself and give it to the peer - and the VPN goes up. In such scenario the VPN works on misconfigured routers without the fix - the router is sending encrypted blob as pre-shared key, and the peer is configured to accept it. After the upgrade to a fixed version the VPN stops working, as the misconfigured router is aborting the negotiation.

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: A Catalyst switch can unexpectedly reload due to a critical software exception. The reload can be seen due to a segmentation fault on process SSF8472 From crashinfo file. "UNIX-EXT-SIGNAL: Segmentation fault(11), Process = SFF8472" SISF error logs seen prior to the reload: SISF_DB_IOS_ERR: sisf add or update record error (Not enough space) SISF_DB_IOS_ERR: TDL MAC xxxx.yyyy.zzzz differs from BT entry MAC xxxx.yyyy.zzzz SISF_DB_IOS_ERR: sisf delete record error (Invalid argument) SISF_DB_IOS_ERR: Unable to find IPv6 entry in mac xxxx.yyyy.zzzz for ip_key SISF_DB_IOS_ERR: Unable to unset binding entry for key and mac xxxx.yyyy.zzzz SISF_DB_IOS_ERR: Unable to find IP and zone in mac record xxxx.yyyy.zzzz SISF_DB_IOS_ERR: Unable to set up MAC's IP binding for xxxx.yyyy.zzzz SISF_DB_IOS_ERR: Unable to set binding entry for key and mac xxxx.yyyy.zzzz SISF_DB_IOS_ERR: MAC record update failed for mac xxxx.yyyy.zzzz address key SISF_DB_IOS_ERR: Unable to update binding from mac record - address is SISF_DB_IOS_ERR: Unable to add/update new binding for mac xxxx.yyyy.zzzz, address , SISF_DB_IOS_ERR: sisf add or update record error (Not enough space) Conditions: This issue may happen in mixed IPv4/IPv6 networks over a long period of time as a result of normal SISF operation. Note that this is triggered by the presence of IPv6 addresses in the network; no specific IPv6 configuration on the affected device is required. Workaround: A periodic reboot of the affected device will reset the memory usage. The "device-tracking tdl-disable" service-internal command may be used to disable the SISF Crimson DB entirely and avoid this issue; however, this means that no SISF data will be available via the Crimson DB to any consumer (e.g. DNAC). This command requires service-internal to remain enabled to persist through reloads. This workaround will prevent further memory leakage due to this issue, but will not recover any memory that has already been leaked; a reboot will do this. The "device-tracking tdl-disable" only disables publication of SISF data in the Crimson database; normal functionality and operation of SISF is not impacted by this. Further Problem Description: SISF database entries are published via the Crimson operational database. When an entry changes, the process to update the corresponding Crimson database entry involves a search to find it. SISF maintains a static IP address structure for use in IP database lookups, in order to reduce the overhead of these; it is used for both IPv4 and IPv6. When an IPv4 lookup follows an IPv6 one, the IPv6 address used for the previous search is leaked rather than being freed properly. Over time, these cumulative leaks will eventualy exhaust the Crimson IOS operational database, at which point this issue may be observed. This issue was introduced in a new feature in 17.2.1 and 16.12.3. It exists in all releases from there until the releases where it has been fixed; it is fixed in 16.12.8, 17.3.5, 17.6.3, 17.7.2, 17.8.1 and 17.9.1. It is in PI code and may therefore be observed on any platform that supports both Crimson and SISF. Note that CSCwb25610 is a very similar issue (it isn't possible to distinguish it from this one in the field as the symptoms are the same) but is fixed in a later set of releases.

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: Padding for IS-IS hellos is enabled by default. Currently hellos are padded to the link mtu (or configured "clns-mtu" if present). As per specification, hellos should be padded to the maximum of (link-mtu, lsp-mtu). This insures the link is capable of sending/receiving the maximum sized LSP that can be sent. Conditions: If lsp-mtu is greater than the link mtu of an interface on which IS-IS is enabled. Workaround: Ensure that the link mtu of all interfaces on which IS-IS is enabled is greater than or equal to the lsp-mtu. Further Problem Description: IS-IS protocol does not support fragmentation. It is therefore required that the link mtu of all interfaces in the network is greater than/equal to the largest LSP that might be sent by any node in the network. This REQUIRES consistent lsp-mtu configuration on all nodes in the network. Note that inconsistent configurations might not immediately demonstrate a problem. If a node does not have enough information to advertise to require multiple LSPs to be sent, it may be that the misconfigured network continues to work. But it may fail to propagate max-sized LSPs once a given node has enough information to advertise to exceed the configured lsp-mtu on at least one node in the network.

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: A vulnerability in the Link Layer Discovery Protocol (LLDP) message parser of Cisco IOS Software and Cisco IOS XE Software could allow an attacker to trigger a reload of an affected device, resulting in a denial of service (DoS) condition. This vulnerability is due to improper initialization of a buffer. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability via any of the following methods: * An authenticated, remote attacker could access the LLDP neighbor table via either the CLI or SNMP while the device is in a specific state. * An unauthenticated, adjacent attacker could corrupt the LLDP neighbor table by injecting specific LLDP frames into the network and then waiting for an administrator of the device or a network management system (NMS) managing the device to retrieve the LLDP neighbor table of the device via either the CLI or SNMP. * An authenticated, adjacent attacker with SNMP read-only credentials or low privileges on the device CLI could corrupt the LLDP neighbor table by injecting specific LLDP frames into the network and then accessing the LLDP neighbor table via either the CLI or SNMP. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to cause the affected device to crash, resulting in a reload of the device. Cisco has released software updates that address this vulnerability. There are no workarounds that address this vulnerability. This advisory is available at the following link: https://tools.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-lldp-dos-sBnuHSjT Conditions: For information on fixed versions of software consult the Cisco IOS Software checker: https://tools.cisco.com/security/center/softwarechecker.x See Vulnerable Products Section of the advisory for full details: https://tools.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-lldp-dos-sBnuHSjT#vp Workaround: There are no workarounds that address this vulnerability. Further Problem Description: Please refer to the Security Advisory. PSIRT Evaluation: The Cisco PSIRT has assigned this bug the following CVSS version 3 score. Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: If IS-IS LSP password/key is modified, updated LSPs with the new key will not be generated. Conditions: Plain text mode: new password has the same length as the old password. MD5 or key-chain mode: any key change after authentication is fully enabled. No other triggers for altering the content of an LSP have occurred (e.g., no adjacency up/down events or new prefix advertisements. Workaround: Trigger an LSP update by modifying a metric on an interface. Further Problem Description: Whenever an LSP is refreshed the new password/key will be used. But until that happens (or other event triggered LSP update occurs), if a new neighbor comes up, LSPs which are not updated due to the inclusion of the new neighbor will not be successfully synced if the new neighbor is already using the new password/key..

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: SR Label is removed from forwarding entry when one of the sources for the prefix advertisement is lost. This results in traffic loss to the affected destinations. If this is associated with a VPN prefix you may see the message: "unusable: no label". when examining the FIB. Conditions: Segment Routing is enabled for IS-IS. Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: BGP flap with short timer when peering with a device configured with default timers Conditions: BGP session flaps periodically. The period of every flap is determined by the lower hold time. Peers have mismatched hold times for the same session. For example, take the topology below: Switch <--(BGP)---> remote-peer UUT# *Jun 10 22:19:15.553: %BGP-5-ADJCHANGE: neighbor 10.0.*.* Up UUT#sh ip bgp neigh 10.0.*.* BGP neighbor is 10.0.*.*, remote AS **, external link BGP version 4, remote router ID 10.0.*.* BGP state = Established, up for 00:00:06 Last read 00:00:06, last write 00:00:00, hold time is 9, keepalive interval is 3 seconds. <<<<< HOLD TIME UUT IS USING IS NOT SUPPORTED Configured hold time is 9, keepalive interval is 3 seconds remote-peer#sh ip bgp neighbors 10.0.*.* *Jun 10 22:19:35.012: %BGP-5-ADJCHANGE: neighbor 10.0.0.* Up remote-peer#sh ip bgp neighbors 10.0.0.* BGP neighbor is 10.0.0.*, remote AS **, external link BGP version 4, remote router ID 10.0.0.* BGP state = Established, up for 00:00:02 Last read 00:00:02, last write 00:00:02, hold time is 180, keepalive interval is 60 seconds. <<<<< DEFAULT TIMERS ARE USED Last update received: 00:00:02 Workaround: Configure the same time value on both devices Further Problem Description: When a peer that supports Graceful Restart (for example, Cat 9300) is configured with a hold time that is lower than the minimum supported GR hold time, the Cat 9300 device will set the hold time to the default in the open message to the peer, but internally will keep using the configured lower hold time. The Cat 9300 device perceives the lower hold time to be the preferred but in the negotiation it actually sent a much bigger hold time of 180 seconds, causing the Cat 9300 to think the peer is unresponsive and send a hold time expire notification since even the keepalive of the peer (60 seconds) is much larger than the Cat 9300's hold time (9 seconds)

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: In case when SRMS server announces prefix range, which overlaps with SID-Prefix, whole SRMS range is ignored by device - prefix will be without label. Based on the RFC 8661, device should ignore only specific overlapping prefix. Example case is when we have announced SRMS range "10.10.10.0/32 500 range 10" and we have in network SID-Prefix 10.10.10.4/32, which overlaps with SRMS range. In this scenario will be example prefix 10.10.10.3/32 without label. In case that we will use non-overlapping range "10.10.10.0/32 500 range 4", prefix 10.10.10.3/32 will have label. In case of overlapping range, device should ignore only specific overlapping prefix. Conditions: Segment Routing is enabled. Segment Routing Mapping Server (SRMS) advertisement has a range which overlaps with SID-prefix Workaround: - Avoid using overlapping ranges - Advertise all SRMS ranges with size of 1 Further Problem Description:

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: Deletion of a VRF may remain in pending state indefinitely. Conditions: Redistribution of IS-IS operating in the default VRF into another protocol operating into a different VRF is attempted. This will fail. But if the redistribution config is (unnecessarily) removed and subsequently the vrf associated with the source protocol is deleted, the VRF will remain in pending delete state indefinitely. Workaround: Remove the IS-IS instance. Further Problem Description: Example config: 1) Configure an empty IS-IS instance: RTR1#conf t RTR1(config)#router isis 1 RTR1(config-router)#exit 2) Configure a VRF: RTR1(config)#vrf definition ONE RTR1(config-vrf)#address-family ipv4 RTR1(config-vrf-af)#exit RTR1(config-vrf)#exit 3) Try to redistribute IS-IS from a protocol in the created VRF. IS-IS correctly rejects the config: RTR1(config)#router ospf 1 vrf ONE RTR1(config-router)#redis RTR1(config-router)#redistribute isis 1 %VRF specified does not match this router RTR1(config-router)# 4) Unconfigure the redistribution configuration that was rejected. RTR1(config-router)#no redistribute isis 1 RTR1(config-router)# 5) Try to remove the VRF config. The VRF will be stuck in deleted state. RTR1(config)#no vrf definition ONE % IPv4 and IPv6 addresses from all interfaces in VRF ONE have been removed RTR1(config)#end RTR1#RTR1#show vrf Name Default RD Protocols Interfaces * ONE ipv4 * Being deleted

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: - "ip domain lookup nsap" is missing from RESTCONF running configuration after applying configuration that includes both nsap and table-map with default copy - DMI sync messages observed on console: "%DMI-5-SYNC_NEEDED", "%DMI-5-SYNC_START", "%DMI-5-SYNC_COMPLETE" - RESTCONF GET for /Cisco-IOS-XE-native:native/ip/domain returns empty response or missing nsap attribute - Configuration drift detected where nsap must be reapplied on every automation run - "show running-config all" may show nsap as a YANG default value, but it is not present in the actual running configuration or NETCONF datastore when issuing `show running | format restconf-json` Conditions: The bug is triggered when ALL of the following conditions are met: 1. Configuration includes "ip domain lookup nsap" 2. Configuration includes table-map with explicit "default copy" statement 3. The nsap configuration is present in the datastore when DMI sync is triggered by table-map with explicit default copy 4. Both configurations are applied in the same transaction (RESTCONF PATCH) or nsap is configured before table-map (CLI) The bug does NOT occur when: - Table-map is configured WITHOUT explicit "default copy" (relies on YANG default) - nsap is configured AFTER table-map and DMI sync have completed (CLI only) - Only one of the two features is configured Workaround: **Option 1 (Recommended):** Omit the explicit "default copy" statement from table-map configuration. The YANG model default value is "copy", so omitting the statement achieves identical configuration behavior without triggering DMI sync. Example working configuration: ``` table-map TABLE-MAP-1 map from 18 to 18 map from 10 to 10 ! (no "default copy" statement - relies on YANG default) ``` **Option 2:** Configure "ip domain lookup nsap" AFTER table-map configuration completes and DMI sync finishes. Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: When configuring logging via RESTCONF PUT operations with both `buffered` severity and `persistent` logging attributes, the buffered severity level fails to appear in subsequent RESTCONF GET responses, despite being visible in the device running configuration via CLI. Terraform and other automation tools report continuous configuration drift, failing idempotency tests. **Example CLI shows correct configuration:** ``` Switch#show running-config | include buffered logging buffered 16384 debugging ``` **But RESTCONF GET returns incomplete data:** ```json { "Cisco-IOS-XE-native:buffered-config": { "common-config": { "buffered": { "size-value": 16384 // severity-level missing } } } } ``` Conditions: This issue occurs when all of the following conditions are met: 1. IOS-XE version 17.15 is running on the device 2. A RESTCONF PUT operation is performed on the `/Cisco-IOS-XE-native:native/logging` endpoint 3. The PUT payload includes both: - `buffered-config/common-config/buffered/severity-level` attribute - `persistent` logging attributes (`persistent/url`, `persistent/size`, and/or `persistent/filesize`) The issue does **not** occur when: - Using RESTCONF PUT without `persistent` attributes (all other logging attributes work correctly) - Using RESTCONF PATCH operations on `/logging/buffered-config` endpoint - Configuring via CLI (CLI configuration syncs to RESTCONF correctly) Workaround: **Option 1 - Two-step RESTCONF approach:** 1. Perform initial PUT without the `persistent` attributes 2. Follow with a PATCH operation to add `persistent` attributes separately ```bash # Step 1: PUT logging config without persistent curl -k -u 'admin:password' -X PUT \ -H 'Content-Type: application/yang-data+json' \ -d '{"Cisco-IOS-XE-native:logging":{"buffered-config":{"common-config":{"buffered":{"size-value":16384,"severity-level":"debugging"}}},"persistent":{"url":"bootflash:/logs","size":1500000,"filesize":750000}}}' \ 'https://device-ip/restconf/data/Cisco-IOS-XE-native:native/logging' # Step 2: Verify with GET curl -k -u 'admin:password' \ 'https://device-ip/restconf/data/Cisco-IOS-XE-native:native/logging/buffered-config' ``` **Option 2 - Use CLI configuration instead:** Configure logging via CLI, which correctly syncs to RESTCONF database: ``` configure terminal logging buffered 16384 debugging logging persistent url bootflash:/logs logging persistent size 1500000 logging persistent filesize 750000 end ``` **Option 3 - Omit persistent logging attributes:** If persistent logging is not required, remove `persistent_url`, `persistent_size`, and `persistent_filesize` from automation templates. All other logging features (monitor, console, trap, history, count, rate-limit, host) work correctly without this issue. Further Problem Description: The bug is isolated to the RESTCONF operational database persistence mechanism. When a PUT request includes both `buffered-config` with `severity-level` and `persistent` attributes: 1. Device accepts HTTP request (returns 200 OK) 2. Configuration applies to running-config successfully 3. RESTCONF database sync fails for `buffered-config/.../severity-level` only 4. GET operations return partial data from RESTCONF database **Tested Configurations:** | Configuration | Result | |--------------|--------| | Base logging (monitor, buffered, console, facility, trap) | ✅ Works | | Base + history | ✅ Works | | Base + count | ✅ Works | | Base + rate-limit | ✅ Works | | Base + origin-id | ✅ Works | | Base + host | ✅ Works | | Base + persistent | ❌ Bug - severity-level missing | | Full config without persistent | ✅ Works | | Full config with persistent | ❌ Bug - severity-level missing | **Affected YANG Path:** ``` /Cisco-IOS-XE-native:native/logging/buffered-config/common-config/buffered/severity-level ``` **CLI Equivalent:** ``` logging buffered ``` **Verification Command:** ```bash # After PUT operation, check if severity persisted curl -k -u "admin:password" \ "https://device-ip/restconf/data/Cisco-IOS-XE-native:native/logging/buffered-config" \ -H "Accept: application/yang-data+json" ```

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: The Catalyst 9800 Wireless LAN Controller experiences repeated unexpected crashes of the linux_iosd-image process with segmentation faults (SIGSEGV). Last reload reason: Critical software exception, accompanied by a system report. Conditions: This issue occurs on Catalyst 9800 Wireless LAN Controllers when Cisco TrustSec is enabled with role-based enforcement, the device is integrated with Cisco Identity Services Engine (ISE), and Security Group Tags (SGTs) with Role-Based Access Control Lists (RBACs) are actively configured. This issue will be addressed via normal resolution channels. If you believe that there is new information that would cause a change in the severity of this issue, please contact psirt@cisco.com for another evaluation. Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: When no ip routing is configured on a device, the router ospfv3 command silently fails. The CLI returns to global configuration mode without entering the router ospfv3 submode and without displaying any error message. The OSPFv3 instance is not created, and no configuration appears in show running-config. This behavior is specific to the CLIv2 syntax (router ospfv3); the CLIv1 syntax (ipv6 router ospf) is not affected. Conditions: This occurs when all of the following are true: - no ip routing is explicitly configured on the device - ipv6 unicast-routing is enabled The user attempts to configure OSPFv3 using the CLIv2 syntax: router ospfv3 This is most commonly seen in IPv6-only deployments where IPv4 routing is intentionally disabled. The issue affects all IOS XE platforms and all software versions since CLIv2 router ospfv3 was introduced. Workaround: Ensure ip routing is enabled before configuring router ospfv3. Since ip routing is the default global configuration, re-enabling it with ip routing in global configuration mode will allow router ospfv3 to succeed. Further Problem Description: The router ospfv3 command required IPv4 routing to be enabled even if we want to only configure IPv6 networks. The fix allows router ospfv3 to be configured regardless of the ip routing state. The IPv4 routing check is now performed only when configuring address-family ipv4 unicast under the OSPFv3 instance, where it is actually needed.

Release Note Enclosure:
Symptom: ZTP-v4 provisioning fails on CAT9300 when using HTTP copy method with DNS lookup where the name server has both "A" and "AAAA" resource records attached to the same hostname of HTTP file server. Lab testing showed that the CAT9300 does NOT send a follow up DNS "A" query after getting a response for "AAAA" query from the name server. This contradicts RFC 4472 which states "AAAA records are typically tried first, and then A records. These are done in serial, and the A query is not performed until a response is received to the AAAA query" Down below is the behavior message flow in broken state 
           DNS Server                  CAT9300                   HTTP Server
               |                          |                           |
               |<--www.test.local AAAA?---|                           |
               |                          |                           |
               |---Global unicast IPv6 -->|                           |
               |                          |                           |
               |<-- www.test.local A?---X |                           |
The command below can be used to verify ZTP provisioning status 
Switch# show auto install status
IPv4 Status         : Failed  <<<
DHCP Server         : x.x.x.x
TFTP Server         : y.y.y.y
Network Config File :
Device Config File  : Boot file URL
Device Image File   :
IPv6 Status         : Aborted
IPv6 Device Config File :
In rare cases the ZTP-v4 provisioning may succeed, below shows the message flow in working state. 
           DNS Server                  CAT9300               HTTP Server
               |                          |                       |
               |<--www.test.local AAAA?---|                       |
               |                          |                       |
               |---Global unicast IPv6--->|                       |
               |                          |                       |
               |<---www.test.local A?-----|                       |
               |                          |                       |
               |----- IPv4 address -----> |                       |
               |                          |                       |
               |                          |---- TCP SYN, IPv4 --->|
               |                          |                       |
               |                          |<-- TCP SYN+ACK, IPv4--|
               |                          |                       |
               |                          |---- TCP ACK, IPv4 --->|
The command below can be used to verify ZTP provisioning status 
Switch# show auto install status
IPv4 Status         : Success  <<<
DHCP Server         : x.x.x.x
TFTP Server         : y.y.y.y
Network Config File :
Device Config File  : Boot file URL
Device Image File   :
IPv6 Status         : Aborted
IPv6 Device Config File :
Conditions: Two conditions must be met 1- Using HTTP copy method with DNS lookup. 2- Both "A" and "AAAA" DNS resource records are attached to the same hostname of the HTTP file server. Workaround: 1- Filtering AAAA in DNS responses by applying a filter on a name server. This filter will force the DNS server to send an "empty answer" in response to IPv6 AAAA query. 2- Using DHCPv6 instead of DHCPv4. Further Problem Description:

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: A memory leak in the PUBd process has been detected in IOS-XE devices. Conditions: The PUBd process will leak memory until it exhausts the available memory for the device. As memory is consumed, the device may display the following or similar log messages: %PLATFORM-4-ELEMENT_WARNING: R0/0: smand: RP/0: Used Memory value 89% exceeds warning level 88%. Top memory allocators are: Process: pubd_rp_0 When all the available memory is consumed, the device may reload in attempt to reset the memory. Workaround: The defect is still under investigation and no workaround has been identified so far. The best option currently is to preemptively reload the device when the high memory is detected, or to remove and re-configure NETCONF-YANG. When removing "netconf-yang", the PUBd process will also be stopped and the leaked memory should be released. When re-enabled, the memory allocated for the PUBd process will be reset and the memory leak will start back from zero. Further Problem Description: The defect is still under investigation and should be updated when more details are made available.

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: The issue is seen on C9300L platform in 17.15.3, 17.15.4d and 17.18.2. Unclear if issue is specific to this model and releases only. Enabling "debug rbm binding verbose" when removing "cts manual" from interface shows IP address of phone deleted from data vlan unexpectedly. Vlan 100 is data vlan and vlan 200 is voice vlan: cts role-based sgt-map vlan-list 100 sgt 100 cts role-based sgt-map vlan-list 200 sgt 200 cts role-based enforcement vlan-list 100,200 Interface connected to phone has "cts manual" configuration for sgt matching sgt for data vlan: interface GigabitEthernet1/0/1 switchport access vlan 100 switchport mode access switchport voice vlan 200 cts manual policy static sgt 100 no propagate sgt Phone IP shows source as LOCAL for sgt in "cts manual": Edge#show cts role-based sgt-map vrf host Active IPv4-SGT Bindings Information IP Address SGT Source ============================================ 100 LOCAL The problem happens when "cts manual" is removed from the interface: interface GigabitEthernet1/0/1 no cts manual The expectation is that phone IP reverts to sgt mapping for the vlan mapping but instead the LOCAL sgt remains stuck: // Actual Edge#show cts role-based sgt-map vrf host Active IPv4-SGT Bindings Information IP Address SGT Source ============================================ 100 LOCAL // Expectation Edge#show cts role-based sgt-map vrf host Active IPv4-SGT Bindings Information IP Address SGT Source ============================================ 200 VLAN Workaround: Remove "cts manual" from interface and reload the switch. Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: When OSPF is configured with redistribute bgp , a hidden BGP placeholder PDB is implicitly created. Removing the redistribution with no redistribute bgp does not clean up this hidden BGP placeholder. This prevents the user from configuring a new BGP instance with a different AS number, producing the error "Please do no router bgp first." Conditions: This occurs when all of the following are true: OSPF (or another routing protocol) is configured to redistribute BGP (e.g., redistribute bgp 20 under router ospf) BGP is not explicitly configured via router bgp The user removes the redistribution with no redistribute bgp The user then attempts to configure BGP with a different AS number Workaround: Explicitly remove the hidden BGP placeholder by issuing no router bgp before configuring a new BGP AS number. Further Problem Description: The fix moves hidden BGP placeholder cleanup ownership into BGP itself. BGP now registers callbacks on both IPv4 and IPv6 redistribution-change notifications and automatically removes the implicit placeholder PDB once no redistribute references remain across any address family.

Release Note Enclosure: This defect causes a loss of routing information and network reachability for leaked OSPF routes following a device reboot. It requires manual administrative intervention to restore functionality. Furthermore, the workaround results in an abnormal configuration state (duplicate commands) and does not persist through subsequent reloads, making the device unreliable in automated or high-availability environments. Symptom: - After a device reload, OSPF routes that are expected to be leaked from the GRT to a VRF are missing from the VRF routing table. Downstream OSPF peers in the VRF stop receiving the leaked routes. The route-replicate from vrf global unicast ospf command is still visible under the VRF address-family in the running configuration. Re-applying the route-replicate command restores the route leaking but generates a duplicate entry of the exact same command in the running configuration. Upon a subsequent reload, the duplicate entry disappears, and the route leaking breaks again. Conditions: - The device is configured for route-leaking from the GRT to a VRF using the route-replicate command under the VRF definition. - The routes being leaked are learned via OSPF in the GRT. - The device undergoes a reload. Note: This behavior is isolated to OSPF. Routes leaked from static entries or other routing protocols like BGP are unaffected and survive the reload successfully Workaround: To temporarily restore the route leaking, manually re-enter the route-replicate command under the VRF IPv4 address family: conf t vrf definition address-family ipv4 route-replicate from vrf global unicast ospf << << << end Applying this workaround will create a duplicate route-replicate entry in the running configuration. If the device undergoes another reload, the secondary entry will be lost, the route leaking will fail again, and the workaround must be reapplied. Further Problem Description:

Release Note Enclosure: n/a Symptom: Output from "show tcp brief" shows old connection to TACACS+ server which was previously used for Command Authorization in CLOSEWAIT state. With TACACS+ single-connection in use, this socket remains on a network device indefinitely and it tries to reuse it during the next command authorization which leads to intermittent command authorization failures until new connection is negotiated. The frequency of command authorization errors increases when multiple simultaneous connections are established to a network device. Sample output from C9200-24P, IOS XE 17.15.04: sw1#show tcp brief TCB Local Address Foreign Address (state) 3A82900C 192.168.22.180.22 192.168.22.10.30556 ESTAB 37B52848 192.168.22.180.49584 192.168.22.179.49 ESTAB 3AE90160 192.168.22.180.11072 192.168.22.179.49 CLOSEWAIT ------------ 0.0.0.0.22 *.* LISTEN ------------ ::.22 *.* LISTEN sw1#show clock % Authorization failed. Conditions: 1. TACACS+ Single Connection mode with command authorization. 2. Network device establishes two separate connections with TACACS+ server - one for Authentication/Athorization/Accounting and another for Command Authorizaiton. 3. When device admin sessions ends, network device fails to close TACACS+ socket used for Command Authorization and it remains forever in CLOSEWAIT state. 4. When new device admin session starts, network device tries to reuse old socket for Command Authorization and expectedly gets TCP RST from TACACS+ server. At this point intermittent command authorization failure can occur, especially when multiple admin sessions are established to a network device and several command authorization requests are sent simultaneously within these sessions. 5. After receiving TCP RST from TACACS+ server, network device establishes new TCP connection to use it from now on for Command Authorization and all subsequent commands are executed successfully. Workaround: #1: Disable TACACS+ Single Connection mode. Drawback: Both TACACS+ server and network device resource consumption will increase. #2: Upon receiving initial command authorization failure, repeat the same command again and it will be executed successfully. Drawback: This approach is not always possible for certain network automation scenarios. #3: Manually delete old TACACS+ socket which is stuck in CLOSEWAIT state using "clear tcp tcb " command. Drawback: This approach is not always possible for certain network automation scenarios. #4: Reload network device. Drawback: Potential loss of network connectivity (service disruption) while network device is restarting. Further Problem Description: n/a

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: "date" process is called in C9800 WLC internally to get its current clock time. It will be called and killed right after successful processing. Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: Stale ISS prefix seen in routing table, Prefix is not advertised in any LSP anymore. Originally it was advertised by BGP to ISIS redistribution on some remote router, but it is not redistributed any more. Conditions: Standard ISIS configuration, no special conditions known. It has to be noted that problem was reproduced artificially at Cisco lab with different timer configuration compared to occurrence in the field. Reproduction with field configuration was unsuccessful. Hence fix was tested against known reproduction procedure only. Fix has two parts, each able to fix the issue 1) Keep flushed LSP which used to advertise a prefix for up to 5 minutes longer in the database, which allows for standard prefix deletion. Release Note Enclosure: When copying a file from switch flash to an HTTP/HTTPS server using an FQDN within a VRF, the DNS lookup for the destination is performed in the default (global) routing table instead of the configured VRF. As a result, the name resolution fails and the copy operation does not complete. The reverse direction (copy from an HTTP/HTTPS server to switch flash) works correctly because the DNS lookup is performed in the VRF as configured by "ip domain lookup vrf source-interface ". Symptom: When attempting to copy a file from switch flash to an HTTP/HTTPS server using a Fully Qualified Domain Name (FQDN) within a specific VRF instance, the DNS lookup is performed in the default routing table rather than the configured VRF. This results in a name-resolution failure and a copy error similar to: %Error parsing filename (Invalid IP address or hostname) File transfers in the reverse direction (from an HTTP/HTTPS server to switch flash) work as expected, because the DNS lookup is correctly associated with the configured VRF. Conditions: This issue occurs when the following conditions are met: • The file transfer is initiated from the switch flash to an external HTTP/HTTPS server. • The transfer is performed within a configured VRF. • An FQDN is utilized for the destination server address. Workaround: To mitigate this issue, manually map the destination server's FQDN to its corresponding IP address in the switch configuration. This bypasses the need for external DNS resolution. Use the following command to add the host entry to the running configuration: ip host Example: ip host example.com 10.x.y.z Verification of the entry can be performed using: show hosts #show hosts | include 10.x example.com 10 IN A 10.x.y.z Further Problem Description:

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: This issue was seen in very specific corner case situation with TRM - Anycast RP configuration where EVPN fabric is used as transit between two external networks. To replicate this problem, there have to happen number of synchronized events. Example scenario would be following: Lets imagine a case where we have build shared three towards one of the Anycast RP switches and source address is known via BGP route type 5. Once receiver on E0/0 joins the tree, there is no problem and multicast traffic is flowing without any problem. Both *,G and S,G entries are present at this stage. (*, 239.5.5.5), 00:58:14/00:03:15, RP 172.16.255.255, flags: S Incoming interface: Null, RPF nbr 0.0.0.0 Outgoing interface list: Ethernet0/0, Forward/Sparse, 00:57:58/00:03:15, flags: Ethernet0/1, Forward/Sparse, 00:58:14/00:03:15, flags: (172.16.200.200, 239.5.5.5), 00:00:40/00:03:10, flags: Tq Incoming interface: Ethernet0/1, RPF nbr 192.168.57.7 Outgoing interface list: Ethernet0/0, Forward/Sparse, 00:00:40/00:03:15, flags: Now, let assume that original receiver on E0/0 is not interested to receive this multicast stream anymore and it prunes this stream. After few minutes, the S,G entry will expire from the mroute table. Normally, the *,G entry would expire as well since there are no receivers, but in this case, we have present another receiver on E0/1 which is RPF interface towards the source as well. Since this is RPF interface towards the source, it cannot be put into OIL list of S,G entry but it will be present in the OIL list of the *,G entry. This will cause that *, G will not expire from mroute table. (*, 239.5.5.5), 01:04:29/00:02:56, RP 172.16.255.255, flags: S Incoming interface: Null, RPF nbr 0.0.0.0 Outgoing interface list: Ethernet0/1, Forward/Sparse, 01:04:29/00:02:54, flags: This is corner case situation in the EVPN fabric since typically we do not have receiver on RPF interface towards the source and once S,G entry will expire, the *, G entry will expire as well. Under the conditions where S,G entry expired and *,G entry is still present, once previous receiver on E0/0 will return, there will be no S,G entry created anymore (despite BGP RT 5 present) and multicast control plane will be broken. We have to clear ip mroute for given group to recover from this state. Conditions: - TRM Anycast RP deployment where EVPN fabric is used for transit - scenario where we have receiver on RPF interface towards the source and as well other receivers - S,G have to expire while *,G entry is still present, source have to be known via BGP route type 5 Workaround: - increase S,G expire timer to decrease possibility of S,G expiry from mroute table - introduce static join to do not allow S,G to expire from network - clear ip mroute for given group once issue is replicated Further Problem Description:

The behaviour has only been seen on IE3x00 devices, and after investigation it is believed to result from the ARM64/ARMv8 core which has "weak memory ordering". This aspect of its design can result in disordered write operations, creating a small window of potential for read incoherence between threads. Due to the small size of this window it should be unlikely to encounter the behaviour, however stressing the system makes that potential more likely. Workaround: Due to the small window size for encountering this behaviour, it is less likely to be encountered when not stressing the ARP throttle table. In this case stressing the ARP throttle table means triggering ARP requests to many peers within a short amount of time, and performing this activity on a regular basis. This does not fully workaround the behaviour, however it may make it much less likely to be encountered. Further Problem Description:

Release Note Enclosure: No sensitive Info Symptom: Communications Manager does not receive SAF pattern information with correct Subscription ID from SAF forwarder running 8000V. Hence It gives the following error. 476 (Unknown Subscription/Query) Conditions: SAF envrionment running SAF Forwaders on 8000v and SAF client's on CUCM. Register first CUCM cluster. Register second CUCM cluster and despite successful registration the second CUCM cluster will not learn pattern info from the first. Workaround: Publish a new pattern on the first CUCM cluster. Configure SAF on CUCM 1 (SAF client) and register to SAF Forwarder (8000v). Configure advertised patterns on CUCM 1. 2. Configure SAF on CUCM 2 and register to SAF forwarder. Configure advertised patterns on CUCM 2 Expected Result ############### Both CUCM's register to SAF forwarder and publish their advertised patterns. At the same time they subscribe to patterns known by the SAF forwarder. The SAF forwarder sends notifies the both CUCM 1 and CUCM 2 with pattern information. Actual Result ########### CUCM 1 registers with SAF forwarder, publishes it's patterns and subscribes for one's known by SAF forwarder. (None exist yet) CUCM 2 registers with SAF forwarder, publishes it's patterns successfully which are successfully sent to CUCM 1 in a notify message When CUCm 2 subscribes for known patterns, the SAF forwarder acknowledges it providing a subscription ID The SAF forwarder attempts to send notifies about it's known patterns advertised by CUCM 1. The subscription ID on the notify is 0 (the correct one in this case is 11) so CUCm sends an error message and the notify is not consumed. Workaround ############ If a new pattern is published by CUCM 1 then all patterns are sent to CUCM 2 in notify messages with the correct subscription ID.

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: On Cisco Catalyst cEdge platforms with the login protection feature configured, the automatic application of a default access list to block management traffic during quiet-mode is observed for IPv4 but not for IPv6. The expected behavior, trigger conditions, and IPv6 support scope for this feature are not fully documented for IOS-XE 17.15.x. Conditions: Cisco Catalyst cEdge platform running IOS-XE 17.15.x. The login block-for command is configured. The device has both IPv4 and IPv6 management connectivity (dual-stack). Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: When using the RFC 5424 Syslog Header format, the switch does not send the configured FQDN in the SYSLOG message header. This occurs regardless of any configuration applied, including hostname and domain settings, with no option available to force FQDN inclusion. By default, the syslog header sends a NILVALUE ("-"). The following configuration options are available for the origin identifier in syslog messages: logging origin-id hostname - uses the origin hostname as the ID (sends Hostname) logging origin-id ip - uses the origin IP address as the ID (sends IP address) logging origin-id ipv6 - uses the origin IPv6 address as the ID logging origin-id string - defines a unique configurable text string as the ID Default (pressing ) - sends NILVALUE ("-") Currently, there is no command or configuration option to force the syslog header to include the FQDN when using RFC 5424 format; only the above origin ID options are supported. Conditions: Hardware: Catalyst 9300 Software: IOS XE 17.12.05 Syslog configuration: Using RFC 5424 syslog format Please note that this issue may also be present on other IOS XE-based platforms and versions. Workaround: Use the origin-id command with the string option and manually enter the FQDN so that it is sent within the header field of the syslog message. Further Problem Description:

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: In an OSPF NSSA topology where one or more ASBRs redistribute the same external prefixes, the count of self-originated Type-5 external LSA redistributions can become inaccurate. This may cause the count to reach the maximum prefix limit even though the actual number of redistributed external prefixes remains below that limit. Conditions: This issue is likely to be hit when following conditions are met: - OSPF is configured with an NSSA area. - The same external prefix redistributed by one or more ASBRs. - The same external prefix is present in both Type-7 and Type-5 external LSAs. - The issue is triggered by routing changes for those external prefixes, such as a route flap, or topology changes. Workaround: To prevent the generation of both Type 5 and Type 7 LSAs for the same external prefix within an NSSA area, customers can use the command area nssa no-redistribution under the router ospf configuration. Release Note Enclosure: Consulted with TL Symptom: this in an enhancement request Observed behavior: The controller continues to try to connect to the originally resolved DNS record. Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: This issue was observed for MPLS VPN deployment where RRs are running rtfilter address family towards PE routers. When PE router will withdraw certain prefix from MPLS network, RR should send BGP withdraw message to the MPLS network informing rest of PE devices that certain destination is not reachable anymore. However, with this issue, RR will not send BGP withdraw and old route will be keep present on PE routers which may lead to traffic drops or outage. BGP withdraw will not be sent in case that replication leader for certain update group did not sent rtfilter for RT attribute of affected route. Issue was observed only for routes, which had same RD value as any of the VRFs on the RR. In case that RD value do not match any existing VRF on RR, issue will not be seen. Potential workaround could be to disable rtfilter AF towards affected PE router or soft clear of BGP peering either on PE router or RR. Conditions: - RR in MPLS VPN network running rtfilter AF - route have same RD as any of the VRFs on RR - replication leader did not sent RT of affected route via rtfilter AF Workaround: - soft clear of BGP peering - disable rtfilter AF towards affected PE router Further Problem Description:

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: In SD-Access Fabric, using L2 Only VLANs or any subnet within the same Virtual Network, using the same IP addresses on endpoints in different VLANs with different source MAC address will traffic failures where ARP resolution will not occur successfully (ARP Reply will be dropped). For example (in the same Virtual Network) - Endpoint A in VLAN 111 with IP address 192.168.1.1 from MAC address aaaa.aaaa.aaaa - Endpoint B in VLAN 222 with IP address 192.168.1.1 from MAC address bbbb.bbbb.bbbb Traffic will only work to/from one endpoint at a time. Endpoint in question will be whichever was first entered in the IP Device Tracking database (which can be checked using show device-tracking database address ip_address. Conditions: This is observed in SD-Access Edge nodes running IOS XE version 17.4.x and above. Workaround: Changing the IP Device Tracking policy (or creating a new one) on the interface where the endpoint is located to "security-level glean" allows to prevent SISF from verifying the IP Device Tracking database binding which causes the ARP Replies to be dropped. It is important to note that removing switch from "security-level guard" implies the interface(s) attached to the IPDT policy will no longer be protected against any duplication / theft / spoofing (MAC or IP) detection / prevention. Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: Devices running affected IOS-XE image and using access-list (ACL) for the NETCONF-YANG, will experience Netconf sessions timeout after 255 connections to the device. Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: Issue was observed in scenario where device in question have configured BGP-LU towards external BGP peer along with VPNv4 AF. When processing transit traffic, this device have to impose both IGP and VPN label into the original packet. The IGP label is signaled via BGP-LU session and during the time of the issue, local MPLS label in CEF doesn't match the local label in MPLS forwarding table. As demonstrated via output below, CEF holds local label value of 21 and MPLS forwarding table have 20. CAT9K#sh ip cef 192.168.1.1 << remote device loopback 192.168.1.1/32 nexthop 192.168.2.2 TwentyFiveGigE1/0/2 label 20-(local:21) CAT9K#sh mpls forwarding-table Local Outgoing Prefix Bytes Label Outgoing Next Hop Label Label or Tunnel Id Switched interface 20 20 192.168.1.1/32 \ 2790 Twe1/0/2 192.168.2.2 This will cause that ASIC will perform, during packet forwarding, lookup for incorrect local MPLS label and will result in packet drop since no valid forwarding entry will be found. Trigger for the issue is flap of BGP session towards the RR. Issue was observed on C9500 platform starting from 17.6.4 image. Applicable for all IOS-XE platforms including CAT9k. Conditions: - device configured with BGP-LU+VPNv4 AF - flap of BGP session towards the RR Workaround: - clear ip route or clear ip bgp on affected device - use image version below 17.6.4 - create mpls static binding mpls static binding ipv4 (BGP peer IP) 255.255.255.255 (static label value) Further Problem Description:

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: SSH connection cannot be established with publickey algorithm ecdsa-sha2-nistp. signature(r,s) has two parts r and s. this issue occurs whenever first few characters of either r or s are NULL. because of NULL characters the length of r or s becomes less than the modulus length, which eventually crates a wrong signature(software doesn't prepend 0 to the signature). Release Note Enclosure:
Symptom: A device may reload unexpectedly after executing "show running-config" or another nonvolatile generation (NVGEN) command. The last reload reason may point to a critical software exception, and users may find a system-report or linux_iosd core file indicating a crash took place. Conditions: This behavior was observed on a device where two different users were accessing the device on separate VTY lines at the same time. Device(config)# username  privilege 15 nopassword secret 9 
ERROR: The secret you entered is not a valid encrypted secret.
To enter an UNENCRYPTED secret, do not specify type 9 encryption.
When you properly enter an UNENCRYPTED secret, it will be encrypted.
The device crashes if the user being modified is logged in during this process and subsequently runs a "show run" or another NVGEN command.

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: A Cisco IOS-XE router may experience a crash with syncfd upon enabling restconf/netconf-yang. During this time, the following log may also be observed: %PMAN-3-PROCHOLDDOWN: R0/0: root: The process syncfd has been helddown (rc 134) The terminal state would also show syncfd in a failed state: show platform software yang-management process state Confd Status: Phase1 Process Status State ------------------------------------------------------- nesd Running Active syncfd Not Running Failed <---- ncsshd Not Running Not Applicable dmiauthd Running Active nginx Running Not Applicable ndbmand Running Active pubd Running Active Subsequent restconf/netconf-yang API calls may also fail. Conditions: - Restconf/netconf-yang are in use by the router - This has been seen on routers that have ACLs with several counter hits across multiple ACEs (show ip access-list). - This syncfd crash is suspected to only be applicable to releases below 17.2. This is due to how ACL information gets retrieved in later releases. Workaround: Clear ACL counters ('clear ip access-lists counters') & restarting restconf/netconf-yang may remediate the problem state enough to bring syncfd back in service. However, as ACL counters begin to increment over time it's possible the problem maybe seen again on subsequent syncs of the datastore. Further Problem Description:

Release Note Enclosure:
Symptom: On affected versions of software, a type-7 hash key used when configuring TACACS/RADIUS displays differently in the running-config. The original key still works as expected. Conditions: service password-encryption and password encryption aes are configured. The issue appears to be specific to TACACS/RADIUS configurations as the issue doesn't exist with username/password configs. Workaround: This issue is cosmetic in nature, and it should not affect access to the device. The hash displayed in the running-config is different, but it should map to the same key. The following workarounds are available for this issue: 1) Configure both type-6 prerequisites (password encryption aes and key config-key password-encrypt) if you plan to migrate to the stronger type-6 encryption. OR 2) Remove both type-6 prerequisites if you don’t plan to migrate to type-6 encryption. This should help avoid the type-7 password re-encryption behavior noted in the "Further Problem Description" section. Only the service password-encryption config is required for type-7 encryption. The password encryption aes config is a type-6 prerequisite that is not required for type-7 encryption. Further Problem Description: This issue is cosmetic in nature. Please see the example behavior below. Configure password encryption: 
    ISR4331(config)#service password-encryption
    ISR4331(config)#password encryption aes
Use type-7 hash key: 
    ISR4331(config)#tacacs server TEST_Server
    ISR4331(config-server-tacacs)#key 7 070C285F4D06
    ISR4331(config-server-tacacs)#exit
    ISR4331(config)#radius server TEST_Radius
    ISR4331(config-radius-server)#key 7 070C285F4D06
    ISR4331(config-radius-server)#end
The hash in the running-config is different for the TACACS config: 
    ISR4331#show run | sec tacacs server TEST_Server
    tacacs server TEST_Server
     key 7 094F471A1A0A <<<------------------------------------------- Hash is different (but maps to the same password)
    ISR4331#show run | sec radius server TEST_Radius
    radius server TEST_Radius
     key 7 070C285F4D06 <<<---- Here, the RADIUS hash matches.
Trying with a more complicated hash than "cisco", we see that the RADIUS config faces the same issue. Password: qWerTyUiOp[!aSD3f5^g Hash: 12083212003F153123043413723411375410563F51 
    ISR4331(config)#radius server TEST_Radius
    ISR4331(config-radius-server)#key 7 12083212003F153123043413723411375410563F51

    ISR4331#show run | sec radius server TEST_Radius
    radius server TEST_Radius
     key 7 1314201719381D1F220B380874232023450554685E <<<------------- Hash is different (but maps to the same password)
This change in the behavior was introduced by the commits for another defect (integrated into 16.10.x and later releases). In that defect, some code changes were introduced to first check whether or not "password encryption aes" is enabled. If it is enabled, the type-7 shared secret is decrypted to plaintext, and then an attempt will be made to re-encrypt with type-6. There are two possible scenarios: Scenario 1: If the master-key is also configured (along with password encryption aes), then the decrypted plaintext key gets converted to type-6, and that type-6 hash will be displayed. Scenario 2: If only password encryption aes is configured but not the master-key, then the type-6 encryption step fails and the plaintext password gets re-encrypted with type-7 encryption. While the plaintext password of both type-7 passwords (former and latter) correspond to the same plaintext string, the type-7 encrypted strings may not be the same. This is why there is no impact on functionality with respect to RADIUS or TACACS authentication.

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: A vulnerability in the implementation of the Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) IPv4 access control list (ACL) feature of Cisco IOS Software and Cisco IOS XE Software could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to perform SNMP polling of an affected device, even if it is configured to deny SNMP traffic.  This vulnerability exists because Cisco IOS Software and Cisco IOS XE Software do not support extended IPv4 ACLs for SNMP, but they do allow administrators to configure extended named IPv4 ACLs that are attached to the SNMP server configuration without a warning message. This can result in no ACL being applied to the SNMP listening process. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by performing SNMP polling of an affected device. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to perform SNMP operations that should be denied. The attacker has no control of the SNMP ACL configuration and would still need a valid SNMP version 2c (SNMPv2c) community string or SNMP version 3 (SNMPv3) user credentials. SNMP with IPv6 ACL configurations is not affected. For more information, see the Details section of the advisory. Cisco has released software updates that address this vulnerability. There are workarounds that address this vulnerability. This advisory is available at the following link: https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-snmp-uwBXfqww Conditions: Please refer to the Security Advisory. Workaround: Please refer to the Security Advisory. Further Problem Description: Please refer to the Security Advisory. Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: - Devices may initiate DNS queries to the public resolver 8.8.8.8 even when no DNS server is explicitly configured on the device. - External DNS traffic to 8.8.8.8 may be observed in flow records, firewall logs, or packet captures. - Name resolution behavior may appear inconsistent if access to public DNS is restricted by policy. Conditions: - Alpine-based app-hosting container images will send DNS requests to all configured DNS servers in parallel. - Because 127.0.0.11 is populated in the resolv.conf file in the container, the Docker nameservers are also used. Workaround: 1) Monitor and control egress DNS traffic to 8.8.8.8 according to your security policy. 2) Configure explicit, approved DNS servers if required by your environment. 3) Review features or workflows that may trigger DNS lookups and adjust policy as appropriate. Further Problem Description: The defect causes unintended DNS reach-outs to 8.8.8.8, which can create audit or compliance concerns and may impact name resolution if public DNS is blocked.

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: We have observed this issue on ASR1004, RP2 running IOS-XE 17.6.5 and ASR1002-HX running IOS-XE 17.6.4. A permit ACE added in the ACL doesn't match any traffic. Therefore the desired traffic is dropped. Conditions: While making an ACL, issue is triggered when a remark statement is added to the ACL with a sequence number which does not match the very next ACE in the ACL and the ACL is re-sequenced. Workaround: Make sure that any remark statement which is added to the ACL has a sequence number which matches the very next ACE. If we ensure all remark statements have a corresponding ACE with same sequence number, then this issue will not happen post ACL resequencing. Further Problem Description: The issue is observed when a remark statement is added in the ACL with a unique sequence number and the ACL is re-sequenced. If the sequence number on the remark statement doesn't match the sequence number of the very next ACE, in this case if the ACL is re-sequenced, and then a new ACE is added we see a mis-match between the ACE entries in the CGM and TCAM. As part of the fix, during ACL resequencing, if we find any dangling remarks (remarks without any corresponding ACE with same sequence number), then those will be deleted and a syslog will be generated. Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: A vulnerability in the implementation of the Simple Network Management Protocol Version 3 (SNMPv3) feature of Cisco IOS Software and Cisco IOS XE Software could allow an authenticated, remote attacker to poll an affected device using SNMP, even if the device is configured to deny SNMP traffic from an unauthorized source or the SNMPv3 username is removed from the configuration. This vulnerability exists because of the way that the SNMPv3 configuration is stored in the Cisco IOS Software and Cisco IOS XE Software startup configuration. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by polling an affected device from a source address that should have been denied. To exploit this vulnerability, the attacker must have valid SNMPv3 user credentials. For more information, see the Details section of this advisory. Cisco has not released software updates that address this vulnerability. However, there is a new method for configuring SNMPv3 so that it will not be affected by this vulnerability. There are workarounds that address this vulnerability. Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: In a CTS deployment with FlexConnect Local Switching, the WLC receives Role Based ACLs from ISE, to push to the APs. If the ISE pushes multiple RB ACLs for a specific rule, the WLC sends them out of order resulting in traffic beeing blocked. Example in Allow List model, we need to specifically allow traffic before the default Deny_all RB ACL. On ISE we define a RB ACL to allow DNS and DHCP and the default rule will have the custom DHCP_DNS _Permit and the default DENY_ALL. Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: A device experiences an unexpected reload after removing an encryption key from a TCP key chain being used for BGP peer sessions. A system report and crashinfo file will be generated. The crashinfo will indicate a segmentation fault, and the process is BGP I/O. Exception to IOS Thread: Frame pointer 0x7CE6B7AF7650, PC = 0x58ECAC31C9D4 UNIX-EXT-SIGNAL: Segmentation fault(11), Process = BGP I/O Conditions: BGP with TCP AO is configured for authenticating BGP sessions. Removing the encrypted key-string while it is still in use can cause the crash. During CLI configuration a warning is given stating the key-string is in use. The crash has been seen when using methods that forcefully remove the configuration, such as "config replace [file] force". An example configuration would include the following: key chain BGP-KEYS tcp key 1 send-id 1 recv-id 1 include-tcp-options cryptographic-algorithm aes-128-cmac key-string 7 [encrypted key] template peer-session BGP-SESSION ao BGP-KEYS include-tcp-options exit-peer-session address-family ipv4 neighbor [IP] inherit peer-session BGP-SESSION exit-address-family Workaround: The crash happens when BGP is using the encryption key and it is removed. Preventing BGP from using the encryption key in it's peer sessions before removing the encryption key will prevent the crash. One way to do this is to remove the peer-session configuration using the key chain from BGP before removing the encryption key. Once you are done making changes to the key chain you can reapply the peer-session configuration under BGP. Further Problem Description:

Release Note Enclosure: A static route is being installed after the renewal process. Symptom: - Our customer is attempting to configure a static IP towards the ISP as follows: "ip route 8.8.8.8 255.255.255.255 gig0/0/0 dhcp". - Interface Gig0/0/0 connects to the ISP, and he receives the IP address via DHCP. - The issue is that the static route is removed following the DHCP renewal process. - We discovered that this is an expected behavior based on the following RFC, as the ISP sends "Option 121 & 3", and once the client receives both, it ignores "Option 3", resulting in the removal of the static route from our side. https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3442 " If the DHCP server returns both a Classless Static Routes option and a Router option, the DHCP client MUST ignore the Router option." - As option 3 is being ignored during the renewal process, if we configure a static route again after the renewal, the static will be installed in the routing table. Conditions: IP address with classless route + static route config with dhcp Workaround: don't remove and apply "ip route 8.8.8.8 255.255.255.255 gig0/0/0 dhcp" after DHCP aqiring the IP address Further Problem Description: If classless route option in place & dhcp client acquired the IP address. If you remove and add state route <> <> dhcp, static route has been set. As per the RFC if device with classless route, that should not configure static route

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: A secondary policy-map is not applied in interface configuration. Conditions: Applying two policy-maps in interface configuration via a EEM script where the trigger is a regex and no 'maxrun' is configured Workaround: N/A Further Problem Description: Applying a second policy-map in interface configuration via an EEM script when 'maxrun' is not configured and if the trigger is a regex. It does not matter if the first is applied 'in' or 'out'; the secondary policy is never applied. The test policy-maps in use are: policy-map 100M class class-default police cir 115000000 pir 115000000 exceed-action drop policy-map test class class-default police cir 1000000 exceed-action drop The test EEM script: event manager applet test_conf event cli pattern "^port_conf.*" enter action 010.010 cli command "enable" action 020.010 cli command "conf t" action 030.010 cli command "int tw1/0/33" action 070.010 cli command "service-policy input test" action 080.010 cli command "service-policy output 100M" action 150.010 cli command "end" The issue is not related to the invalid command 'port_conf' because if we use a valid command like 'systat' as trigger within a regex, the second policy-map is still not applied. If the EEM script is manually triggered (with 'event none' configured), both policies are applied into the interface configuration.

Release Note Enclosure:
Symptom: Catalyst 9000 switch crashes due to a segmentation fault in the session manager (sessmgrd) process: 
Critical process sessmgrd fault on rp_0_0 (rc=139)
Users should look for a "system-report.tar.gz" file in the affected switch's file system and provide it to Cisco TAC for decoding and confirmation of this issue. Conditions: The crash occurs in code tied to the Enforcement Policy Module (epm). The crash is seen with Cisco TrustSec (CTS) applied with dot1x/mab configurations on particular interfaces. The crash occurs when an avpair from ISE profiling gets incorrectly interpreted as a Security Group Tag (SGT). Because the avpair is a string instead of a valid SGT integer, the switch ultimately crashes due to a segmentation fault. Workaround: Remove the dot1x/mab configurations from the problematic interfaces. If a user is unsure of which specific interface's configs are problematic, it is safest to remove dot1x/mab entirely. Users could also remove the problematic ISE profile which contains an invalid SGT value. Further Problem Description:

Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: A crash was seen in the CTS Core process: UNIX-EXT-SIGNAL: Segmentation fault(11), Process = CTS CORE -Traceback= Conditions: CTS is being used on the device. Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: Older config files (archived prior to reload) are NOT getting purged. Conditions: Problem is triggered when the router is reloaded. Workaround: Where possible, until this is fixed, kindly consider manually purging/deleting the previous config archive files. Alternatively do not use this feature until this is fixed Further Problem Description: ! archive log config logging enable logging size 768 notify syslog contenttype plaintext hidekeys path flash:running-config.bak maximum 14 write-memory ! The sub-cmd maximum controls the number of config revisions to be stored in flash:. Release Note Enclosure: Symptom: + if upon the reception of a BGP open message, the BGP passive peer replies with a BGP notification "no supported AFI/SAFI)", the the BGP active peer does not resend open messages, resulting in a stuck bgp neighborship: CE# show ip bgp vpnv4 vrf C96 neighbors BGP neighbor is 10.10.10.101, vrf C96, remote AS 64496, external link BGP version 4, remote router ID 0.0.0.0 BGP state = Idle, down for 02:36:20 <<< Last reset 02:36:28, due to BGP Notification received, no supported AFI/SAFI <<< Conditions: + The LNS is configured as a passive peer: router bgp <> ! address-family ipv4 vrf osp-231721 neighbor <> transport connection-mode passive + There is a considerable number of BGP sessions established between the LNS and the CEs (254 sessions is known to cause this issue) + Those BGP sessions flap. That flap on the sessions must be distributed on a short period of time. Meaning that we cannot just shut all the BGP sessions and unshut them at the same instant. Each BGP session must be unshut at a slightly different instant (for instance if we only have one CE with many bgp sessions to the LNS, a clear ppp will allow thie behavior to manifest). Workaround: + Configure multi-session OR + clear the bgp session on the CE Further Problem Description: There is large number of BGP neighbors configured on the PE node of the order of 2000. When interface between PE and CE is flapped, the eBGP session goes down and never recovers. BGP session on PE is passive and single session. Root Cause: BGP session on PE while processing OPEN message doesn't find an active topology to establish session. The reason being TCP connection from previous session is not closed yet and BGP could not find an active topology to associate with the session. PE side declines with notification ?no supported AFI/SAFI? with afii safi values filled. The receiving speaker upon receiving this notification will never attempt to connect again. %BGP-3-NOTIFICATION: sent to neighbor 172.16.16.132 passive 2/8 (no supported AFI/SAFI) 3 bytes 000101 Had the notification was sent with out afi safi values filled in, peer would retry after connect retry timer expiry. The proper solution would be to not support this notification for single session neighbor. This DDTS, we are disabling the support for this notification with afi/safi values filled in the data part and later cleanup would stop supporting it in entirety.
